**Updated by:** Builder — **the identity ruling implemented (Chris, 2026-08-05): FieldScout stores no name for a person**, branch `fix/identity-username-only-v2`. Not a milestone task — a whole-app ruling that lands across the league surface, so it is recorded here. Chris, verbatim: *"we don't need either a display name or a full name. we just need the email, password and unique username."* `handle_new_user` seeded `profiles.display_name` from the OAuth `full_name` claim, so a Google sign-in wrote a REAL NAME into a row that the `profiles` policy "Profiles are viewable by everyone" USING (true) exposes to **anon** — and every identity surface rendered `display_name ?? @username` (Chris saw his own name across the app). **Migration 075** does two things and no more: `handle_new_user`'s profile INSERT becomes `(id, username, avatar_url)` — no name written, the OAuth claim ignored — and `UPDATE profiles SET display_name = NULL` clears the names already stored. **No schema change**: the column is NULLABLE with no default, so once nothing writes it it sits inert, and the migration and the app deploy are order-independent against the live site (this is what sank the earlier PR #96, which renamed the column to `full_name` and called it private — the world-readable policy made that untrue, and neither merge order was safe). The migration body is production's LIVE `handle_new_user` (`pg_get_functiondef`, 2026-08-05) minus the name write — it deliberately does NOT import the 049/050/051 username-contract guards, which were never applied to production and which 073 reverted locally too; restoring them is a real but SEPARATE bug, flagged not smuggled (see D115(3)). The five other functions that read the column (`notify_list_followers`, `create_league`, `seat_league_member_internal`, `get_join_preview`, `draft_actor_name`) are deliberately NOT replaced: each reads through a `COALESCE` onto `username`, so with the column permanently NULL they already resolve to the handle — zero churn, and three of them do not exist in production at all. `ai_personas.display_name` is untouched (PUBLIC parody brand copy carrying the "(AI)" transparency marker — no human behind it, nothing to leak; PR #96's `persona_name` rename is dropped). Spec **v2.9** folds the ruling into §7.2's identity table + render rule, §7.2.1's retained-history line, §12.23's claim-preview comment and §16.4's growth-loop rule. Account settings loses its name field entirely: email, password, avatar and a read-only permanent handle. New vitest `src/lib/identity-render.test.ts` (10): source-level sweep of every surface (the `launch-scope-gates` precedent) — no code reads or writes a name on a profile, no PostgREST select pulls one out of `profiles`, settings offers no name field, no seed/dev script plants one, and 075 makes no `ALTER TABLE`/`RENAME`/`DROP COLUMN` at all. pgTAP 005's R31 slot now asserts the trigger writes **no** name (the strongest form of that guard). **Search narrowed to handle-only matching** — there is nothing else left to match on. D115. ### MP task checklist *(breakdown authored 2026-08-21 and **rewritten the same day to Chris's second ruling** — **awaiting his approval of breakdown PR (this one)**; `MP.*` is takeable only after it merges, and only once ACTIVE-BUILD carries the lane clause — **F102**)*

*(**Why this lane exists — TWO premises were wrong, and the second is the bigger one.** **(1)** §8.8 said since v2.3 that a mock is a rehearsal of one specific league (*"v1 scope: league-attached only"*). Chris: *"a user may run a mock draft without even being 'in a league'."* **Practice is the purpose; a league is optional context.** The failure that told on it was `create_mock_draft`'s seat gate (`092:1233–1241`) refusing his own practice — *"it says i need 11 more people"* — **working exactly as designed and answering the wrong question.** **(2)** This document's first cut then answered the corrected premise by designing a hidden per-user "practice container" — a `leagues` row nobody sees — so a league-less mock could satisfy league-shaped RLS, league-shaped FKs and §8.8 isolation. Chris: *"i didn't think mock drafts were going to add so much complexity … I doubt they are doing any of this inivisible league blah blah blah security container stuff."* **He is right and the reason generalises: mocks were built INSIDE the leagues system and inherited its whole threat model — RLS by membership, isolation, commissioner authority, audit immutability — all of which exists because a real draft has twelve humans with money at stake. A MOCK HAS ONE HUMAN AND ELEVEN BOTS: no adversary, nothing to protect.** The complexity was **inherited, not required**. **The new shape: a mock is STANDALONE, settings from the six base scoring templates plus the spec's own defaults, which the launcher changes at launch.** **D228 (the container) is WITHDRAWN and kept in the record as withdrawn**, with its figures corrected — it priced the alternative at *"50 in-body `is_league_member` sites across 18 files"*; measured against the deployed schema it is **13 calls across 9 live functions, 11 sites across 8 on a mock's path** — roughly 4× too high. **League-attached mocks are DEFERRED, not cancelled** (Chris rates the feature highly), and §6.1 of the breakdown protects them. Spec **v2.16** is the fold.)*

**Sequencing:** MP is a **peer of `AP.*`, `MS.*`, `DR2.*` and `SE.*` and blocks none of them.** **`MP.1` is an investigation and nothing skips it — it decides the storage shape every server task is built on.** `MP.5` may start immediately and in parallel. **TWO hard ordering constraints. (1) `MP.2` before `MP.3` — RULED 2026-08-24 by D234(8), a hard prerequisite and not a preference:** under D234's chosen shape a NULL `league_id` makes `draft_mock_cpu_need`'s `JOIN public.leagues` match nothing and every bot's need term collapse, and no storage decision can defend against it. **(2) THE `MP.6` CHAIN, SPLIT IN THREE 2026-08-24 (D243, answering Q25) AND ORDERED `MP.6` → `MP.6b` → `MP.6c` — route, then write path, then spine.** The order is a rule: **MP.6c's acceptance is a browser drive** (bots acting, pause/resume, the chat posts rendering) and **none of it can run until MP.6b's verbs work league-free**; built the other way it would claim its states from intent (§4 rule 9). **`MP.7`'s leagues-off pin needs `MP.6c`, not `MP.6`** — MP.6 gives the room a URL, MP.7(4) asserts the room LOADS (**R470** / D231(3a)). **`MP.8` is takeable now but SEQUENCED AFTER the 6-chain** (D243(6)): a standalone mock cannot COMPLETE until the room works, and a report verified only against league-attached mocks is the half the lane exists to escape. **`MP.9` has no such dependency.** `MP.10` after the surfaces exist; `MP.11` last. **One cross-lane seam: `MP.4` and `MS.8` both touch the launch form AND the launch RPC — neither forks; whichever lands second composes.** **Recommendation recorded for Chris (not applied — F102):** the **mock track runs AHEAD of the league lanes**, since it is what users are invited to during the 2026 launch while league work waits for demand.

**Release gate:** its **own** flag — `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLAG_MOCK_DRAFTS` / `featureFlags.mockDrafts`, **never `featureFlags.leagues`**. **A RELEASE statement, not code isolation:** the shared draft engine stays shared (and is what makes the standalone mock affordable — 58 live functions / 6,252 lines that name their tables literally). **Independence is a claim about ROUTES as well as components** — `(room)/leagues/layout.tsx:18` redirects every `/app/leagues` URL when the leagues flag is off, mock room included (**R470**). **Launch-facing:** Chris intends to invite users to it, so states and polish are in scope (**§4 rule 14**).

Task breakdown, §1 surveyed facts (opened on `main` @ `1d4620d` or measured against the **deployed** schema — the stack was up, so the engine facts are `pg_proc` reads), §2 the two corrections, §3 the rulings verbatim, design decisions (**D225–D233**, entering §4 verbatim at merge), standing rules (tasks-M3 §4 rules 1–8 + tasks-DR §4 rule 9 verbatim + seven lane rules), §6.1 **the deferred feature and how to protect it**, §7 the MS relationship task-by-task, §8 **Q23 lapses / F85 de-targeted**, §11 **Q24**: `docs/specs/tasks-MP-mock-practice.md`.

## 3. Spec questions

*Anything where the spec is ambiguous, silent, or seems wrong. Write it here and STOP rather than improvising — per CLAUDE.md. Move to "Resolved" once Chris answers; the answer should also get folded back into the spec itself as a changelog entry.*

### Open

**STANDING RULE — THE COMMISSIONER CAN DO ANYTHING. RULED BY CHRIS 2026-08-09 (Q50(e)), RESTATED 2026-09-09 TWICE, AND RESTATED AGAIN THE SAME DAY BECAUSE THIS FILE KEPT ASKING. This entry exists so nobody asks a fourth time.**

*"League manager needs to be able to basically do anything. It seems like I keep repeating myself."* — Chris, 2026-09-09, after the third separate verb-level refusal was brought to him as a finding. Earlier the same day: *"yes a commissioner (league manager) can basically manually edit anything. this is the fallback that allows the league to ultimately get through any exception case."*

- **(a) THE RULE.** A commissioner may perform **any** action any manager can perform, **on any team**, at any time the league is in a state where the action is meaningful. There is no per-verb ruling to seek. **A verb that refuses a commissioner is a DEFECT, not a design** — file it and fix it; do not open a §3 question about it. *(**CARVE-OUT — TRADES, ruled by Chris 2026-09-30, in chat:** *"A commissioner cannot do anything to a trade unless it's already been accepted and the only option is veto or instantly push it through."* / *"Remove reverse."* A commissioner does NOT propose, accept, turn down, counter or call off a trade for a team he does not manage — those refusals (migration 174) are the RULE, not defects; on an accepted trade his only tools are veto and push it through (approve / force); a completed trade stands. As a team's own manager he trades like anyone. D463.)*
- **(b) THE ONE CONDITION, and it is Chris's own.** *"no receipt if nothing is done. only when something is done."* A commissioner action that CHANGES something writes a receipt — an audited row with a reason (§15.4's header: *"all require `reason`; all write `commissioner_actions`"*). A no-op writes nothing. That is the whole price of the power.
- **(c) THE RULE IS NOT NEW AND NEVER WAS — §15.4 ALREADY GRANTS IT, and this is the answer to "I don't know where that came from".** `spec:1689-1699` enumerates **ten** commissioner override verbs, including verbatim: `commish_move_player(player_id, from, to, reason)` and `commish_force_add_drop(...)`. So the commissioner's roster power was never withheld by anyone's decision — it is spec LAW that was **scheduled for M6 and never built**, while the MANAGER's verb shipped in M4. `roster_add_drop`'s manager-only check (`115:415-426`) is not a policy against the commissioner; it is the manager's verb declining to be the commissioner's door, and its own comment says so: *"his roster move is M6's `commissioner_move`"*. The observable effect on a live league is nevertheless identical to a prohibition, which is why Chris experienced it as one and why the sequencing was wrong.
- **(d) SO M6A's SCOPE IS §15.4 IN FULL, not a hand-picked subset.** Superseding the "four asks" framing of Q51(e) and the narrower slice scoped on 2026-09-09: **IN** — `commish_edit_score`, `commish_set_result`, `commish_move_player`, `commish_force_add_drop`, `commish_edit_lineup` (see (e)), ~~`commish_edit_record`~~ *(struck 2026-09-27 — **Q60 RULED NO by Chris**: there is no record-editing verb; a commissioner changes a record only by correcting the game — edit score / set result — which already flows to standings; spec v2.16.42)*, `commish_change_setting`, plus **`commish_rename_team`**, which §15.4 does NOT list and which no verb anywhere provides (Q53(e)(i)) — under this rule its absence is a defect. **DEFERRED FOR WANT OF A SUBJECT, not for want of authority** — `commish_force_or_reverse_trade` and `commish_edit_faab`: there are no trades and no FAAB ledger until M5, so these land WITH M5 rather than before it. **ALREADY BUILT, needs auditing only** — the §11.7 manual matchup edit (`111`'s `schedule_edit_matchup`, reachable at `POST /api/leagues/[id]/schedule/matchup`) covers `commish_edit_schedule`; check its receipt against (b).
- **(e) ONE PLACE THE POWER IS ALREADY THERE AND THE RECEIPT IS NOT — a §12.12 hole, found 2026-09-09.** `set_lineup` **already accepts a commissioner acting for another team** (`114:243-247`, `NOT (v_is_manager OR v_is_commish)`) and the team page already wires it (`team-page.tsx:132` `canEdit = isOwnTeam || isCommish`, `:239` `isCommissionerArm`). So a commissioner can edit any team's lineup TODAY. What it records is a two-valued flag — `edited_by_commish = NOT v_is_manager` (`112:1103`, mirrored into the result at `112:1193`) — and **no reason and no audit row**, because `commissioner_actions` does not exist. Under (b) that is backwards: the one commissioner power that shipped is the one with no receipt. `commish_edit_lineup` is therefore not a new capability but the audited upgrade of an existing one.
- **(h) OVERRIDE IS A MODE, NOT A PER-SAVE DECISION. RULED BY CHRIS 2026-09-11, after using the shipped flow on four teams.**
  - *"what I would prefer is the commissioner going into 'override mode' which lets them act like any GM in the league, and then when they're done they exit override mode. when override mode is active there is some visual indications that it's on."* And on the reason: *"instead of doing it on a per transaction basis which gets messy."*
  - ~~**THE REASON IS CAPTURED ONCE, when the mode is switched ON, and carried by every action taken in that session.**~~ **SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY, by Chris, before it was built:** *"yeah i think no reason at all is fine"* … *"if anyone cares they can ask"*. **So the commissioner is NEVER PROMPTED FOR A REASON — not per save, and not on entering the mode.** Entering the mode is one action; saving is one action; there is no text field anywhere in the path.
    - **What the receipt still is.** §(b) is untouched: a change writes an audited row, a no-op writes nothing. `commissioner_actions` still records the actor, the instant, the before/after `slot_map` and the week — which is the whole of what makes a post-kickoff edit legible to the league. The *explanation* lives in the league's conversation, where it always actually lived; a form field only ever produced *"fix again"*.
    - **What the client sends instead, and why it is not a lie.** `commish_edit_lineup` RAISEs on a blank `p_reason` (`123:665-669`) and so does `set_lineup`'s commissioner arm (`114:316-321`), and §15.4 says every commissioner action carries one — changing that is a migration plus a spec edit and buys nothing visible. So the CLIENT supplies a fixed **label**: `COMMISSIONER_OVERRIDE_REASON = 'commissioner override'` for the audited verb and `COMMISSIONER_ARM_REASON = 'commissioner action'` for the manager verb's commissioner arm (`src/components/leagues/lineup-editor-ops.ts`, both named constants with the ruling cited at the definition). They name the MECHANISM and nothing else — deliberately not prose that pretends to be a justification, because a fabricated *"manager unreachable"* in an audit row is worse than a label that says only what happened. **No migration, no RPC change, no API contract change.**
    - **CLARIFIED 2026-09-16 (L.E1.15 / F362 / F343; Q66, spec v2.16.41; migration 131):** ~~the label is needed so `123:295-296`'s CHECK still receives a non-blank string~~ — **the label was a workaround for 123:295's NOT NULL, which 130 §0 removed; since 131 every commissioner verb (123's, 126-129's, 111's two, and `set_lineup`'s commissioner arm) NORMALISES a blank reason to NULL instead of refusing it, so the client MAY SEND NOTHING.** The two constants remain legal (a non-blank label is still stored trimmed and posted) and nothing in this clause obliges the UI to keep sending them; L.E1.12 / L.E1.13 decide, and their docblocks in `lineup-editor-ops.ts` describe the pre-131 state until then (F363).
  - **WHAT SHIPPED WAS WRONG AND WHY — recorded because the failure was in the INTERACTION, not the verb.** The L.E1.1 build made the override an offer that appears *after* a refusal: Save → refused → "Override as commissioner" → (a Reason field appears) → "Save override". Measured against Chris's live league on 2026-09-11: Team 8 succeeded (refusal `15:07:13`, override `15:07:43`, reason *"fix again"*) because he happened to type a reason; **Teams 5 and 6 produced a `set_lineup` refusal and NO override call at all** (`15:10:47` Stevenson, `15:12:01` Shaheed; zero `commissioner_actions` rows). His words: *"i hit save, then it made me hit this override as commissioner button"* and *"i just set the lineup for team 6, hit refresh and it's unset again"*.
  - **The defect:** clicking "Override as commissioner" READS as a confirmation ("yes, do it") and is actually a mode switch that then silently waits for two more actions. The save button stays disabled until the reason has text and says nothing about what it wants. A disabled control with no stated precondition is the same class as an empty result read as success — the screen reports nothing and the user infers completion.
  - **Scope: UI only.** `commish_edit_lineup` already takes `p_reason` per call, so a session-level label is the client sending the same string each time. No migration, no RPC change, no audit-shape change.
  - **AS BUILT (2026-09-11).** The mode is a **persistent, unconditional switch** for a commissioner in every week state — never behind a refusal, never behind `editability.state === 'closed'` — and it **stays on across saves and across team pages** until he exits it (`src/stores/commish-override-store.ts`, keyed by league, in memory only; he fixed four teams in one sitting and a per-page flag would have made him re-enter it on each route). While it is on: the whole editor is framed in the lime "look here" tokens, a `✸ Override mode ON` badge sits in the team card **above the week picker** so it is legible on a phone with nothing scrolled, and the locked rows go live through the shipped `lockExempt` machinery (unchanged — R973's five prop hops, one memo and two `frozen` expressions all still counted). **Exiting never discards the draft** — the placements stay exactly as arranged and the consequence is said out loud (`overrideExitCopy`), because silently eating his work is the bug class this exists to end. The refusal-driven offer is **kept, as a shortcut INTO the same mode**: the ruling makes the switch the way in, but a refusal that dead-ends with no route out would be worse than what shipped. Pins: `team-page.render.test.ts` (the switch on an open live week, absent for a manager, no `<input` anywhere in the path, the visible state on/off, the closed week opening, the "why is Save disabled" line), `lineup-editor-ops.test.ts` (`lineupSaveRequest` — same request twice, both labels non-blank after the server's own `btrim`), `commish-override-store.test.ts` (keyed by league).

- **(i) THE BOUNDARY, AND IT IS THE TEST TO APPLY TO EVERY FUTURE VERB. RULED BY CHRIS 2026-09-11, explaining Q59:** *"it's not fixing something that's broken, it's changing the game entirely."*
  - **Commissioner powers exist to FIX WHAT IS BROKEN. They do not exist to CHANGE WHAT THE GAME IS.** That single sentence is the boundary on (a)'s *"can do anything"*, and it is the question to ask of any verb before building it: **is this repairing something that went wrong INSIDE the rules, or is it redefining the rules?**
  - **Repairs — all IN, no ruling needed:** editing a lineup after kickoff (a manager could not be reached), moving a player between rosters (a draft-day mistake), editing a score or declaring a winner (a cancelled game), renaming a team, forcing an add or drop. Every one of these restores a state the rules already contemplate. The lock, the week gate and the roster gate are all TIMING and REACHABILITY constraints — they say *when* and *by whom*, and a commissioner exists precisely to stand outside them.
  - **Redefinitions — OUT, whatever the authority:** a wide receiver in the quarterback slot. Nothing went wrong that this repairs; it makes the lineup something the game does not have. **No authority makes a malformed lineup well-formed**, which is why Q59 is NOT an exception to (a) but a demonstration of where (a) was never pointed.
  - **Why this needed saying:** I read (a) as a permission rule that therefore bypassed validation, and twice pressed Chris to lift E16 on that reading. He refused, and the refusal is not a carve-out — it is the correct reading of (a) all along. A permission rule answers *who may act and when*; it never answers *what counts as a valid move*. **Apply (i) BEFORE opening a §3 question about a commissioner refusal**: if the refusal protects the shape of the game rather than its timing or its actors, it is not a defect and there is nothing to ask.

- **(g) NAMED APPLICATION — THE GAME-DAY LOCK DOES NOT BIND THE COMMISSIONER. RULED BY CHRIS 2026-09-09:** *"an LM should be able to set the lineup even after the games have started. it's the entire point of having LM powers."* Recorded separately from (a) because a reader could argue the lock is not an authorization refusal and therefore not covered — it is covered, and this clause removes the argument.
  - **AS-BUILT:** `v_is_commish` appears in `set_lineup_internal` exactly ONCE, at the auth gate (`114:244-245`). The two lock arms — `114:449-462` (a stored starter whose game kicked off may not leave his slot) and `114:464-476` (a player whose game kicked off may not enter or move slots) — carry **no commissioner exemption**, so today a commissioner can open any team's lineup and is then refused on exactly the players an exception would be about. Same for `roster_add_drop`'s E32 drop lock (`115`).
  - **THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED ONCE AND NOT AS AN OBJECTION.** Editing a lineup after kickoff means editing it with the points already known. That is not a side effect to be designed away — it is the *purpose*: the cases Chris keeps naming (a manager who never showed, a postponed game, a league deciding its own version of fair) are all discovered after play starts. The integrity answer is Chris's own §(b): **the receipt**, not the refusal. An audited row naming the actor, the instant, the before/after `slot_map` and the reason is what makes a post-kickoff edit legible to the league; a hard refusal just moves the argument off-platform.
  - **SO `commish_edit_lineup` (§15.4:1695) IS NOT THE SAME VERB AS `set_lineup` WITH A COMMISH ARM.** It is the lock-exempt, reason-required, audited one. `set_lineup`'s existing commissioner arm stays as it is for the ordinary pre-kickoff case (and still owes its receipt — see (e)); the new verb is what an exception goes through. **This makes L.E1's lineup task materially bigger than "add an audit row" and it must be re-scoped in the M6A breakdown before a builder takes it.**
  - **DO NOT WEAKEN THE LOCK ITSELF.** §7.3.4/§11.2 lock semantics are on CLAUDE.md's never-weaken list and they still bind every manager. The exemption is a property of the commissioner verb, never a relaxation of the rule the manager verb enforces — the same shape as every other §15.4 override.

- **(f) WHAT THIS RULE RETIRES.** Q51's "four asks" enumeration is superseded as a SCOPE statement (its sequencing argument stands). Any future finding of the form "verb X refuses a commissioner" is an F-number and a fix, never a Q-number. The STOP rule in CLAUDE.md still governs everything else — this rule removes exactly one class of question from it, the class Chris has now answered three times.


**Q70–Q79 — FILED 2026-09-27 BY THE M5 ARCHITECT (`tasks-M5-transactions.md` §11, breakdown PR open for approval). Each names the M5 tasks it blocks; every task not named can start without an answer. All ⬜ OPEN.** *(Q70 is F229's waiver-scheduling investigation; Q73 is F239; Q78 is F333's lock half; Q79 is F211's swap / auto-sub arms.)*

**✅ Q70–Q79 ALL RULED by Chris 2026-09-27 — *"approve M5, all recommendations"*: every question below is decided exactly as its RECOMMENDATION reads; the breakdown (`tasks-M5-transactions.md`, PR #323) is APPROVED. Builders treat each recommendation as the ruling; no task is blocked on Q70–Q79 any more.**

**Q70 — HOW DO WAIVERS RUN IN YOUR LEAGUES? (F229) — blocks L.D2.4's schedule part, L.D2.7, L.D2.9, L.D2.13's schedule copy.**
- You described two leagues: (1) waivers every day at 9:00 AM Pacific until Sunday 6:00 AM, then instant-pickup free agency until Monday night's last game ends; (2) waivers once, Tuesday at midnight, then instant pickup for the rest of the week. Today's settings can express neither.
- **Proposed model:** a league picks **(a) when waivers run** (one or more days, one local time, in the league's own time zone) and **(b) when free agency is open** (instant pickup for any unowned player whose game hasn't started — e.g. "Sunday 6:00 AM until the week's last game ends", or "from the waiver run until the week's last game ends"). Outside free agency every unowned player is claim-only until the next run. Your two leagues become presets, plus "no waivers, always free agency".
- **Three details, each with a recommendation:** a player dropped Friday in league 2 is **on waivers until the next run** (the spec's default — a dropped player goes on waivers); right after the draft, undrafted players are **on waivers until the first run**; when the week ends, unowned players go **back to claim-only until the next run**.
- ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4). F229 discharged.

**Q71 — CAN A TEAM WIN MORE THAN ONE PLAYER IN ONE WAIVER RUN, AND DOES "BIGGEST BID WINS" BEAT A MANAGER'S OWN RANKING? — blocks L.D2.8, L.D2.9.**
- Example: Team A bids $5 on Player X (its only claim). Team B ranks #1 Player Y ($3), #2 Player X ($50). **(1)** The highest bid on a player always wins him — B gets X for $50; a team's ranking only settles its own collisions (two claims dropping the same player, or not enough budget for both). **(2)** Strict ranking — B's #2 isn't looked at until B's #1 is settled, which can hand X to A for $5.
- **Recommendation: (1)**, and a team can win several players in one run as long as each claim is still valid when its turn comes. ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4). (In the spec since v2.16.57 — C77, L.D2.8; not re-folded — folded in v2.16.57 (C77); v2.16.58 only aligns §14's row (R1185). F422 (a)/(b)/(c) stay OPEN.)

**Q72 — BEFORE THERE ARE STANDINGS, WHO GETS FIRST WAIVER PRIORITY? — blocks L.D2.8, L.D2.9.**
- Example: week 1's run, two teams bid the same $12 on the same player (or the league uses rolling priority).
- **Recommendation:** reverse draft order until the first week is final, then reverse standings or the rolling order as the league chose; rolling priority starts from reverse draft order and a team moves to the back only when it wins a claim. ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4).

**Q73 — A WAIVER CLAIM THAT DROPS A PLAYER WHO ALREADY PLAYED THIS WEEK: GO THROUGH OR FAIL? (F239) — blocks L.D2.8, L.D2.9.**
- Example: claim "add A, drop B" set Wednesday; B plays Thursday night; claims run Friday. The `bench_lock` setting (on by default): on = the claim fails, no FAAB spent, the manager is told why; off = it goes through and B's Thursday points still count. You ruled a player who has kicked off can't be dropped until the week's last game ends.
- **Recommendation: remove the setting — the claim always fails, the same rule as a manual drop.** ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4).

**Q74 — CLAIMS ON A PLAYER WHOSE GAME HAS ALREADY STARTED — blocks L.D2.8, L.D2.9.**
- Example (league 1, daily 9 AM runs): Player C played Thursday night, so he can't change teams until Monday night's last game ends.
- **Recommendation:** the app won't accept a new claim on C until then (same message as the pickup lock), and a claim already pending on C at Friday's run **fails** with the reason and no FAAB spent, rather than silently waiting for a later run. ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4).

**Q75 — AN ACCEPTED TRADE WHERE ONE PLAYER ALREADY PLAYED THIS WEEK — blocks L.D3.3.**
- Example: Sunday morning a 2-for-2 trade is accepted; one player played Thursday night, the other three haven't played. The league setting (`trade_lock_behavior`, default "defer") waits and runs the whole trade automatically after Monday night's game; "reject" fails it. The spec's wording is "while the game is live"; your add/drop rule is "until the week's last game ends".
- **Recommendation:** keep "defer" as the default; the wait is until the week's last game ends, all players move together, and while it waits the players stay with (and can be started by) their current teams. ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4).

**Q76 — WHAT EXACTLY DOES "TRADE DEADLINE: WEEK 11" MEAN? — blocks L.D3.3.**
- **Recommendation:** trades can be proposed and accepted until week 12 begins (Wednesday 00:00 ET); a trade accepted before the deadline still completes even if its review or game-lock wait ends after it; offers still pending at the deadline expire with a note to both managers. (The commissioner can still move players afterwards with his own tools.) ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4).

**Q77 — LEAGUE-VOTE TRADES: WHO VOTES, AND WHEN DOES THE TRADE GO THROUGH? — blocks L.D3.4 and L.D3.7's vote UI.**
- **Recommendation:** every manager except the two teams in the trade may vote to veto; vetoed as soon as veto votes reach the league's number (default half the league, rounded up); otherwise it goes through when the review period ends (default 24 h); votes can change until then; the league sees the count, not who voted. ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4).

**Q78 — IF A MONDAY GAME IS POSTPONED PAST TUESDAY NIGHT, DO PLAYERS UNLOCK AT WEDNESDAY 00:00 PACIFIC ANYWAY? (F333) — blocks L.D2.10.**
- Q50 ruled the week closes by Wednesday 00:00 Pacific even if a game hasn't been played. **Recommendation:** at that moment every locked player unlocks and waivers run on schedule; the unplayed game's points stay pending until it is played or the commissioner steps in (operator tools, M8 — not M5). ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4).

**Q79 — AUTO-SUB AND HOT SWAP SPOTS: WANTED FOR THE TEST COHORT THIS SEASON? (F211) — blocks nothing in M5.**
- **Auto-sub** (league setting, off by default): a starter ruled out before his game is swapped for a bench player at his position. **Hot Swap spots** (default 0): a manager names a backup for one starter ahead of time. Neither is part of waivers or trades.
- **Recommendation:** leave both out of M5; if you want them this season they become a small slice after M5 (its one open question is Q36). ✅ RULED 2026-09-27 as recommended — Chris: *"approve M5, all recommendations"*. Folded into the spec v2.16.58 (L.D2.4).

**Q80 — RULED by Chris 2026-09-28: "Yes" — the second league's "Tuesday at midnight" waiver preset is 12:00 AM Wednesday, Pacific** (L.D2.7's reading, confirmed). A preset — commissioners can change it.

**Q81 — A stat fix comes in after a week is final. Should the commissioner get a one-tap way to apply it? (C81; F381's stat-correction sentence)** — ✅ **RULED NO, 2026-09-29.** Chris: *"Q81: Is this what other platforms do?"* (the orchestrator's summary given him, not verified research: the standard platforms don't apply a correction after their deadline — spec §23.4's list: Sleeper through Thursday, Yahoo until the next week's first game), then *"Q81 should not be a commish decision. if the stat window has closed I think we have to forget it because if our platform is scoring differently from the others that could be a problem."* **The rule:** after the window a late stat fix never changes league scores; there is no commissioner apply door (none of options (a)–(c)); the player's real stats (research) still update; the league corrections view lists only corrections that changed a league score. **Consequences:** L.E2.2 / L.E2.4 drop every "would-be" number and the commissioner door (breakdown APPROVED note); the other task sentences that assumed a listed `week_final` row are F510. That leaves `players.adp` (`002:15`), a DRAFT-DAY signal doing an in-season job, already the tiebreak-of-last-resort at the draft autopick's never-stall floor (`095:3484-3491`).
- **RECOMMENDATION: ship `adp ASC NULLS LAST, player_id ASC` as the DEFAULT, with the sort isolated as ONE clause** (the *build for flexibility* preference — a weekly-projection input is later a one-line swap, not a redesign), and say plainly in the PR that this is a placeholder signal. The *AI rankings: fun, not perfect* preference applies: an autopilot lineup should feel reasonable, not be a source of truth.
- **Per the standing rule this is NOT a verb-refusal question and must not block the build.** **~~⬜ OPEN~~ — silence ships the recommendation. [AND THE SILENCE HAS NOW SHIPPED IT, 2026-09-12 (L.E1.4, migration 125 — R1001): the recommendation is live code, `ORDER BY p.adp ASC NULLS LAST, r.player_id ASC` at `125` (grep `ORDER BY p.adp ASC NULLS LAST` — line numbers in 125 moved in the same PR's fix round; R1003), verbatim. Answering this question DIFFERENTLY IS NOW A MIGRATION, not a choice — one clause, by design, but a migration. The question stays OPEN because Chris has not ruled; what changed is the cost of a different answer.]**
- **✅ THE RULING (Chris, 2026-09-27, in chat): autopilot starts the eligible player with the highest projected points.** Selection order: **(1)** THIS WEEK's projected points, scored through the league's own scoring settings; **(2)** fallback — **positional rank = season-to-date fantasy points scored**, ranked within the position, under the league's scoring — *"positional rank comes from how many points that player has scored thus far into the season"* (e.g. the RB ranked 10th starts over the RB ranked 25th); **(3)** Week 1 / no games yet — **preseason positional rank**; **(4)** last resort — ADP, then `player_id` (determinism). Weekly projections do not exist in the schema today: they come from **Sleeper**, the source `scripts/sync-projections.ts` / `src/lib/sync/projections.ts` already uses for preseason — a new weekly sync + storage is required (plain fetch, no scraping service — project rule). **Also RULED: `Doubtful` sits** — it joins autopilot's blocking designations (today 125 blocks OUT, IR, PUP, NFI, Suspended, and bye; kicked-off players are locked); **Questionable remains eligible.** **What followed:** spec v2.16.42 (§7.2.1(c)); tasks **L.E1.19** (weekly projections sync), **L.E1.20** (the league-scored values — scoring lives only in TypeScript, so the canonical scorer computes and persists and autopilot's one SQL sort reads; D371), **L.E1.21** (the order + `Doubtful`). ~~Readings those tasks carry as RECOMMENDED and flagged for their reviewers: the rank pool, the preseason rank's source, and `Doubtful` as a preference rather than a hard filter~~ **✅ THE THREE FOLLOW-UPS RULED by Chris 2026-09-27 (second answer, in chat):** **(i) Doubtful with no healthy replacement — *"yes start the doubtful."*** A Doubtful starter is swapped out only when a healthy, unlocked, eligible replacement exists; otherwise he starts, and a slot is never left empty on his account (a Doubtful start is legal for a manager too, `114:596`, so he is a preference, never the `allow_illegal_lineups = FALSE` hard filter). **(ii) Across positions (a FLEX slot) the fallback compares *"total scored points"*** — season-to-date fantasy points under the league's scoring, not rank against rank; within a position the order is the same either way. So the sort key is the POINTS, and **the population question is moot** — a player's own points do not depend on whom he is ranked among. **(iii) ~~The preseason fallback likewise compares the league-scored season projection value across positions~~ [Relabelled by the PR #312 review, R1093: Chris ruled only that Week 1 falls back to the preseason rank, and that ranking is by points — he did NOT name the preseason source.]** The source — the league-scored `players.projected_stats` season line, compared across positions by that value — is **this docs session's READING, flagged for L.E1.20's reviewer**. **Ledger: F379.**

**Q63 — DOES AUTOPILOT SUBSTITUTE A STARTER A HUMAN ONCE CHOSE? GENUINELY UNDECIDED; blocks only L.E1.4's SUBSTITUTION arm, not its FILL arm. — ✅ RULED by Chris 2026-09-27: the shipped narrow rule STANDS — AND, WIDER: autopilot is OFF BY DEFAULT, behind a per-team commissioner switch. Spec erratum v2.16.42 (§7.2.1(c), §10.1, §23 `lineup-lock`). Built by L.E1.22 (F380).**

- A seat can be unmanaged **today** while carrying last week's lineup from a manager who left mid-season (`120:645-659` keeps the roster; `116:456` carries the map). Filling an **EMPTY** slot is unambiguously right. Replacing a departed manager's **healthy, unlocked** starter with a higher-ranked bench player is a different act.
- **RECOMMENDATION: substitute ONLY when the seated starter carries a blocking designation or is on bye AND a healthy, unlocked, eligible replacement exists; never on value alone.** That is the narrow reading, it matches `spec:733`'s trigger word-for-word (*"officially OUT/inactive"*), and it keeps autopilot from silently out-managing the ghost of a real person. **~~⬜ OPEN~~ — silence ships the recommendation. [AND THE SILENCE HAS NOW SHIPPED IT, 2026-09-12 (L.E1.4, migration 125 — R1001): the recommendation is live code — the two-pass fit at `125` (grep the two-pass fit banner — R1003) / `:509-531`, where a seated bye/OUT man is vacated ONLY if a healthy, unlocked, eligible replacement actually takes his key and is otherwise RESTORED where he sat (D356(2)). Answering this question differently is now a MIGRATION, not a choice. Still OPEN because Chris has not ruled.]**
- **✅ THE RULING (Chris, 2026-09-27, in chat):** autopilot **keeps a set lineup and substitutes ONLY players who can't play** — the shipped option: a blocking designation (now including `Doubtful`, Q62) or a bye, with a healthy, unlocked, eligible replacement. **AND, WIDER: autopilot is OFF by default.** *"the default would be the commissioner has to manage the team, but give the [commissioner] a button that lets them put the team on autopilot."* So a vacated (orphaned) or never-filled seat is **not** auto-managed; the commissioner (and co-commissioners) manage it via the existing act-as / override tools, and get a per-team **"Put on autopilot"** switch (on/off, audited like every commissioner action, reason optional, shown in League Home activity). If neither happens, the team plays the lineup it has; empty/unplayable slots score zero — *"that is fine."* **No additional reminders** for this case: *"if there is a reminder for any manager who has a player in their lineup that is out or on a bye that's fine, but we don't need any additional reminders for this exception case."* **What followed:** spec v2.16.42 amends §7.2.1(c) (*"(autopilot). Lineups auto-set …"* struck with correction), §10.1's *Membership* row and §23's `lineup-lock` row (*"UNCONDITIONAL"* struck with correction). **§7.2's *"empty seats auto-set to autopick"* (the draft-short capacity override) is DRAFT-time autopick and is NOT changed by this ruling**, nor is any other draft autopick text. Task **L.E1.22** builds the flag (default OFF — existing seats included, so production's unmanaged seats stop being auto-filled until the switch is flipped), the verb, arm (c)'s gate, the route/hook/UI — **and re-cuts L.E1.14's synthetic gate**, whose invariant 8 premise counts unmanaged seats and must now count seats with the switch ON, with the sim flipping the switch through the real verb and keeping ≥ 1 OFF seat as a negative control. **Ledger: F380.**
- **✅ BUILT 2026-09-27 by L.E1.22 (migration 139, pgTAP 087; D376; spec v2.16.47).** The switch is `team_autopilot` (no row = OFF); `commish_set_autopilot` / `POST …/commish/autopilot` / the team page's switch inside override mode; arm (c) fills only a switched-ON seat and names every OFF one. **Pushing 139 turns autopilot OFF for every existing team in production** (the ruled default, no backfill) — Chris's live league stops being auto-filled until he flips each unmanaged seat's switch. **Q68 is untouched** (still OPEN — the Doubtful-replacement behaviour is 138's, unchanged).

**Q67 — AN EMPTY LINEUP BEFORE ANY GAME: MAY THE COMMISSIONER EDIT THAT MATCHUP'S SCORE? FILED 2026-09-27 BY THE L.E1.18 RE-REVIEW (R1100). DOES NOT BLOCK L.E1.18's MERGE (135 strictly narrows production's behaviour); BLOCKS ITS FOLLOW-UP F384.**  - **What is built (135 after its fix round).** A side with NO `team_lineups` row is not finished (`lineup_not_set`, refused outside a final week). A side whose row exists but holds no starter with a game reads `no_starter_game` (editable). When a week opens, the carry (118:1813-1825) writes an EMPTY row for every team that never set a lineup — so in a live week, a matchup where neither side has a starter yet is editable before any game is played, and the override freezes it; a manager may then fill the lineup with a not-yet-played starter, and the frozen override still stands (measured by the re-reviewer, rolled back). Where it bites: week 1 before managers set lineups, and teams nobody manages (autopilot OFF by default, Q63).
- **The question, in product terms.** If neither team has anyone in its lineup yet, can the commissioner edit that matchup's score? And if a manager later puts a player who hasn't played yet into the lineup, should an override made before that stand?
- ~~⬜ OPEN~~ **✅ RULED by Chris 2026-09-27 — option (1), locked:** *"you cannot edit a score for a matchup that has not finished yet."* A matchup is editable only once it is actually over: every starter on both teams has finished his game, **or** the week's games are all done (a FINAL week stays always editable). **A team with no starters picked therefore holds its matchup locked until the week is done** — an existing lineup row with no starter no longer reads `no_starter_game` ⇒ editable outside a final week. Built by **L.E1.25** (discharges F384). **[✅ BUILT 2026-09-27 — L.E1.25, migration 142 (pgTAP 083 re-cut + 090; D379); F384 DISCHARGED.** Per side, as the task text reads: outside a FINAL league week a side whose row holds no starter WITH A GAME (the carry's empty row, or bye / no-team starters only) is not finished — refused, the team named. ~~**One reading flagged for Chris, not decided (D379(4)):** "the week is done" is built as the league week being FINAL, so in the correction window (every NFL game over, the league week not yet closed) such a side still holds the matchup locked; if Chris means "every NFL game of the week is final", it is a one-predicate change.~~ **[RE-CUT by PR #321's fix round — R1140, resolved by the orchestrator from Chris's plain rule and STATED TO HIM 2026-09-27, open for him to correct (D379(11)): a matchup has finished when EITHER (A) every NFL game of the league week is over (every row `final` or moved out of the week) OR (B) every STARTING slot on BOTH sides holds a player whose game is final. An empty slot, a bye starter, or a side with no lineup / no starter holds it open under (B); (A) releases it once the week's games are all over — so the correction window is EDITABLE; a FINAL week always is. This also supersedes Q61's gloss that a bye starter and an empty slot "do not hold the matchup open".]**]**

**Q68 — AN OUT (OR BYE) STARTER WHOSE ONLY REPLACEMENT IS DOUBTFUL: SHOULD AUTOPILOT PUT THE DOUBTFUL PLAYER IN? FILED 2026-09-27 BY L.E1.21 (migration 138). DOES NOT BLOCK — BUILT AS THE RULINGS' TEXT READS; a different answer is a one-hunk migration.**
- **What is built (138).** Q63 is ruled: autopilot substitutes a starter who cannot play *"only when a healthy, unlocked, eligible replacement exists"* (spec §7.2.1(c)). Q62 is ruled: `Doubtful` *sits* — it joined the blocking designations. Read together, a Doubtful bench player is not a healthy replacement, so an **OUT (or bye) starter whose only eligible, unlocked bench option is Doubtful now STAYS in the lineup** and scores zero. pgTAP 086 **D7 / D7b** pin it by name; the tick's report names the OUT man in `restored[]`, so it is visible, not silent.
- **What changed.** Before 138 a Doubtful player counted as healthy, so that OUT starter WAS swapped for him. (For an EMPTY slot nothing changed in that direction: a Doubtful candidate is still seated ahead of an OUT / bye one — D375(4).)
- **The question, in product terms.** *A team on autopilot has a starter who is ruled OUT. The only player on the bench who could replace him is listed as Doubtful. Should autopilot put the Doubtful player in?*
- **Two more facts (R1123, PR #316's review, measured).** **(a) The outcome depends only on whether the OUT man is ALREADY SEATED.** 086 **D7** (OUT man seated at flex, Doubtful on the bench ⇒ the OUT man STAYS) and **D8** (the same two kinds of player, flex EMPTY ⇒ the Doubtful man STARTS, ahead of the OUT man) give opposite answers for the same pair. **(b) In a league with `allow_illegal_lineups = FALSE`, autopilot now keeps a starter it ITSELF flags `out`** while a legal Doubtful replacement sits on the bench — X10's fixture with the league flipped to FALSE, same instant: 138 ⇒ `flex:0` = the OUT man, flags `["out"]`, named in `restored[]`, the Doubtful man benched; **production's 125 chooser, same fixture ⇒ swaps him out for the Doubtful man (`substituted`, reason `designated OUT`, flags `[]`)**. So in such a league this is a regression from what production does today: the league forbids illegal lineups, and autopilot leaves one it could have fixed.
- **Options.** **(1) No** — as built: only a healthy player replaces a starter (the rulings' text). **(2) Yes** — when no healthy replacement exists, a Doubtful one replaces a starter who is OUT / on bye (never one Doubtful player for another, and never on value alone). **Recommendation: (2)** — an OUT player is a certain zero and a Doubtful one sometimes plays, and it matches *"yes start the doubtful"* when nothing healthy exists; it is one hunk in pass 1 (offer the Doubtful tail to a vacated BLOCKED key before restoring him).
- ~~⬜ OPEN~~ **✅ RULED by Chris 2026-09-27 — option (2):** *"Q68 yes, swap in the doubtful."* When no healthy, unlocked, eligible replacement exists, a Doubtful one replaces a starter who is OUT / on bye (never one Doubtful player for another). Restores production's (125) behaviour in `allow_illegal_lineups = FALSE` leagues and makes D7 agree with D8. Built by **L.E1.25**; should land before the 135–138 push reaches production. **[✅ BUILT 2026-09-27 — L.E1.25, migration 142 (pgTAP 086 re-cut + 090; D379).** 086 D7 now swaps and agrees with D8; the `allow_illegal_lineups = FALSE` case (R1123(b)) is 086 D7c / D7d — swapped, flags clear.**]**

**Q69 — A SCORING CHANGE WITH RE-SCORE ON: IS LAST WEEK, STILL SHOWN AS "FINAL (PENDING CORRECTIONS)", RE-SCORED? FILED 2026-09-27 BY THE L.E1.24 REVIEW (R1134, PR #320). BLOCKED #320's merge until ruled. — ✅ RULED by Chris 2026-09-27: (b) — last week keeps its scores.**
- **What is built (141, L.E1.24).** "Open" = 131's `v_open_weeks` = `live` + `correction_window` (`141:323`, `:420`), so with `rescore = true` a week in its stat-correction window IS re-queued and re-scored under the new rules (089 §E pins it; probe P4 reds it). Only `final` weeks are kept.
- **Why it is a question (the reviewer's evidence).** The app shows a `correction_window` week to members as finished: `schedule-view-ops.ts:163-164` labels it *Final (pending corrections)*; `matchup-view-ops.ts:64`'s hover reads *"Every game is over…"*; spec §7.3.6 — *"Matchups show `final (pending corrections)` until it closes."* Chris's chosen words for Q64 were *"Finished weeks keep their original scores and results."* The builder's case (§10.1 v2.16.42's *"open and future weeks"*) rests on the orchestrator's transcription, not Chris's wording, and the spec never defines "open". The task text said to ESCALATE if the reviewer read "finished weeks" as including `correction_window`.
- **The question, in plain fantasy terms (R1134's wording).** *"A commissioner switches the league to PPR on Tuesday. Last week's games are all over, and the matchup page shows last week as 'Final (pending corrections)' until Thursday, while stat corrections can still change it. With 're-score' turned on, which should happen? (a) Last week is re-scored under PPR, which can change who won it. (b) Last week keeps its scores like the weeks before it, and PPR starts with the coming week."*
- **Two facts put with it.** (a) is what 141 does. (b) is NOT a one-line change (R1136): the score worker refuses only `final` and `upcoming` weeks (`score-week-worker.ts:924-932`) and re-scores a `correction_window` week on every stat correction through the league's CURRENT snapshot (`:936-938`), so flipping 141's predicate alone would leave the week scored under two rule sets — keeping it honestly needs F397's per-week rules first.
- ~~⬜ OPEN~~ **✅ RULED by Chris 2026-09-27 — option (b):** *"Q69 keep last week's scores."* A scoring change with re-score ON does **not** re-score a week in its stat-correction window (*Final (pending corrections)*); it keeps its scores like the final weeks, and the new rules start with the coming week. **141 as merged re-scores a `correction_window` week — that behaviour is INTERIM and CONTRADICTS this ruling; L.E1.27 changes it (F404)**, on top of F397's per-week rules (RULED the same day: *"F397 yes build it"*). Until L.E1.27 merges, 141 is not to be pushed to production (ACTIVE-BUILD).
- **The `live` (current) week — read from the two rulings, not re-asked.** Q64's chosen words *"The new rule applies to this week and later"* cover the week in `live` status, whether or not its games have started; Q69 moved only the correction-window week. `league_weeks` goes `upcoming → live` at `nfl_weeks.starts_at` — Wednesday 00:00 ET (`118:1787-1799`; `112:135`) — so in Q69's Tuesday scenario "the coming week" is still `upcoming` and takes the new rules when it opens, and from Wednesday it is the `live` week, which a rescore reaches. L.E1.27 builds that reading; a builder or reviewer who reads *"the new rules start with the coming week"* as excluding a `live` week whose games are under way STOPS and files it in plain terms rather than guessing.
- **✅ BUILT 2026-09-27 — L.E1.27 (migration 144; D382):** a correction-window week is kept and named beside the final ones; the live week is re-scored (read as above — not re-asked); each week keeps being scored under its own stored rules (F397).

**Q66 — MUST A COMMISSIONER GIVE A REASON TO EDIT THE SCHEDULE *BEFORE* WEEK 1 KICKOFF? SPEC §11.7:770 / E41 SAY NO (A REASON-FREE WINDOW); MIGRATION 130's ONE RECEIPT HUNK MAKES `schedule_edit_matchup` REQUIRE ONE ALWAYS. BLOCKS L.E1.9's MERGE (PR #300) — REVIEWER R1046, VERDICT ESCALATE. — ✅ RULED by Chris 2026-09-16, WIDER THAN EITHER OPTION: a reason is OPTIONAL on EVERY commissioner action; the audit row is ALWAYS written; every action is SHOWN in League Home's activity section. Spec erratum v2.16.41 (§10 / §11.7 / §15.4 / E41). Built for 130's two verbs in L.E1.9's fix round (same PR); the six earlier verbs are the sweep, F362, filed not built.**

- **What the spec says.** `spec-redraft-leagues.md:770` (§11.7): *"Allowed freely until the **first NFL kickoff of league Week 1**. After that, Remix and any matchup edit become commissioner **overrides** (reason + audit entry per §10)."* `:2016` (E41): reason required only *"after Week 1 kickoff"*. PROGRESS **F40** (`:2733`): *"REQUIRED once league Week 1's first kickoff has passed — E41/D290; optional before."*
- **What 130 does.** The task's one receipt hunk (`130:1105-1121`) makes `schedule_edit_matchup` write a `commissioner_actions` row on EVERY edit, and that row's `reason` is `NOT NULL` (`123:295-296`) — so **a commissioner editing the schedule in August is refused without a reason** (078 D1; `schedule-edit-api-db.test.ts`'s "AHEAD (2099)" cell now expects 400). pgTAP 059 H1–H4 and the `…36` side flip were amended to pass a reason where they passed `NULL`; F361 was filed for the panel's now-stale hint.
- **Why the Builder's cited authorities do not carry it.** (a) F225's amendment (`PROGRESS:2890`) says the gate *"moves to the explicit `E' \t\r\n'` class with the 500 bound"* — a character-class change, nothing about conditionality. (b) `spec:1690`'s heading (*"all require reason; all write commissioner_actions"*) governs **§15.4's verbs** — the new sibling `commish_edit_schedule` — not §11.7's `schedule_edit_matchup`, whose route is `POST …/schedule/matchup`. D348 itself says of 111's verb *"changing it is a user-visible change."* **D361(6) records the Builder weighing alternatives and choosing — which is the improvisation CLAUDE.md forbids** (*"If the spec seems wrong or ambiguous: STOP, write the question"*). Recorded here as the Q that should have been filed before the code.
- **Chris rules one of:**
  - **(A) Accept as built and erratum the spec** — §11.7:770, E41 and F40 become *"a reason is required always; the free window only drops the override tail and the chat marker."* One rule instead of two; every other commissioner override already requires a reason; the user-visible cost is one panel hint (F361, L.E1.13). Fix round: spec erratum (v2.16.41, the L.E1.2/Q65 precedent), D361(6) retracted into this Q, R1047's bracket-row confirm folded in.
  - **(B) Keep the free window** — gate the receipt hunk on `NOT v_free`: a pre-kickoff edit is *"allowed freely"* — no `commissioner_actions` row, no reason — exactly as the spec prints it. Fix round: the hunk gains the guard (still one hunk), 059 H1–H4/`…36` and the API-test amendments revert, F361 withdrawn, a cell pinning that a free-window edit writes NO receipt.
- **Reviewer's recommendation: (A)** — recorded as the reviewer's, not a ruling.
- **R1047 folds into the same ruling as a one-line confirm:** `111:881` (a bracket row) was among the four refusals the task text names to lift and was **KEPT** instead (F360). The technical reasoning holds — `111:1075-1091`'s every-team-once re-validation counts every non-retired team per `(week, round_type)` and a `playoff` row seats a subset, so lifting it refuses one gate later with the wrong message, and `118:1573-1594` re-seeds bracket rows at each sync — but a narrowing of a lifted refusal is not the Builder's call under rule (i) without a nod. **Confirm: bracket rows stay unlifted, F360 open, no verb today — OK?** (If yes, the banner/F360 cite is corrected from `118:1075-1077` to `118:1573-1594`.)
- **Not merged until ruled.** Two nits ride the fix round either way (R1048: the chat post carries the plain-`btrim` reason while the receipt stores the explicit-class trim — cosmetic, one-hunk discipline forbids touching the post; R1049: no action). ~~**⬜ OPEN — filed 2026-09-15 at L.E1.9's review.**~~
- **✅ THE RULING (Chris, 2026-09-16, verbatim, after two rounds of clarification in plain user terms):** *"No we should not require a reason for anything, I thought we talked about this already. I think it's fine to have one but it's not required. What is required is storing the transaction and displaying it in the 'activity' section of the League Home."* Confirmed: **optional for all of them** — fix lineup, correct score, move player, rename team, change setting, edit schedule. Neither (A) nor (B): the reason-free window is not a window, it is the whole rule; the receipt is what §10 requires. **R1047's confirm, same session: bracket rows stay unlifted in 130 — but hand-picking playoff matchups is a WANTED commissioner feature and its OWN task** (F360 re-scoped from "a gap" to a planned verb; the banner/F360 cite corrected `118:1075-1077` → `118:1573-1594`).

Migration 130 **§0**: `commissioner_actions.reason` DROP NOT NULL, CHECK re-minted as `reason IS NULL OR <123's explicit class + 500 bound>` — 123 is in production and untouched; **the first writer under Q66 lands the column change once, for the sweep to build on.** `commish_edit_schedule`: no reason gate in any window; blank / whitespace-only ⇒ NULL stored (never ''), non-empty stored trimmed, 500 bound kept, the post's `— reason:` clause conditional, `reason_required` FALSE at both levels (E41 no longer requires one either; the field stays for the panel, F361). `schedule_edit_matchup`'s hunk: still EXACTLY ONE (re-derived: one `@@`, zero `-` lines) — no refusal for a missing reason, stores `NULLIF(btrim(v_reason, E' \t\r\n'), '')`, leaves `reason_required` as 111 computes it. pgTAP 078 `plan(129)` (§D/§H re-cut to LAND without a reason with NULL-reason receipts; new §M pins the column change with the CHECK as a stored literal), 059 §H1–H4 / `…36` pass NULL again, 071 A3 flips to `col_is_null`, the stack vitest's free-window edits pass no reason and assert `reason: null` receipts. **D361(6) RETRACTED** (struck in place, the F342 way). Typegen `reason: string → string | null` (3 lines), alias block byte-identical.
- **THE ONE THING THE FIX ROUND DID NOT DO, SAID OUT LOUD:** 111's OWN post-kickoff gate in `schedule_edit_matchup` (`111:952-957`) and its post text (`111:1123`) are ORIGINAL lines outside 130's one hunk; removing them is a second and third hunk in a body D137 / F341 / the task text say carries exactly one. **Q65 — MAY A COMMISSIONER CHANGE `team_count` IN-SEASON? SPEC §7.3:197 SAYS YES; MIGRATION 129's POLICY TABLE REFUSES IT IN EVERY STATUS, AND THE REFUSAL'S OWN REMEDY IS A DEAD END. BLOCKS L.E1.8's MERGE (PR #299) — REVIEWER R1039, VERDICT ESCALATE. — ✅ RULED by Chris 2026-09-15: option (b). Spec erratum v2.16.40 (§7.3:197 — `team_count` is PRE-DRAFT ONLY); 129's `refused_why` corrected; 077 E2 re-pinned. Built in L.E1.8's fix round, same PR.**

- **What the spec says** (`spec-redraft-leagues.md:197`, §7.3): *"After the draft, structural settings (roster slots, **team count**, scoring categories) become commissioner-override-only (changing them mid-season is allowed but logged and warned)."*
- **What 129 does** (`129:330-334`): `commish_setting_policy('team_count')` → REFUSED by name in every status. Its `refused_why` says *"post-draft a franchise is added with `add_placeholder_seat`"* — but `063:445-446` raises *"this league already has all % seats — raise `team_count` first"* at the ceiling, and post-draft nothing can raise it (`118:2489-2497`'s gate, which 129 lifts for other keys, plus 129's own refusal). `grep "team_count =" supabase/migrations/*.sql` → only `update_league_settings` writes it. **So a commissioner seating a 9th franchise in-season has no route, and the message points him at one that refuses.**
- **How the Builder got there:** the task text (`tasks-M6A:519`) says season-window keys *"move the window under rows that already exist — the table says what each does"*, read as "refuse". Defensible for `regular_season_weeks` / `playoff_start_week` (Q10 coupling; 111's generated schedule rows). `team_count` is the one key the SPEC itself lists as allowed.
- **Why it is a Q and not a fix:** standing rule (i) says a reachability refusal is a defect to fix — but the fix direction depends on which text is right, and the spec and the table say opposite things. CLAUDE.md: if the spec seems wrong or ambiguous, STOP and file it. Chris rules one of:
  - **(a) `team_count` becomes changeable in-season, with its consequence stated in the receipt** — raise-only (`>= seated`, even, `≤ 16`), the document naming *"no schedule row exists for the new seat until a remix"*. The verb then has a real post-draft route and `add_placeholder_seat`'s message becomes true.
  - **(b) Spec §7.3:197 gets an erratum narrowing "team count" to pre-draft** (the L.E1.2 errata precedent), and 129's `refused_why` stops citing `add_placeholder_seat` as a post-draft route — it names the true state: there is none.
- **Reviewer's recommendation: (b)** — its stated reason: an in-season team add with no schedule rows changes the game rather than fixes it. **Recorded as the reviewer's recommendation, not a ruling.** The same ruling can cover `regular_season_weeks` / `playoff_start_week` explicitly so the table is not re-litigated at L.E1.13.
- ~~**Not merged until ruled.**~~ **RULED 2026-09-15 — Chris picked (b), adopting the reviewer's reason (an in-season team add with no schedule rows changes the game rather than fixes it).** Either answer was a fix round on PR #299; (b)'s shape shipped: **spec v2.16.40** strikes *"team count"* from §7.3:197's mid-season list with the correction beside it; 129's `refused_why` for `team_count` no longer cites `add_placeholder_seat` as a post-draft route and states the true state (pre-draft only by spec; NO post-draft route); pgTAP 077 **E2** pins the corrected message with a pattern shown RED on the wording it replaced. The round also carried the review's three nits (R1040 `roster_settings` canonicaliser rebuilt from the known keys — TAKEN; R1041 045's "67-table" → "71-table" — TAKEN; R1042 "the file is retired" → "no entry is added", in 129's banner and ACTIVE-BUILD — TAKEN). **Scope of the ruling: `team_count` ONLY.** `regular_season_weeks` / `playoff_start_week` stay refused on the task text's reading (`tasks-M6A:519`), not on Q65 — L.E1.13 must not cite v2.16.40 for them. ~~⬜ OPEN — filed 2026-09-15 at L.E1.8's review.~~ **✅ RULED (b) 2026-09-15.**

**Q64 — DOES `rescore: true` REQUIRE `reopen_week` TO BE BUILT FIRST? BLOCKS L.E1.8's `rescore` ARM ONLY. — ✅ RULED by Chris 2026-09-27: option 1, going forward only — the open week and later weeks are re-scored, final weeks are not. ~~The shipped refusal is permanent~~ The shipped whole-call refusal CONTRADICTS the ruling (F382 → L.E1.24, R1090); `reopen_week` is not wanted. Spec erratum v2.16.42 (§10.1 / §15.4). F359 closed as not wanted.**

- `score_write_week_batch` skips `status='final'` rows and the total-points arm guards `is_final = FALSE`, so on a final week `rescore` is **a no-op today**. `reopen_week` is in §12.12's own action vocabulary and `league_weeks.reopened_by_action_id` has had its FK since `123:463-464` with **zero writers**.
- **RECOMMENDATION: ship `rescore` REFUSING a final week BY NAME in L.E1.8, and build `reopen_week` as its own task if you want the capability.** Silently accepting a flag that does nothing on exactly the weeks a commissioner would use it for is the one option §4 rule 15 forbids. ~~**⬜ OPEN.**~~
- **SHIPPED ITS RECOMMENDATION 2026-09-15 (L.E1.8, migration 129), the Q62/Q63 precedent — the row stays Chris's and stays OPEN.** `commish_change_setting` refuses `rescore = true` BY NAME whenever the season has ≥ 1 FINAL week (P0001 listing the weeks; the whole call rolls back; the message names both routes — resubmit with `rescore = false`, or wait for `reopen_week`), and performs the rescore on every OPEN week when there is no final week. `reopen_week` was NOT built and the reserved seam (132 / 080) was released unspent. **The refusal is ONE marked block** — `129` step (11b), `-- Q64 SEAM`, pinned by pgTAP 077 G14 — and the banner says exactly what replaces it: a per-week `reopen_week_internal` call writing its own `reopen_week` receipt and flipping `league_weeks` final → correction_window with that id in `reopened_by_action_id` (110's guard already demands exactly that), after which 129's existing enqueue loop covers the reopened weeks too. **A different ruling from Chris is now a SEPARATE task (F359), not a change to this one.**
- **✅ THE RULING (Chris, 2026-09-27, in chat): option 1, going forward only.** The option Chris chose read: *"The new rule applies to this week and later. Finished weeks keep their original scores and results."* A mid-season scoring change re-scores the **current open week and later weeks**; **final weeks are never re-scored**. ~~The shipped refusal of `rescore` on a final week (129 step (11b), `-- Q64 SEAM`, pinned by 077 G14) STANDS as the permanent behaviour — the seam is no longer a seam.~~ **[Corrected by the PR #312 review, R1090 — the orchestrator's reading of the chat record:** the shipped step (11b) — `129:831`, carried verbatim into the newest definer at `131:2741-2756` — RAISEs and rolls back the WHOLE call whenever `rescore = true` and ANY week is final, so from week 2 onward the open week can never be re-scored. That contradicts the ruling: a **defect, not a question** — **F382**, built right by **L.E1.24** (re-score the open weeks, skip the final ones by name).] **`reopen_week` is NOT wanted**: F359 → ✅ closed as not wanted; `league_weeks.reopened_by_action_id` and its FK stay, with **no planned writer** (and §12.12's `reopen_week` action-type value stays in the vocabulary, unused). Spec v2.16.42 strikes §10.1's *"reopen a finalized week"* and *"option to re-score prior weeks or not"* with corrections. **Not ruled, recorded as F381:** E57 / §23.5's *"reversible via rescore"* and §10.1's *"recompute a week from current stats"* are not the scoring-setting change this question asked about.
- **✅ BUILT 2026-09-27 by L.E1.24 (migration 141 / pgTAP 089; D378; F382 discharged).** `rescore = true` with a final week now LANDS: the open weeks (`live` + `correction_window`) are re-queued and the final weeks are named as kept (*"final week(s) [1] keep their original scores and results"*). Found while measuring, NOT this question's: after any scoring change the nightly reconcile and the box score re-derive a final week under the NEW rules (**F397**).
- **[+ 2026-09-27 — Q69 RULED (below):** a week in its stat-correction window is kept too — *"Q69 keep last week's scores"*. **141's re-scoring of a `correction_window` week is INTERIM and contradicts that ruling; L.E1.27 changes it (F404).** Q64's own words — *"this week and later"* — still govern the `live` week.**]**

**Q59 — DOES THE COMMISSIONER OVERRIDE LIFT *LEGALITY* AS WELL AS *TIMING*? RULED BY CHRIS 2026-09-11: NO. *"even a commish cannot break the positional rules."* TIMING IS LIFTED; POSITIONAL LEGALITY IS NOT.**

- **(RULING)** The line the L.E1.1 builder drew — timing lifted, legality kept — **stands as built**. A commissioner may edit after kickoff, in a closed week, in a past week; he may **not** seat a player in a slot his position does not admit. E16's bipartite fit (`lineup_fit_internal`) binds him exactly as it binds a manager, and no code change follows from this ruling.
- **(I WAS WRONG TWICE AND IT IS WORTH RECORDING WHY.)** I twice told Chris this question was my own invention — that the standing rule ("a commissioner can do anything") made the split an over-reach a builder had smuggled in, and offered to close it by lifting E16 and teaching `checkLineupLegality` the exception. **He ruled the opposite.** The standing rule is about AUTHORITY — which teams and which moments are his — and not about what constitutes a lineup at all. A quarterback slot holding a wide receiver is not an exercise of commissioner power; it is a malformed lineup, and no authority makes it well-formed. The lesson generalises: *"the commissioner can do anything"* does not mean *"any input is valid"*, and reading it that way turns a permission rule into a validation bypass.
- **(WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE.)** Q59 as filed bundled E16 with `allow_illegal_lineups` (the bye/OUT/inactive setting). Chris's words name the **positional** rules. The bye/OUT half is a per-league SETTING (§7.3.6) rather than a structural rule — his own league runs it TRUE, so the case does not arise there — and it is left as built (not lifted) until it arises in a league that runs it FALSE.
- **(THE PRINCIPLE, in Chris's words, and it generalises past this question.)** *"Here is why Q59 is different, it's not fixing something that's broken, it's changing the game entirely."* Recorded as standing-rule **(i)** above, because it is the test for every remaining §15.4 verb and not a fact about lineups.
- **(THE QUALITY-GATE ARGUMENT IS NOW MOOT, and should not be cited again.)** The build's stated reason for keeping E16 was that `checkLineupLegality` (`season-invariants.ts`) reds on any stored lineup the fit cannot seat, so a lawful commissioner lineup would fail a gate. That reasoning is retired by this ruling — the restriction stands on the product rule, not on the instrument. **Filed 2026-09-09, OPEN until this ruling.**

*(Original filing, kept for the record: OPEN, NOT DECIDED. Filed 2026-09-09 at the M6A L.E1.1/L.E1.2 fix round, because the call was being made inside a migration banner where nobody would find it.**

*Why it is a question and not a defect under the standing rule: §11.1:721 arguably already answers it, and the build deliberately did not follow that reading. The rule in (a) says a verb that refuses a commissioner is a defect — so this needs to be either fixed or explicitly excepted, in the open.*

- **(a) WHAT SHIPPED.** `commish_edit_lineup` (migration 123) lifts every **TIMING** rule: both per-player kickoff lock arms (114:449-462, 114:464-476), the matcher's own hidden copy of the lock (`fixed`, 112:498-505/518), the past-week and closed-week gates, the IR lock-timing gates and the Restricted-IR stint. It does **NOT** lift the **LEGALITY** rules: E16's bipartite-fit refusal (114:497-507), the `allow_illegal_lineups = FALSE` bye/OUT gate (114:605-616), the IR *designation* eligibility gate, or any shape/ownership gate. The line drawn is: *a timing refusal is lifted; a legality refusal is not.*
- **(b) THE SPEC ARGUABLY SAYS OTHERWISE.** §11.1:721 — *"Illegal rosters are blocked on normal actions … but never block the commissioner."* §11.2:725's annotation routes that clause to M6 as **F224(c)**. Read literally, `allow_illegal_lineups = FALSE` should not refuse this verb.
- **(c) THE MEASURED REASON IT WAS NOT TAKEN.** Season gate invariant 2, `checkLineupLegality` (`src/lib/leagues/sim/season-invariants.ts:303-337`), reds when ANY stored lineup has unplaced players or is REARRANGED by `lineup_fit_internal` — for **every** week of the season, final weeks included. Lifting E16 here would let a lawful commissioner lineup red a quality gate, and teaching that invariant provenance ("this one was a commissioner override") is real work that belongs with the verb that needs it.
- **(d) THE OBSERVABLE COST TODAY.** A league with `allow_illegal_lineups = FALSE` refuses the commissioner at `123`'s §7.3.6 arm with the same words a manager gets, when he tries to seat a bye/OUT player for an unreachable manager. Chris's ruling (g) is verbatim about games having **STARTED** — it names the lock and nothing else — so the shipped line is defensible, but it is a line, and it was drawn by a builder.
- **(e) RECOMMENDATION.** Lift `allow_illegal_lineups` for this verb (a bye/OUT starter is the commissioner's business and scores 0 either way — no invariant reads it), and **keep** E16 until `checkLineupLegality` can be taught the exception, because E16's refusal is "this arrangement cannot be seated at all", which is a different kind of statement from "this player will score 0". That splits (b) rather than deferring all of it. **Carried as F324 either way** — the ledger row exists so the deferral is visible there and not only here.

**Q56 — AN UNMANAGED TEAM CANNOT FIELD A LINEUP, SO A 1-HUMAN TEST LEAGUE SCORES ELEVEN ZEROES. MEASURED 2026-09-09 against Chris's live league. NOT a spec question — the spec promises this and the promise is UNBUILT.**

Found while answering "what about building our next milestone?" — it changes the answer, so it is recorded before it.

- **(a) THE MECHANISM, read not guessed.** `lineup_carry_internal` (116:369) populates a lineup ONLY from an earlier week: `IF v_from IS NOT NULL THEN` (116:456) over `tl.week < p_week`. **Week 1 has no earlier row, so the carried map is `{}` and every slot lands in `v_f_empty` (116:513).** That is correct and intended for week 1 — a manager sets the first lineup. The problem is the team that has no manager to set it.
- **(b) CHRIS'S LEAGUE, as it actually stands.** 12 franchises, **1 human, 11 `is_placeholder` seats with `user_id` NULL** (measured). `set_lineup` is manager-scoped, and `roster_add_drop` refuses a commissioner acting on another team by name (`113:486-495`). So in week 1 his own team fields a lineup and **eleven field nothing**: his matchup is a real score against a zero, and the other five matchups are zero against zero. The in-season half of the 2026 cohort test produces no signal at all.
- **(c) THE SPEC PROMISES THE FIX ONCE, AND IT IS NOT BUILT. [CORRECTED 2026-09-09 — I first wrote "TWICE" and that was an over-claim; the M6A survey caught it.]** The one promise is §7.2.1(c): an orphaned team runs on *"autopilot"* and its *"Lineups auto-set (last valid, healthy-substitution per existing autopick logic)"* (`spec:185`). **§7.2's capacity rule (`spec:173`) is NOT a second promise of it** — its subject is starting a DRAFT (*"Cannot start a draft until…"*), and the "autopick" it names is `league_members.is_autodraft`, which the draft tick reads and which **nothing in migrations 109–122 reads at all** (the entire in-season stack; measured, zero hits). Counting it as a second promise overstates the spec's coverage and would let a builder claim §7.2 authorizes a lineup behaviour it never mentions.
  - **What exists is the DRAFT half only** — `110:1033`, *"Orphaned seats count (they draft on autopilot — E48)"*. Grep finds no lineup autopilot anywhere. And a placeholder seat is not `orphaned` in the first place (no stint ever opened), so even the built half addresses a different state.
  - **Also corrected:** `is_placeholder` and `user_id` are columns on **`league_members`**, not on `teams` (`052:66-69`; a `teams` query for `is_placeholder` errors 42703). The counts in (b) are right; the table was wrong by implication, which matters because autopilot's "this seat has no manager" predicate must read `league_members` (or `team_managers`), never `teams`.
- **(d) A SPEC/REALITY DIVERGENCE WORTH FIXING BEFORE ANYONE SCOPES M6.** §7.2's "Generalized Act as Manager" (v2.6, `spec:194`) closes with *"No new persistent state: this reuses the existing `acting_as_team_id` tagging already built for orphaned teams (§12.12) — the only change is that the UI stops gating the 'Act as' entry point."* **That premise is false as-built. `acting_as_team_id` exists nowhere** — measured three ways: absent from every migration, absent from `src/`, and absent from the production database's `information_schema.columns`. So Act-as-Manager is NOT a UI un-gating: it needs the column, the §12.12 audit tagging, and a second authorization arm on every manager verb (`set_lineup`, `roster_add_drop`, and M5's waiver/trade verbs when they land), each of which refuses a non-manager today. Anyone estimating M6 off `spec:194`'s closing sentence will estimate it far too low.
- **(e) THE TWO SHAPES, and they are not alternatives.** **Autopilot** (a team with NO manager gets a lineup by rule) is what makes a placeholder-heavy test league score anything without a human in the loop, and it is what §7.2.1(c) already promises. **Act-as-Manager** (the commissioner acts FOR a named team, audited) is what Chris asked for all day and is the fallback for every exception. A 1-human/11-bot league needs (i) to score at all; a real league with a quiet manager needs (ii).
- **(f) WHY IT LANDS ON THE MILESTONE QUESTION.** M4's own exit criterion 2 is the real-2026 replay, calendar-blocked on the first recorded week — which is THIS week. The cohort's in-season feedback starts now, and (b) says it starts empty. Recommendation: a narrow slice — **lineup autopilot for unmanaged seats + Act-as-Manager on the verbs that exist today** — ahead of M5, with M5's waiver/trade verbs picking up the same second auth arm as they are written rather than retrofitting it. M8 already depends on M5 (there are no waivers to pause before it), so nothing downstream is disturbed by the insert.

**Q55 — THE DRAFT BOARD CANNOT SHOW A COMMISSIONER'S OWNERSHIP MOVE. Reported by Chris 2026-09-09 mid-draft; diagnosed the same hour. Not a bug in the move — a limit of the grid.**

*"so after using the Move team feature, the draft board didn't reflect the player moves. so how does that work?"*

- **(a) THE MOVES LANDED.** Measured in production: Bijan Robinson (pick 2) Team 7 → Team 2 and Christian McCaffrey (pick 5) Team 6 → Team 2, at 19:10:20 and 19:10:32, each with its §8.7 row-5 system post in `league_chat`. `draft_move_player` writes `UPDATE draft_picks SET team_id` (100:1082) and the realtime trigger covers UPDATE as well as INSERT (`070:270`), and `reducePickUpdate` patches `team_id` in place — with a comment recording that this exact class of drop was already found and fixed once, as R260. **The whole chain is correct.**
- **(b) THE GRID IS INDEXED BY PICK NUMBER, NOT BY OWNER.** `buildBoardModel` places every cell at `slotIndexForPick(pickNumber, …)` (`draft-board-ops.ts:113`) and the column headers are the stored round-1 `draft_order` (`draft-board-grid.tsx:76`). A moved player therefore stays in the cell he was drafted into — under the column of the team that no longer owns him. `draft-board-ops.ts`'s own header says so deliberately: a commissioner move *"renders the row's truth **in place**"*.
- **(c) SO THE ONLY VISIBLE CHANGE IS A 9px SUFFIX.** The cell's third line is `{team}{byManager ? ' · ' + byManager : ''}` (`draft-pick.tsx:77`) — `text-[9px]`, `truncate`, in a `minmax(96px, 1fr)` column. Bijan's cell now reads `ATL · Team 2` beneath a header saying `Team 7`. It did change; it is illegible and contradicts the column above it.
- **(d) WHERE OWNERSHIP IS RIGHT.** The roster and recap surfaces derive per-team rosters from `draft_picks` (`draft-recap-ops.ts:69`), so they show the true owner. The board is the one surface that structurally cannot.
- **(e) RECOMMENDATION, small and geometry-preserving:** when a made cell's `team_id` differs from `teamForPick`'s predicted slot owner, render an explicit override marker (a `→ Team 2` badge) instead of a truncated suffix. The card stays where it was drafted — which is the honest record of who picked when — but the override stops being invisible. Worth noting ESPN and Sleeper avoid the question entirely by not moving players on the board; ownership lives on rosters.

**Q54 — THE DRAFT ROOM NEEDS ITS OWN DOOR, OPENABLE AT ANY TIME. RULED BY CHRIS 2026-09-09. Not a spec question; recorded here because it came in the same breath as Q50–Q53 and because two adjacent UX faults share its cause.**

*"okay there needs to be an Enter draft room button. users should be able to enter the draft room anytime, even before it's scheduled. sure there's nothing to do there, but you can still open it and exit it. that's how ESPN and Sleeper work."*

- **(a) THE ROOM ALREADY OBEYS THIS RULING.
