**Q13 — Exit Draft: where does it go, and should leaving mid-draft warn? (filed by the draft-room redesign Architect session, 2026-08-17; spec §16.4 zone 1. Does NOT block any DR task — DR.2 builds the recommendation.)**

**Evidence.** You ruled **Exit Draft appears in the top bar for both commissioner and non-commissioner** — everyone must be able to leave. With the room in its own browser tab (desktop), "leaving" has two plausible meanings that the shipped **Exit room** link (`snake-draft-room.tsx:704–706`, a plain link to `/app/leagues/[id]`) never had to distinguish: navigate this tab back to the league, or close the tab. There is a hard constraint on the second: **`window.close()` only works on a tab a script opened**, so it would work when you came from the in-app CTA and **fail silently** on a deep link, a refresh, or a bookmarked room — the worst kind of button.

**Options:**
- **(a) Navigate in place to league home; never close the tab; no confirmation (recommended).** One behavior on every entry path, no silent failures. No warning on the way out because leaving costs nothing real — the draft continues without you and autopick covers your picks (§8.4), which is exactly what it is for.
- **(b) Navigate in place, but confirm when it is YOUR turn.** Honest about the one moment leaving is expensive. Costs a modal on the room's most time-pressured surface, and the clock keeps running while you read it.
- **(c) Try to close the tab, fall back to navigating.** Rejected: the same button does two different things depending on how you arrived, and users learn buttons by what they did last time.

**Recommendation: (a)**, with (b) available later as a small addition if test-cohort feedback says people leave by accident. Flagged because "Exit" doing something you did not expect is a trust problem, not a polish problem.

**What's gated:** nothing. DR.2 builds (a).

**RULED 2026-08-17 (Chris): option (a)'s MECHANICS — navigate in place to league home, never `window.close()`, no confirmation — but the REASON is different from the one recommended, and the reason is what gets built.** Verbatim: *"Exit draft just exits you from the draft room and after a certain amount of time puts you into 'auto draft' mode. Which is how all mock drafts work."*

**The recommendation's rationale is corrected here.** It said "no warning because leaving costs nothing real". That is wrong: **leaving DOES hand your picks to the engine — and that is intended and expected**, the incumbent mental model Chris is naming (you leave, the bots draft for you). The mechanics are unchanged; what changes is that the behavior is a *stated feature*, not a cost to be papered over.

**Which mechanism — the load-bearing half of this ruling.** Two distinct autopick paths exist and **Exit triggers only the first**:
- **The D102 away path (§8.5.5's v2.8.13 erratum, migration 068) — THIS is what Exit fires.** The room's `draft_touch` heartbeat stops when you leave; after the 45s freshness constant (`draft_liveness_freshness()`, `068_draft_tick_autopick.sql:347–355` — 3 × the 15s room cadence) the seat reads **STALE**; at each of that manager's deadlines the pick is then **held open for `disconnect_grace_seconds`** (§7.3.8, default 30) and autopicked from queue → primary board → Big Board → ADP (§8.4). **Returning to the room restores manual control immediately** — the next heartbeat re-freshens the seat, and a manager who returns mid-hold may still pick by hand (E3).
- **The persistent `is_autodraft` toggle** (`league_members.is_autodraft`, §8.4's "Auto-draft me"; §12.2:762). This keeps autopicking **even after you come back**, until it is explicitly switched off.

**Exit must trigger the first and must NOT write the second.** `is_autodraft` is a deliberate, sticky choice a manager (or a commissioner on their behalf) makes; setting it on exit would silently strip a returning manager of manual control and make them hunt for a toggle to get it back. The heartbeat/staleness machinery already delivers exactly what Chris described, with the strictly better return-to-control property. **DR.2 must not touch `is_autodraft`**, and needs no new mechanism at all — Exit is a navigation.

**Verified against the code 2026-08-17 (the ruling depended on it, so it was checked rather than assumed).** The heartbeat is a `useEffect` at `src/hooks/use-draft.ts:394–413`; its cleanup (`:409–412`) calls `clearInterval(id)` and removes the `visibilitychange` listener. Navigating away unmounts the room, React runs that cleanup, and **no further `draft_touch` calls are made** — so leaving genuinely stops the heartbeat today. (The effect is additionally gated on `heartbeatActive` — defined at `:393`, early-returned at `:395` — so it never runs outside `live`/`paused`; and closing the tab stops the interval with or without the cleanup.) **There is no gap to close — DR.2 inherits working machinery** rather than owning a fix.

**Consequence for copy (part of the ruling, not a nicety).** Exit's affordance must say what actually happens. "Exit Draft" alone is not sufficient: the control states that **picks will be made from the manager's Targets while they are away, and that returning restores manual control**. The vehicle is the Builder's within the no-confirmation ruling — a `title`/tooltip on the control, a short line in the command bar, or a brief toast on the way out — but a confirmation modal is explicitly not one of the options (§16.5.4's designed-copy rule). Folded into spec §16.4 zone 1; **DR.2 owns it**.

**Q12 — Does the chrome-free full-screen treatment extend to the LOBBY and the RECAP? (filed by the draft-room redesign Architect session, 2026-08-17; spec §16.1's v2.12 note. Does NOT block any DR task — DR.1/DR.7 build the recommendation.)**

**Evidence.** Your ruling names "the Draft Room". Two neighbouring surfaces are not obviously in or out. **The lobby is not a choice:** it shares the `/draft` route and the room flips lobby→live **in place** (D120), so it inherits the chrome-free frame by construction — the only alternative would be splitting the route, which would break the in-place flip that makes draft-night feel live. **The recap is a real choice:** `…/draft/recap` (`src/app/app/leagues/[leagueId]/draft/recap/page.tsx`) is a separate route serving both the real and mock variants — a post-draft *reading* surface people revisit days later, where the nav, search and the right rail are useful rather than noise.

**Options:**
- **(a) Lobby chrome-free (forced), recap stays in the app shell (recommended).** The chrome-free treatment is for the live, time-pressured experience; the recap is a document. Keeping the recap in the shell also means the way *out* of it is the app's own nav rather than a bespoke exit.
- **(b) Both chrome-free.** Consistent — "everything under `/draft` is full-screen" is an easy rule to remember — but it puts a reading surface in a frame with no navigation, so every route out has to be rebuilt inside it.
- **(c) Lobby in the shell, room chrome-free.** Rejected on the mechanics above: it would break the in-place lobby→live flip.

**Recommendation: (a).** Recorded in spec v2.12 as the working assumption so the DR tasks have something to build; say the word and (b) is a small change to one route group.

**What's gated:** nothing.

**RULED 2026-08-17 (Chris): option (a) — the lobby and the live room are chrome-free; the recap keeps the app shell.** Verbatim: *"having a bunch unnecessary UI mid draft doesn't make sense… you need all the space you have for the draft surfaces"*, naming ESPN, Yahoo and Sleeper as doing exactly this.

**The framing above is replaced — Chris pushed back on it and he was right.** The full-screen treatment exists for **one reason: the live draft is space-hungry, and any app chrome on screen mid-draft is space taken from a draft surface.** That is a UX reason and it is the whole reason — not a route-mechanics argument, and not an open architectural question about where the app shell belongs. The lobby and the live room share the `/draft` route and are both part of that live surface, so both are chrome-free. **The recap was never in scope of the ruling**: it is not a draft surface at all — it is a post-draft reading page people revisit days later — so it keeps the app shell, and the app's own navigation is the way out of it.

Recorded as **a rule with its reason** in spec §16.1 (the v2.12 note's last paragraph rewritten in place) and in the **DR.1** / **DR.7** banners. *(If consistency is ever wanted, flipping the recap to full-screen is a one-route-group change — it moves from `(shell)` to `(room)` and nothing else changes.)*

**Q12 — §7.3.3.1 (spec v2.11, custom scoring editor): are K and D/ST editable in the test-cohort editor? (filed 2026-08-16 by the scoring-editor Architect session, PR #152.)** Chris's C37 requirements define the five sections for "every position except K and DEF" and named no K/D-ST sample players — silent on whether those two positions are editable at all. Options were **(a)** editable, one single-section page each; **(b)** template-locked (K/D-ST silently inherit the starting template's tables); **(c)** hidden entirely. Recommendation was (a).

**RULED 2026-08-16 (Chris): (a) — K and D/ST ARE editable**, one single-section page each, and the **sample players are NAMED, not generic: Neil Rackers (K) and the Seahawks (D/ST)**, joining Marino (QB) / Peterson (RB) / Moss (WR) / Gronk (TE). Their stat lines are written into §7.3.3.1 like the offensive four (K: 2 FG 0–39, 1 FG 40–49, 1 FG 50+, 3 PAT, 1 miss · D/ST: 3 sacks, 1 INT, 1 fumble rec, 1 def TD, 17 PA, 289 YA — the PA/YA figures deliberately sit near a family cut point so tier behavior is visible).

**CORRECTION recorded with the ruling (the filed question's option (a) was wrong on the facts and Chris pushed back):** the phrase *"the PA/YA bucketization chosen as a preset set (shared vs ESPN)"* implied points-allowed and yards-allowed are alternatives a commissioner picks between. **They are not.** They are two independent tables that pay **additively** — a defense's week is its events **plus** its PA tier **plus** (where the model carries one) its YA tier; ESPN pays both, the single-model platforms pay PA only (the D44 `dst_model` distinction). What actually varies between families is **where the tiers are cut** (ESPN 14–17/18–27/35–45/46+ vs shared 14–20/21–27/35+). Every site carrying the bad framing was rewritten in the same fold (§7.3.3.1 editable-scope + section catalog + guardrail 2, §23.5).

**RULED the same session — defense tiers, two parts.** **(a) The document format reserves per-league tier boundaries NOW** (`tier_cuts`), even though the UI ships later: cut points can only live in the league's own scoring doc, so adding them later would force a **third** format version plus a migration of every stored doc and a re-proof that every frozen draft snapshot still scores identically — deciding now costs nothing, deciding later costs a migration. Tier keys are **generated** from the cut list; the generation rule was **verified to regenerate all three of today's families byte-exactly** against `templates.ts` (ESPN PA 8 keys, shared PA 7, YA 9), which is the backward-compatibility argument and gets a pin. **(b) First-version UI inherits boundaries from the starting template and does NOT edit them** — no preset-set dropdown, no boundary fields; the commissioner edits **what each tier pays**. Boundary editing is its own task immediately after the editor: **ledger row F59**, routed to a follow-up Architect breakdown, explicitly not in the cohort editor build.

**RULED the same session — the boundary INPUT DESIGN, recorded now so the F59 follow-up inherits it:** boundaries are entered as **CUT POINTS, not ranges** — one ascending integer list per table (e.g. `0, 7, 14, 18, 28, 35, 46`), each tier derived as `[this cut, next cut)` with the last open-ended. This makes overlapping tiers and coverage gaps **structurally unconstructible** rather than validation-caught (freehand ranges admit both the F21 double-pay overlap and silent-zero gaps; derived-from-cuts admits neither — the same posture as the F21 guardrails). Residual validation is trivial: ascending, integers, ≥ 2 cuts; the PA and YA tables are independent (different domains, own cut lists).

**Q13 — §7.3.3.1/§23.5 (spec v2.11): `return_yards` for the Special Teams section — the stat does not exist in the system (no registry key, no `player_stats` column, no provider mapping). (filed 2026-08-16, PR #152.)** Chris's requirement (3) names Special Teams "e.g. return yards"; the only scorable special-teams key today is `return_td`. Options were **(a)** ship `return_td` now and add `return_yards` via a parallel §23.5 data task with the editor field code-gated (the C43 pattern); **(b)** block the editor build on adding the stat first; **(c)** drop return yards. Recommendation was (a).

**RULED 2026-08-16 (Chris): (a)** — his words: *"Ship with return TDs with the ability to easily add yards when we find a source."* **The emphasis on "easily" is folded in as a requirement on the design, not a hope:** §7.3.3.1's Special Teams bullet now spells the future data task as a 4-step checklist — (1) map the feed field in the provider adapter into `player_stats.advanced` (no migration, §23.5's storage rule); (2) add one `STAT_KEYS` entry (`return_yards`, `core_box`, `storage: 'advanced'`, `scoring_surface: 'scorable'`); (3) add the key to the Special Teams section catalog and flip its code gate on; (4) done — calculator, resolver, guardrails, and editor rendering are all key-agnostic. To keep step (3) trivial the editor renders sections **from the catalog** and the gated field is a catalog flag, never a hand-written form row. Nothing about the format, the snapshot, or scoring changes when it lands.

**Q11 — §7.2.1:190's notification recipient on the VOLUNTARY-LEAVE path: is the departing user notified, or only the commissioner? (filed by the M1 batch-15 remediation per R96, 2026-07-26; STOP-CONDITION HALT of R96's leave-path notification pin — the rest of the batch landed.)**

**Evidence.** §7.2.1's "Removal mechanics (all paths)" bullet at spec:190 reads: *"The removed user is notified with the outcome category (removed / left / franchise retired) and can be re-invited later — to any team, including their old franchise."* spec:192 then says *"Voluntary leave uses the same flow with `end_reason='left'`"*, which pulls the voluntary path INTO that bullet block. The parenthetical's three categories map to the §12.22 `end_reason` values that end a tenure (removed = `kicked`, left = `left`, franchise retired = `seat_retired`), and `left` is written by exactly ONE path in the repo: `leave_league` (063). Shipped behaviour: `remove_manager` notifies the REMOVED user on both takeover (`event: replaced`) and vacate (`event: removed`) — consistent with the bullet under either reading — while `leave_league` notifies **the sitting commissioner** ("A manager left <league>", `event: left`) and writes NOTHING to the departing user. The commissioner recipient is spec-silent: §7.2.1 never names the commissioner as a notification recipient anywhere (the nearest precedent is E54/spec:1734, "commissioner notified", for a near-simultaneous seat-claim collision — a different event, implemented in 062).

**Why this is a stop and not a Builder call.** Whether a user who just left gets a receipt is a PRODUCT decision (this file's §4 preamble routes product/scope calls to the spec changelog, not the decisions log), and both readings are defensible: **(a)** the block says "all paths", `left` can only mean the voluntary path, so the leaver IS a named recipient and the code omits a required notification; **(b)** "the REMOVED user" has no referent on a path where nobody was removed — the leaver performed the act synchronously and already has the RPC's success response, so the parenthetical is category VOCABULARY and the party who learns something new is the commissioner now holding an open seat. Under (a) the shipped code diverges from the spec; under (b) it is correct and the commissioner notification is a sanctioned addition. Pinning today's behaviour would silently cement (b) — precisely what R96's fix direction warned against.

**Options:**
- **(a) The leaver is notified too (recommended).** `leave_league` additionally calls the notifier for the departing user with the `left` category ("You left <league>"), keeping the commissioner notification as a spec-silent-but-useful addition recorded in the changelog. Correct under BOTH readings; ~6 lines plus one pin. The "it's noise" objection is real but bounded — §16's notification matrix (spec:1546) already defaults everything non-urgent to digests, and this is the least urgent class there is.
- **(b) Only the commissioner is notified (record the reading).** Rule that spec:190 addresses commissioner-initiated removals only; a one-clause §7.2.1 erratum says so and names the commissioner as the voluntary path's recipient. No code change — and the erratum is what stops this being re-found at every review.
- **(c) Both, with the leaver's as a digest-only receipt.** Needs a priority/digest flag `notifications` does not have, i.e. a new column for a row nothing consumes yet (F34: this notification has no consumer until L.A2.5/L.A2.7). Not recommended.

**Recommendation: (a)** — the only option correct under both readings, and smaller than the erratum (b) requires. Flagged as a product call because a notification's recipient set is very hard to change once a consumer exists.

**What's gated (precisely):** ONLY R96's leave-path notification pin, and any change to who `leave_league` notifies. Everything else in batch 15 landed on `feat/M1-L.A1.15-member-management`: R90–R95 and R97–R99 complete, full green proof chain, and R96's takeover/vacate row pins landed too (their recipient is the removed user under BOTH readings, so they cement nothing). **No task is blocked and no §5 blocker is filed** — the Q10 precedent for a question that gates a fix rather than a lane. L.A1.15 is done; the next lane heads (L.A2.x UI) do not consume this notification. Apply the ruling in whichever session next touches 063, or as a one-line PR; ledger row **F37** carries it.

**RULED 2026-07-26 (Chris): notify BOTH the user leaving AND the league manager (commissioner)** — recommendation (a), the reading correct under BOTH interpretations of §7.2.1:190. Applied same-day (M1 batch-16 remediation, same branch/PR #60): `leave_league` (063) now calls `notify_league_member_internal` for the departing user (`league_member` / "You left <league>" / `event: 'left'`) in addition to the pre-existing sitting-commissioner notification. **The deferred pin landed**: pgTAP 017 §S now pins BOTH the departing-user row and the commissioner row on §K's L1 leave (privileged 016-style read, `event='left'` scoped so it isolates from u5's earlier `removed` row). **Spec fidelity:** §7.2.1:190's "removed / left / franchise retired" categories already covered the departing user under reading (a) — now authoritative — but §7.2.1 named NO commissioner recipient anywhere, so the commissioner-too behaviour was spec-silent; folded in as spec erratum **v2.8.9** (§7.2.1:192 now names both recipients + changelog). **F37 flipped ✅**; the §5 Q11 note is cleared. Mechanics + the rest of batch 16 in D76.

**Q10 — `playoff_start_week` ↔ `regular_season_weeks` consistency: §7.3.1 promises a validation §7.3.8 never defines, and no formula fits the printed ranges (filed by the M1 batch-6 remediation per R62, 2026-07-22; substance observed by L.A1.6/D60(12), previously carried only as ledger row F25 — this entry puts it in the ruling queue).**

**Evidence:** §7.3.1's `playoff_start_week` row (D 15 · R 14–17 · note *"Validated against `regular_season_weeks`."*) promises a cross-field check, but §7.3.8's validation-bullet list contains no such bullet and prints no formula — and no formula is consistent with the printed ranges: strict continuity `playoff_start_week = regular_season_weeks + 1` is **unsatisfiable at `regular_season_weeks = 12`** (would need start 13; the printed floor is 14) and makes start 17 unreachable (would need a 16-week regular season; the ceiling is 15), while anything looser permits **gap weeks** (e.g. regular 12 + start 17 → weeks 13–16 belong to neither the season nor the playoffs, and nothing defines what an idle league week IS — L.D0's schedule engine has no such concept). With no check at all — the shipped state — an **overlap** is expressible: `regular_season_weeks = 15` + `playoff_start_week = 14` parses clean and `validateLeagueSettings` accepts it (L.A1.6 implemented exactly the task-enumerated §7.3.8 bullets, deliberately not improvising a formula — D60(12)). The §7.3.8 arithmetic bullet (`start + rounds × weeks_per_round − 1 ≤ 18`) bounds the playoff END only; it says nothing about the seam.

**Options:**
- **(a) Strict continuity + range erratum (recommended).** Rule `playoff_start_week = regular_season_weeks + 1`; spec erratum adjusts the printed R from 14–17 to **13–16** (13 reachable only at a 12-week season) and the schema range follows. No overlap, no gap weeks, no new concepts; the field becomes fully derived — the wizard can render it read-only next to `regular_season_weeks` (the `playoff_byes = 'auto'` precedent), with the stored value kept for §12.1 compat. Incumbent-consistent: ESPN/Yahoo/Sleeper all derive the playoff start; none lets a commissioner express an overlap.
- **(b) No-overlap lower bound only.** Rule `playoff_start_week ≥ regular_season_weeks + 1`; printed ranges stay. Kills the overlap but leaves gap weeks expressible, and gap-week semantics (standings? waivers? locks?) would then need defining somewhere before M4's schedule engine — a bigger spec debt than the seam check itself.
- **(c) Explicit won't-validate ruling.** Record that §7.3.1's note is aspirational in v1; the per-field ranges are the only guard and seam consistency is the commissioner's problem. Cheapest, but ships a settings surface that accepts playoffs starting before the season ends — and the note column then needs an erratum anyway (it currently promises otherwise).

**Recommendation: (a).** It is the only option with neither silent overlap nor undefined gap-week semantics; the cost is a two-line erratum (§7.3.1 R column + note, one §7.3.8 bullet) plus a ~6-line check in `validateLeagueSettings` with boundary pins — one small PR once ruled.

**What's gated (precisely):** NOT the current lane heads — engine is at L.A1.10 and schema at L.A1.11, neither touches playoff-week validation, so **no §5 blocker is filed**. The ruling gates **L.A1.12**: `create_league` (+ the L.A2.1 wizard on top of it) is the first surface that can PERSIST an inconsistent pair — creation must not ship on the unruled validator. L.A1.13's settings PATCH is the second exposure, not the first (the F25 row's original routing said L.A1.13 — corrected per R62). L.A1.6 itself remains complete; this question is bookkeeping mis-filed at first, not a new halt.

**RULED 2026-07-22 (Chris): option (a) — verbatim answer "a" — strict continuity `playoff_start_week = regular_season_weeks + 1`.** Applied 2026-07-25 (branch `feat/M1-Q10-playoff-seam-ruling` — the "one small PR once ruled" this entry promised): spec erratum **v2.8.6** (§7.3.1 R column 14–17 → **13–16**, note now names the formula; ONE new §7.3.8 seam bullet — no overlap, no gap weeks; changelog carries the rationale: 13 reachable only at a 12-week season, 17 unreachable and dropped, incumbent-consistent, field effectively derived). 5. **Sleeper scoring-options article** (support.sleeper.com/en/articles/3998131-scoring-settings) — categories reconfirmed (PA = shared family buckets; YA buckets = ESPN's nine; FG buckets 0–19/20–29/30–39/40–49/50+, **no 60+ tier**) — but the article publishes **no default values**, and a support-center search ("default league settings") finds no Sleeper defaults article. Sleeper's in-product creation defaults sit behind account login (out of bounds). **Per the house verification rule (this task's charter): Sleeper's six template value-sets ship as App B best-known values FLAGGED unverified (ledger row on landing), never silently trusted.**

**The blocking finding (1): ESPN's default kicking table has a 60+ = 6 tier — App B.4's three-bucket shape (`fg_0_39`/`fg_40_49`/`fg_50_plus` at 3/4/5) cannot express it.** Product-confirmed twice, independently: the Scoring-Formats standard table (60+ = 6, 50–59 = 5) and both in-product default payloads (`[198,5]` = FG 50–59, `[201,6]` = FG 60+ — 198/201 are the only unaccounted 5/6-valued kicker ids, and their values match the article exactly). This is not a value drift on an existing key — it is a **category the engine's namespace cannot represent**: no `fg_50_59`/`fg_60_plus` keys exist, no columns exist, and — decisive — **the Sleeper feed has no 60+ signal** (`fgm_50p` aggregates everything ≥50; the L.A1.7 adapter audit lists sub-40 buckets but nothing above 50), so even new keys would have no data source on the current tier. Consequence: cent parity for ESPN templates is unachievable as-is on made 60+ FGs (order ~5–15 league-wide per NFL season; −1 pt each vs ESPN's product).

**The blocking finding (2), same class, smaller:** ESPN's defaults score two D/ST PAT micro-categories — PAT-safety = +1 (`[209,1,{16:1}]`) and PAT-return = +2 (`[206,2,{16:2}]`), both also published in the D/ST article. No catalog keys, no columns, no feed signal on any current provider tier (order ~1–3 plays league-wide per season).

**Why this is a stop and not an L.A1.7-style recorded erratum:** L.A1.7's charter explicitly licensed "seed what ESPN actually publishes and note the delta" (additive derived keys, no storage or feed dependency). L.A1.9's charter says the opposite — "Divergences from App B: stop and file a spec question (parity guarantee is the product promise — never silently ship drifted values)" — and this divergence has real options with product impact (below), including one that would add player_stats columns (schema beyond the task). Value-level per-platform differences (Yahoo's no-miss-penalty kicking, ESPN's no-PAT-miss) are NOT treated as divergences: B.1 defers K/D-ST to "each platform's own tables (⚠ verify)", so the verified platform table governs those cells; the stop is specifically for categories the catalog/namespace cannot express.

**Options:**
- **(a) Documented parity exception (recommended).** ESPN templates ship `fg_50_plus = 5`; the 60+ extra point and the two PAT micro-categories become a **named, documented parity exception** in §7.3.3/App B (spec changelog entry): "ESPN parity is cent-exact except made 60+ FGs (−1 pt vs ESPN) and D/ST PAT-safety/PAT-return (unscored) — categories the current data tier cannot observe." Rationale: the alternative keys would be **permanently pending/zero** for lack of any feed signal — a standing E61 state manufactured on every ESPN league every week is strictly worse than a documented ~1-pt/season-scale exception; and the parity guarantee's operative promise ("a migrating league's scores feel identical") survives a documented exception, not a standing honest-badge.
- **(b) Add `fg_50_59`/`fg_60_plus` (+ PAT-micro) keys and columns now.** Expresses the table, but no provider signal exists to fill them — every ESPN league shows permanent pending on those keys (E61), and it adds player_stats columns from inside a task chartered for `is_template` + seed only.
- **(c) = (a) + a September F-row:** the F10 raw-endpoint inspection window additionally checks whether Sleeper's raw feed carries a 60+ FG spelling (e.g. `fgm_60p`) and PAT-play detail; if a signal exists, upgrading ESPN kicking parity becomes the one-PR §23.5 data task it should be, and the exception shrinks or closes.
- **Recommendation: (a) + (c)'s September check.** One ruling line unblocks L.A1.9; the post-ruling build is mechanical (all six platforms' evidence is already in this entry).

**What's blocked:** L.A1.9 (migration 058 + pgTAP 012 + the 6 template rows) and the schema lane behind it (L.A1.11), plus L.A1.10/L.A1.12's template-row dependencies. **Not blocked:** L.A1.6 (engine lane, pure TS — still open and unstarted). F19 stays ⬜ Open (it discharges only when the ESPN rows land) but both its sub-obligations are answered above; the landing session should cite this entry in the 058 banner rather than refetching.

**RULED 2026-07-22 (Chris): option (a) + (c).** Ship `fg_50_plus = 5`; the ESPN 60+ FG tier (6 pts) and the two PAT micro-categories (+1 PAT-safety, +2 PAT-return) are **NAMED PARITY EXCEPTIONS**, not pending categories — recorded as a spec erratum (**v2.8.5**: §7.3.3 parity-guarantee erratum + App B.4 annotation + changelog) with the rationale (provider-unobservable, ~5–15 plays league-wide per season, permanent-pending would violate E61 semantics). **Condition:** the exceptions must be user-visible in the ESPN templates' description/detail metadata — a plain-language line a commissioner can read — not only in migration banners. **(c):** the September F10 check additionally looks for a Sleeper raw-feed 60+ spelling (e.g. `fgm_60p`) and PAT-play detail; if a signal exists, the tier becomes expressible as a one-PR §23.5 data task and the exception lifts — path noted in the erratum. Implementation: migration **058** + pgTAP **012** + `src/lib/leagues/scoring/templates.ts` (D59); the exception line lives in `scoring_systems.description` (the schema's existing detail column — a natural home, no schema change needed) and is pinned verbatim by pgTAP 012 and the templates tests. Sleeper's unpublished default values ship App-B-flagged per the house rule — ledger **F24**. B3 cleared; F19 flipped ✅.

**Q7 — Q4-application conflicts the conflict report didn't surface (filed 2026-07-20; STOP-CONDITION HALT of L.A1.1).** Recording the Q4 ruling (usernames 5–20, permanent) against the actual codebase hit two conflicts that C5 never surfaced, tripping the Builder session's ruling-vs-codebase stop condition — the migration was **not** written:

1. **AI persona accounts live in `profiles.username` with hyphenated handles** — `fieldscout-ai` (system owner) plus the ~19-persona roster (`bathew-merry-ai`, `zj-jachariason-ai`, …; `src/lib/personas/roster.ts`), created as real auth users + profiles rows by `scripts/seed-ai-personas.ts:88`, **existing in production** (the personas feature is live). *[Corrected — see D49(9)/R36: the roster personas are `ai_personas` rows, not profiles rows; only `fieldscout-ai` holds a profiles row. The conflict (and the ruling below) stands either way — the exempt pattern must cover every persona-shape handle a privileged writer seeds.]* A blocklist test *enforces* the `-ai` suffix (`blocklist.test.ts:41`), and the handles key avatar file paths + public URLs. Every one violates the `[a-z0-9_]` charset §7.2 gives the username contract — the CHECK as ruled would **fail the prod push** and break persona seeding. Needs your call: **(a)** exempt persona/system accounts — the CHECK becomes `human-pattern OR persona-pattern` (e.g. hyphenated, `-ai`-suffixed). Bonus: keeping hyphens out of the human charset means **no human can ever register a `*-ai` handle** — free namespace separation for the AI-transparency convention; **(b)** allow hyphens for everyone (loses that separation); **(c)** rename personas to underscores (touches public URLs, avatar files on disk, the blocklist tests, and any indexed content). **Recommendation: (a).**
2. **The account-settings page ships a live username-**change** flow** (`src/app/app/settings/page.tsx:173–181` — editable field, saves `username` with its own 3–30 validator), contradicting PERMANENT. Related definitional wrinkle: "no changing after creation" needs a boundary — signup *creates* the profile with an auto-generated `user_xxxxxxxx` placeholder, and the username-selection page (`/username`) is itself an UPDATE, so a literal no-update-after-creation guard would break onboarding. **Recommendation:** permanent = **after explicit selection** (the placeholder is pre-selection); remove the username field from settings (display-only `@handle`); typo/regret recovery is a support/admin path, not self-serve; a DB-level permanence guard is deferred until the selection flow moves server-side (an RPC that can tell selection from rename).
3. *(Minor, listed for completeness:)* `scripts/seed-dev-user.ts` seeds username `'dev'` (3 chars) — breaks under the 5-minimum; mechanical rename (e.g. `dev_user`/`dev_pro`) ships with the Q4 migration.

**What's blocked:** L.A1.1 (migration 040 carries the Q4 constraint per your ruling) and the serialized schema lane behind it. **Not blocked:** L.A1.6 (engine lane, pure TS). The Q5/Q6 rulings had no conflicts and are fully recorded/applied. One line from you on (1) and (2) unblocks the lane.
**RESOLVED 2026-07-20 (Chris): recommendations accepted for items 1, 2, and 3.** (1) Persona exemption **(a)**: the DB CHECK is `username ~ '^[a-z0-9_]{5,20}$' OR username ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*-ai$'` — human charset stays hyphen-free, so no human can register a `*-ai` handle (enforced at the DB layer by a 025-pattern guard trigger blocking persona-pattern usernames for `authenticated`/`anon`, since the CHECK alone can't tell a persona insert from a hostile PostgREST rename). (2) Permanent = **after explicit selection** — the signup-time `user_xxxxxxxx` placeholder is pre-selection and the `/username` page's UPDATE is the sanctioned selection write; the settings-page username field becomes **display-only**; typo/regret recovery is a support/admin path; a DB-level permanence guard is deferred until the selection flow moves server-side (documented residual: a determined user can still rename to a *valid human* name via direct PostgREST until then). (3) `seed-dev-user.ts` username `'dev'` → `'dev_user'`. Implementation: L.A1.1/040 (D49). B2 cleared.

**Q4 — username identity contract: §7.2 vs deployed reality vs spec-auth-profiles (filed per C5, 2026-07-20).** §7.2 requires `username` be **citext, 3–20 chars `[a-z0-9_]`**, and treats usernames as **changeable** ("league surfaces update live"; E52 tests a mid-season rename). Deployed reality: plain `TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL`, zero DB constraints; the only validation is a client-side regex allowing **3–30 chars, must start with a letter** (lowercased app-side at write); and `spec-auth-profiles.md` says usernames are **permanent in V1**. Three product calls needed: (a) do existing 21–30-char handles stay valid (grandfather) or get migrated? (b) citext conversion vs a `lower(username)` unique index? (c) changeable (per §7.2) or permanent (per auth spec) for v1? **Recommendation:** grandfather existing handles; enforce §7.2's charset + 3–20 length on *new/changed* usernames only (DB CHECK scoped via trigger on change); take the `lower(username)` unique index instead of a citext type migration (same case-insensitive semantics, no column rewrite); adopt §7.2's *changeable* contract — league surfaces join on `user_id` so renames are already safe, and the auth spec's "permanent" reads as a V1 simplification this epic supersedes (fold into both specs' changelogs on resolution). **M1 interim (D36, not gated on this):** invite-by-username matches via `lower(username)`; no column migration ships until you rule.
**RULED 2026-07-20 (Chris): usernames are minimum 5 characters, maximum 20, and PERMANENT (no changing after creation).** Supersedes both §7.2's 3–20/changeable contract and the deployed 3–30 client rule. No production users → no grandfathering: the DB constraint itself moves to 5–20 as part of the schema work (Builder's call on home: **folded into 040** — noted in tasks-M1 L.A1.1). Uniqueness stays case-insensitive via a `lower(username)` unique index (no citext conversion). Recorded in spec **v2.8** (§7.2 table + prose; E52 obsoleted). **Application halted same-session on Q7** (persona `*-ai` handles + the settings-page rename flow — neither surfaced by the conflict report); the ruling itself stands.

**Q5 — transactional email vendor for seat-targeted invites (filed per C6, 2026-07-20).** §7.2 makes email the **primary** invite channel ("a real email is sent with a claim link") — and the repo has **zero** outbound-email capability (no email lib, no edge functions, production SMTP commented out; only Supabase Auth's built-in mails + the local dev capture inbox). Needed from you: vendor choice, API key, and a `fieldscout.gg` sender domain (DNS records). **Recommendation:** Resend (Next.js-native, template-friendly, free tier covers beta). **M1 interim (D37, not gated on this):** the invite flow ships complete behind an `EmailSender` seam with a dev/log implementation (local capture inbox in dev), so flipping the real vendor on is config + a ~20-line adapter whenever the account exists.
**RULED 2026-07-20 (Chris): no email vendor is chosen now.** M1 builds invite email-sending behind a seam — **interface only, no vendor binding** (D37 confirmed as recommended). The v1 minimum bar, which must work regardless of vendor: **the league join link is always visible and copyable by the league manager**, so they can paste it into any email/text themselves (tasks-M1 L.A2.5 updated). Vendor selection deferred until the invite-send feature is ready to ship mail. Recorded in spec **v2.8**.

- **D339 — AUTOPILOT'S "NO MANAGER" PREDICATE READS `league_members`, NEVER `teams.status`, AND A TEAM WITH NO MEMBER ROW IS REPORTED, NEVER AUTOPILOTED.** The predicate is the exact complement of `set_lineup_internal`'s auth (`114:240-243`, under the comment that states the doctrine at `114:237`: *"AUTH, in-body (F35: league_members' cache column, never a stint)"*): `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.league_members m WHERE m.team_id = t.id AND m.user_id IS NOT NULL)`. It covers **both** unmanaged shapes with no `OR`, because they converge in that table — `add_placeholder_seat` mints `(user_id NULL, is_placeholder TRUE, team_id SET)` on a `teams` row that takes the DEFAULT status `'active'` and gets **no stint** (`063:455-464`; `team_managers.user_id` is NOT NULL by design, `053:82`), while `remove_manager`'s vacate arm sets `user_id = NULL, is_placeholder = TRUE` keeping `team_id` and only THEN sets `teams.status = 'orphaned'` (`120:645-650`, `:656-659`). **A predicate keyed on `teams.status = 'orphaned'` misses all eleven of Chris's seats.** It must also not key on `is_placeholder`, which is `BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE` with no NOT NULL (`052:69`; `052:66` is `user_id`) and so can be NULL. **The failure direction is unsafe and must be ASSERTED, not inferred:** `NOT EXISTS` is also TRUE for "this team has no `league_members` row at all", and in that case autopilot would seize a human's team. The invariant that makes it safe is stated in code, not schema (*"ONE league_members row per seat, always (§12.2)"*, `120:558`; `120:561-564` is the D301 FAAB note) while `league_members.team_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` (`052:67`). This is CLAUDE.md's "never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'" in its exact shape — a zero-row read meaning two different things — so a team with no member row is a **named, reported state**.

- **D356 — AUTOPILOT'S BUILD MECHANICS: A PURE CHOOSER + A WRITING ARM, TWO FIT PASSES, AND A PRECISELY-WORDED SILENCE (L.E1.4, migration 125 / pgTAP 073).** Six decisions a Builder had to make that D337-D340/D354 leave open, recorded so the next schema task inherits them rather than re-deriving them. **(1) THE SPLIT.** `lineup_autopilot_internal` READS and RETURNS; it never writes. The `team_lineups` UPDATE and its loud `ROW_COUNT <> 1` live in `lineup_lock_tick` arm (c), which is where §5 puts them — so there is exactly ONE writer, the `119:882-886` pattern is reused verbatim, and pgTAP can call the chooser directly for the posture cells. The chooser RAISES `P0002` when the row is absent: D354 puts materialization in the caller, under the league lock, through the unchanged carry, and an invented lineup would be the silent second row 116's banner refuses. **(2) TWO FIT PASSES, which is what makes Q63 EXACT.** One pass cannot express *"substitute only when a healthy replacement actually takes the key"*: the matcher's augmenting path will not evict an unhealthy incumbent (it re-routes him instead, and if he has nowhere to go the healthy candidate goes unplaced — the OPPOSITE of a substitution). So pass 1 offers every empty slot AND every vacated unhealthy-unlocked slot to the HEALTHY candidates only; a vacated man whose key nobody took is then RESTORED `fixed` at that key; pass 2 re-seeds pass 1's whole assignment `fixed` (`112:501-505` seeds a fixed player unconditionally, so pass 1 is reproduced exactly) and offers what is left to the unhealthy tail. Consequence, stated because it is a product-visible line: **an occupied slot is never turned into an empty one**, under either value of `allow_illegal_lineups` — item 4c's hard filter governs SEATING SOMEONE NEW, and leaving an incumbent where he already sits is the status quo, which is also the shape of `114:605-610`'s own exemption. **(3) THE NO-OP IS `slot_map` EQUALITY**, `set_lineup`'s own test (`114:633`); `starters`/`bench`/`locked_at` are projections of it and arm (b) owns the kickoff refresh of an unchanged row — which is what makes the idempotence cell honest rather than accidental. **(4) THE SHORT-CIRCUIT LIVES IN THE CHOOSER**, immediately before the first fit call, because it is the one place holding both halves of the predicate (no empty slot AND no unhealthy unlocked starter); half-duplicating it in the tick, where designations and kickoffs are not in scope, is how the two halves drift apart. **(5) FOUR COLUMNS, NOT FIVE.** `set_at` and `edited_by_commish` are deliberately NOT written: item 3 enumerates four, autopilot is a SYSTEM act (D338), and `edited_by_commish` is a user-visible badge (`team-page.tsx`) whose meaning D346 is already widening for a different reason. **(6) `no_unmanaged_seats_in_a_live_current_week`, in those words.** Arm (c)'s driving query is bounded to `lw.status = 'live'`, so "the arm saw nothing" also covers an unmanaged seat whose current week has closed into `correction_window`. A bare `no_unmanaged_seats` there is precisely the plausible-looking silence §4 rule 15 forbids, so the string says what was actually measured. Pinned by pgTAP 073 §I with a positive control at the SAME instant (ordered control-first, because the `league_weeks` transition guard permits only `upcoming → live → correction_window → final`, §12.17/F4). **(7) ADDED BY THE FIX ROUND (PR #295, R998–R1002 — amended in place, the D355 precedent: D356 does not exist on `main`, so there is no landed history to rewrite). (7a) THE KILL SWITCH'S TABLE IS HARDENED IN THE MIGRATION THAT MAKES IT A SAFETY CONTROL.** `REVOKE TRUNCATE ON TABLE system_flags FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated` is migration 125 section 0 — a grant narrowing, not DDL — because RLS does not cover TRUNCATE and the Supabase default granted it to `anon`/`authenticated` (D350's own lesson, `123:410`/`:491`), so the banner's *"a `service_role` write and nothing else"* was false as measured until this PR. No BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger: that belongs to `commissioner_actions`, where §12.12 makes immutability a LAW claim; this is operational state whose owner must stay able to truncate it in a recovery (`123:484-491`'s shape). The assertion is PER ROLE with `has_table_privilege` (073 §F1e/§F1f) — a `pg_policies` cell structurally cannot see a TRUNCATE grant, which is how the hole survived 070. Origin recorded as **F348** (122 omitted it), app-wide sweep as **F349** (64 of 67 `public` tables still grant it, 65 before this PR). **(7b) `autopilot_reason`'s ARMS ARE ORDERED AND EACH NAMES SOMETHING MEASURED.** The D339 decline gets its own value, `every_unmanaged_looking_seat_declined_no_league_members_row`; `no_row_and_no_materialize` is restricted to a seat that REACHED the materialize step and still had no row, detected by re-reading `team_lineups` after the carry returns, and its arm sits AHEAD of the `v_ap_seats = 0` arms because such a seat is `CONTINUE`d before `v_ap_seats` is incremented. Before this, the same pass that correctly REFUSED to seize a team reported either a materialization failure that never happened or *"nothing_fillable"* about seats it never evaluated — §4 rule 15's own shape in the field built to abolish it. Every emittable value now has a cell (073 §J/§K/§L), and the one that is unreachable while the carry's INSERT-or-RAISE contract holds is proven by FAULT INJECTION inside the test transaction rather than asserted as a guard that cannot fire (§4 rule 14(b)). **(7c) A DEFECT THE NEW CELL CAUGHT, AND IT WAS IN (2).** `lineup_designation_internal` returns NULL for a healthy player, `NULL IN (…)` is NULL, and the classification loop's `IF v_locked OR NOT v_unhealthy` therefore fell to its ELSE for EVERY healthy seated starter: a manager-set or carried placement was displaced and re-contested on value (a D340 violation), and because such a man also re-entered the candidate pool, the restore clause could seat him at his old key while pass 1 had placed him elsewhere — **one player written into two slots**. Both classification sites now wrap the `IN` in `COALESCE(…, FALSE)`. It was invisible to every original cell because **no fixture ran the pass over a map containing a healthy seated starter**; §J is that fixture. The general lesson for the rest of M6A: in this codebase a designation read is three-valued, so any boolean built from one and then NEGATED needs `COALESCE` — the `IF (x) IN (…) THEN` form used at `112:1051` / `114:596` / `116:520` / `123:979` is safe only because a NULL `IF` does not fire.
- **D357 — THE MATCHUP OVERRIDE'S BUILD MECHANICS: ONE INTERNAL UNDER TWO ROUTES, THE RECEIPT BEFORE THE WRITE, AND A BACKSTOP THAT BINDS THE OWNER (L.E1.5, migration 126 / pgTAP 074).** **(1) NUMBERS.** Migration head measured `125_lineup_autopilot.sql`, pgTAP head `073_lineup_autopilot.sql` (`ls … | tail -1`, D161/D166) ⇒ **126 / 074**, confirmed again at write time. **THE SPLIT SEAM WAS NOT TAKEN** — items 1–5 all fit one migration, so **131 / pgTAP 079 stay unspent** and §6's graph is unamended; **127 was never at risk**, it is L.E1.6's. **(2) ONE INTERNAL, TWO ROUTES, ONE REPLAY NAMESPACE.** `commish_matchup_override_internal(league, matchup, home, away, winner, action_id, at, reason, verb)` is PLAIN + `search_path=''` + triple-REVOKEd; `commish_edit_score` and `commish_set_result` are thin DEFINER wrappers passing `now()` and their own name. `p_verb` does three jobs — it names every refusal after the route the client actually called, it selects the `action_type` (`edit_score` / `set_result`, both already in §12.12's printed vocabulary, so **no new column**, D336), and it is itself validated so the internal cannot be driven from an unexpected caller. **The two routes SHARE `commish_matchup_actions`** (D350) because they are one verb family over one row: a retry carrying the same `action_id` must return the same document whichever route sent it, not two. **(3) THE ORDER OF THE RECEIPT AND THE WRITE IS §12.12'S, NOT 123'S, AND IT IS FORCED TWICE OVER.** D336 part (2) says the log call goes AFTER the state write. Here it cannot: the backstop refuses an `is_overridden` write with no GUC and **the GUC is a side effect of the logging helper** (`123:447`), so a verb that wrote first would be refused by its own guard; and `matchups.override_action_id` is an FK to the row the helper mints (`123:459-460`), which D341's single statement needs in hand. §12.12 prints exactly this order (`PERFORM set_config(...)` then the trigger sketch). **The load-bearing half of D336(2) is untouched:** both the log call and the write sit INSIDE `IF NOT v_no_changes THEN`, so Chris's one condition holds, and a failed UPDATE aborts the transaction and takes the audit row with it — a receipt can never outlive its change. **(4) `before`/`after` MIRROR FOUR VALUE DIMENSIONS AND `override_action_id` LIVES IN `metadata`** — because its *after* value IS the audit row's own `id`, which cannot exist before the call that consumes the document, and printing a row's primary key inside its own `after` is noise. `metadata.override_action_id_before` carries the id being replaced (NULL the first time) and 074 **E6** asserts `matchups.override_action_id = commissioner_actions.id` directly. `metadata.affected_team_ids[]` per D353, home-then-away, away omitted on a bye. **(5) THE NO-OP INCLUDES THE FLAG, AND IT MUST.** `v_no_changes` compares `home_score`, `away_score`, `result` **and `is_overridden`** by `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` — the scalar analogue of `123:1013-1018`'s jsonb equality, scale-blind on NUMERIC exactly as the write door's own comparison is (`119:653-654`), which 074 **G5** pins with `77.00` over a stored `77`. Dropping the flag from the comparison would report *the first* override of an untouched row as `no_changes` and write no receipt for a change that freezes live scoring. `override_action_id` is deliberately NOT a dimension — it is the receipt of a change, so it moves only when something else does. **(6) THE BACKSTOP'S HOT-PATH COST IS PAID IN THE `WHEN` CLAUSE.** 123 deferred this trigger because `matchups` is UPDATEd in loops by 111/116/117/119. The predicate D343 mandates sits in the trigger's `WHEN (NEW.is_overridden IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.is_overridden)`, so those loops never enter the function at all; it is **re-stated in the body** so a `prosrc` pin can see it (074 **B15**) and so the guard survives a trigger recreated without its `WHEN`. `BEFORE UPDATE` only, never INSERT: every INSERTer of `matchups` takes the column default and no client holds an INSERT policy (`109:193-194`), so guarding INSERT would buy nothing and cost every schedule generation a trigger call. **(7) D137 — `rebuild_team_week_results` HAS EXACTLY ONE BODY HUNK**, authored against `117_standings_rebuild.sql:758-891`'s FILE TEXT and never against `pg_get_functiondef`. The hunk is the first guard (`117:779-782`). The contract DOCBLOCK above it is re-stated rather than copied, because its authority bullet is the sentence this migration makes true; that is a comment, and the banner says so, so the diff is not read as a second hunk. 074 **B18** asserts every one of 117's named refusals (`week_not_final`, `matchup_not_final`, `result_drift`, `already_consistent`) survived, and **B17** that it is still one overload. **(8) THE TIE GAP IS ROUTED, NOT LEFT.** `spec:1693`'s `winner` UUID cannot express a tie. A tie IS reachable — through the score arm with equal scores, where `matchup_result_internal` derives `'tie'` — so the refusal for a winner who is not a side NAMES that route rather than leaving the commissioner to discover it. **F351** carries it to L.E1.12's copy. **(9) THREE EXISTING pgTAP SUITES AND TWO STACK SUITES CHANGED, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS THE NEW LAW ARRIVING, NOT A TEST BENT TO FIT.** 045's census is a stored literal whose own text says a migration that adds a table must move it and re-derive §C/§E's mid-state allowlists — done, and the allowlists came back UNCHANGED (`commish_matchup_actions` is unreachable from a mock: zero policies, DEFINER-only writer). 057's `is_overridden = NULL` cell reded because `NULL IS DISTINCT FROM FALSE`, so the backstop now pre-empts the NOT NULL constraint; the cell keeps D302's claim (the write is refused) ~~and **gains a `col_not_null` sibling so the constraint itself stays provable** — without it, dropping the trigger later would leave a three-valued flag with nothing red~~ **[CORRECTED in the fix round, R1009 — the sibling was a byte-equivalent duplicate of `057:76`, which has pinned `col_not_null('public','matchups','is_overridden', …)` since before this PR and already reds in exactly that case. The stated rationale was therefore factually wrong. The sibling is DROPPED and `plan(213)` reverts to `plan(212)`; the comment now points at `:76` instead of restating it. The SUBSTANCE of the 057 change stands and is stronger than it claimed: the rewritten cell pins D343's predicate as well as D302's refusal, because §12.12's printed form would let the NULL fall through to the NOT NULL constraint and restore 23502 — **measured under break probe 1, where 057 cell 103 reds alongside 074's B15/H3/H4/H10–H14**]**. 059's fixture arms the GUC around its one direct flag flip and clears it immediately so no later cell inherits it. `reconcile-db` and `score-week-worker-db` reached the overridden state through a **service-role** `UPDATE`, which the backstop now refuses — correctly: exit criterion 1 is about the OWNER and `service_role` is no different, and §12.12's own caveat is that RLS does not restrain it. A `set_config` cannot ride a PostgREST request, so both now RE-CREATE the row (the trigger is BEFORE UPDATE; INSERT is unguarded by design and 126's banner says why), with the reason in a comment naming F325/D343. **(10) Q61 SHIPPED TO ITS RECOMMENDATION WITH THE DEFAULT ON ONE LABELLED LINE** — grep `Q61 SWAP LINE`. See §3's Q61 for the exact swap and what it does not move. **(11) ADDED BY THE FIX ROUND (R1007 — amended in place, the D355/D356 precedent: D357 does not exist on `main`): AN OPEN QUESTION'S OTHER BRANCH IS CODE, SO IT GETS A TEST, WHICH MEANS THE DECISION MUST BE AN ARGUMENT AND NOT A LITERAL.** "The swap is one line" was true in PLUMBING and false in CORRECTNESS. The freeze copy was an inline `CASE` written around the shipped `v_set_over := TRUE`, and its `ELSE` silently assumed *"not frozen AND the matchup is not final ⇒ the week is final"* — true only while that literal stands. Trace the documented swap on a LIVE week with a LIVE matchup, which is the exact case Q61's other ruling exists to serve, and the verb reported **`week_final — live scoring for this week is over`** while the week was live, and the chat post (a bare `CASE WHEN v_frozen … ELSE '' END`) said **nothing at all** about the drain about to overwrite the commissioner's number — §4 rule 15's discovered consequence, hiding on the one branch no cell walked, because 074's E11/E12/J5 only ever exercised the `TRUE` arms. The remedy is **`commish_override_freeze_internal`**, a PURE `IMMUTABLE` chooser (PLAIN, `search_path=''`, triple-REVOKEd) taking `p_set_over` / `p_week_final` / `p_matchup_final` / `p_was_overridden` and returning `{frozen, why, chat_clause}` — the `lineup_autopilot_internal` pure-chooser shape (D356(1)) applied to a decision that is still Chris's. It adds a `not_frozen` arm naming the overwrite, single-sources the three texts so the receipt and the chat post cannot drift, and makes **both rulings testable today without editing the swap line** (074 §L, eleven cells, all five states plus a delegation pin so the `CASE` cannot be re-inlined). **The general rule for the rest of M6A: when a spec question's other answer is documented as a one-line swap, the branch that line does not take is unproven code — put the decision behind an argument and walk both arms, or the swap is a promise rather than a fact.** **(12) THE GUC IS NOT THE SECURITY BOUNDARY, AND BOTH THE BANNER AND THE REFUSAL NOW SAY SO (R1010).** 126's banner claimed *"the rebuild still refuses every caller who cannot also reach a `commissioner_actions` INSERT"* and the backstop raised *"…with no audit entry"*. **Neither is true as built, and it was measured:** with the 074 fixture and the owner role, `set_config('app.commish_action_id','forged-not-a-uuid',true)` then a direct `UPDATE matchups SET is_overridden = true` **moved the flag** with `override_action_id` NULL and **zero** `commissioner_actions` rows — because both guards read a string and join it to nothing. (The PR's own modified 059 fixture is the living demonstration: it sets a UUID naming no audit row and gets through.) **This is NOT a hole** — the only reachable actor is the table owner, who is already omnipotent; `authenticated` has no UPDATE policy on `matchups` at all (`109:193-194`) and no EXECUTE on the rebuild (`117:892-893`, pinned by 074 A2), and §12.12 prints the GUC-only check. But a banner that credits the wrong mechanism is how somebody later GRANTs EXECUTE on the rebuild believing the GUC would hold the door. Both texts now name the REVOKE and the missing policy as the boundary and the GUC as an **intent marker, not a credential**. **(13) A `lives_ok` OVER A ZERO-CHANGE WRITE PROVES ITS CLAIM AND EXERCISES NOTHING (R1011).** 074's H5 asserted *"a status-only UPDATE passes untouched"* against a row the fixture already inserts as `'final'`, setting it to `'final'`. The `WHEN` clause is correctly false either way, so the cell was true and hollow. H5 now aims at `d5…42` (`live` → `final`, on a week this suite never finalizes) and is bracketed by **H5a**, asserting the starting status so the transition is real, and **H5b**, asserting it landed.
- **D358 — THE ROSTER OVERRIDES' BUILD MECHANICS: ONE INTERNAL UNDER TWO VERBS, A NO-OP DEFINED BY THE REQUESTED END STATE, AND A LINE BETWEEN TIMING AND LEGALITY DRAWN GATE BY GATE (L.E1.6, migration 127 / pgTAP 075).** **(1) NUMBERS.** Migration head measured `126_commish_matchup_override.sql`, pgTAP head `074_commish_matchup_override.sql` (`ls … | tail -1`, D161/D166) ⇒ **127 / 075**, confirmed again at write time. No split seam was needed or taken. **(2) ONE INTERNAL, TWO VERBS, ONE REPLAY NAMESPACE, TWO INTERNALS TOTAL.** `commish_roster_override_internal(league, team, add, drop, player, from, to, action_id, at, reason, verb)` is PLAIN + `search_path=''` + triple-REVOKEd, and `commish_move_player` / `commish_force_add_drop` are thin DEFINER wrappers passing `now()` and their own name (126's `p_verb` shape, validated in-body so the internal cannot be driven from an unexpected caller). A SECOND internal, `commish_roster_lineup_sync_internal`, carries the lineup consequence because a MOVE runs it TWICE — once per side — and duplicating 115's interplay loop inline is how the two copies drift. **Both verbs share `commish_roster_actions`** (D350): they are one family over one league's rosters, so a retry carrying the same `action_id` must return the same document whichever route sent it. **(3) THE TWO VERBS NORMALIZE TO ONE PLAN — "this team loses a player, that team gains one" — which is what lets ONE body carry the receipt, the no-op, the chat post, the transactions row and the scoring clause.** A MOVE is an `UPDATE` of the ONE `league_rosters` row (which is why exclusivity is preserved *by construction* rather than by a check); a force add/drop is a DELETE and/or an INSERT. Everything downstream reads `v_lose_team` / `v_gain_team` / `v_lose_player` / `v_gain_player`. **(4) THE NO-OP IS "THE REQUESTED END STATE ALREADY HOLDS", AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT REACHABLE AT ALL.** D336(3) mandates a no-op detected by value, and §4 rule 14(b) forbids a cell asserting a guard that cannot execute — so the no-op had to be a state this family can actually reach. Empty arguments are NOT it: a submit that names no player is a MALFORMED call and is refused by name (126's rule). The reachable no-op is `commish_move_player` naming a player who is **already on the destination**, and `commish_force_add_drop` whose add is already on this roster and whose drop is already on none. The rejected alternative — 115's refusal, *"he is on X's roster, not Y's"* — makes a fallback verb non-idempotent in the one direction it most needs not to be: a retry under a fresh `action_id` after a network loss. A player on a THIRD team (neither source nor destination) is still refused, because there the commissioner's view is wrong in a way that matters. **(5) THE TIMING / LEGALITY LINE IS DRAWN GATE BY GATE, IN THE BANNER, UNDER STANDING RULE (i).** LIFTED, each NAMED in `bypassed[]` and each **evaluated** rather than assumed (the lock helper really runs, so the receipt names a lock that was measured closed): E32's drop and add arms, the waiver period, the acquisition caps, the manager-only auth. KEPT, each refused BY NAME with the lawful route in the message: player exclusivity, `roster_size`, a `retired` franchise (**F352**), D294's broken mirror, and the season gate (rosters do not exist before draft completion, so that one is the absence of a subject and not a timing rule). **F324's second site is this list**, recorded and not decided. **(6) A CONSEQUENCE OF D353's OWN SHAPE, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED (§4 rule 15): a commissioner force-add does not CONSUME the team's acquisition budget.** `115:497-506` counts a team's acquisitions by `initiator_team_id`, and `transactions.initiator_team_id` is NULL for a commissioner move by design (`109:243`). So the verb neither obeys the cap nor spends it, and the result says so in `caps.commissioner_move_not_counted`. **(7) THE ORDER IS D336(2)'s PLAIN ONE, not 126's inversion.** The receipt goes INSIDE the no-op guard and AFTER the state write. 126 had to invert it because the `matchups` backstop refuses a flag write with no GUC and because `override_action_id` is an FK; neither applies here — no trigger guards `league_rosters`, `league_player_pool` or `team_lineups`, and the one FK to `commissioner_actions` is the `transactions` row, which is therefore written LAST. **This verb is `transactions.related_action_id`'s FIRST writer** (the FK landed at `123:461-462` with zero rows behind it). **(8) `before`/`after` DESCRIBE THE ROW OF `target_id`, AND THE DROP SIDE OF A COMBINED CALL LIVES IN `metadata`.** §5's printed shape has room for ONE roster row; an add+drop moves two. `target_id` is the added or moved player when there is one, else the dropped one, and `metadata.drop_before` / `drop_player_id` / `drop_to_state` carry the other half. pgTAP 075 **D14** asserts `before || after` equals `after` exactly, which is what proves the two documents' KEY SETS are identical rather than merely overlapping. **(9) THE SCORING CLAUSE IS 123's, AND THE SYMMETRIC DIFFERENCE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.** The sync helper RETURNS the current-week slot it vacated, and the enqueue set is built from that — so "an added player lands on the bench and is therefore never in the difference" is a fact the code reads back, not a comment. Stamp, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, `score_enqueued` / `score_not_enqueued` / `score_stale` / `score_stale_reason` are 123's verbatim, and all three arms are walked (075 §C, §D, §H). **`edited_by_commish` is written on EVERY lineup row the verb changes and `set_at` on none** — the D356(5) four-not-five posture: nobody SET this lineup, a roster move changed it underneath. **(10) F350 IS RE-ROUTED, MEASURED OUT OF ITS OWN ROUTING.** It was routed here because `commish_move_player` was expected to seed fixed placements into `lineup_fit_internal`. It does not call the matcher at all (075 **I3** asserts zero `prosrc` hits), because a roster move is not a re-fit — it copies 115's interplay loop, which removes a key by name and appends to the bench behind a `NOT (bench ? p_add)` guard, so the map it writes is always the stored map MINUS one key. The verb carries its own site-local duplicate assertion anyway (the added player in NO `slot_map` value and EXACTLY ONCE on the bench, on every row it touched), because a duplicate written HERE would double-count in `startersOf`. The matcher still has no guard; its three callers still rely on their own COALESCE discipline (D356(7c)); no remaining M6A task adds or replaces a caller, so the owner is the next migration that does (M5's trade verbs). **(11) A THIRD SCORING HALF D346 DID NOT HAVE, FOUND BY THE STACK TEST AND NOT BY READING (F353).** The worker maps a queued player to LEAGUES through `league_rosters`; `commish_edit_lineup` never meets that because its benched player stays rostered, but a force-DROP deletes the row, so the queue row the verb writes for the dropped man maps to nothing and the drain never arrives. Measured: the first cut reded with `report.leagues: []` on the drain after the drop while the identical drain before it reported the league `written`. So 127 queues a changed starter only if the league still rosters him (naming the rest `unrostered`), ALSO queues a REACH SET of players the league still rosters so the drain ARRIVES, and then MEASURES reachability with the worker's own predicate — `score_reach_enqueued[]` / `score_reachable` on the receipt, `score_stale_reason = 'unreachable'` when the answer is no. **The general rule for the rest of this family: an enqueue is only a signal if the queued player is still reachable from the thing you want recomputed. Any future verb that REMOVES a player and expects a re-score inherits this.** **(12) ADDED BY THE FIX ROUND (R1016–R1023), because four of the eight findings are mechanics the next verb in this family repeats. (a) **TWO ENQUEUE SITES NEED TWO CELLS.** 127 writes `score_fanout` twice (the symmetric difference and the reach set) and the first cut pinned only the second, so a probe on either one reded the same cell and attributed nothing. A verb with N insert sites owes N independent pins and at least one cell that SHOWS the other site was empty at that call. (b) **A VERB'S `action_type` DESCRIBES THE PLAN THAT EXECUTED, NEVER THE PARAMETERS THAT ARRIVED** — the normalized plan is the only honest source once any arm can be a no-op; the sole exception is a TOTAL no-op, where nothing executed and the document's job is to report the request. (c) **`action_id` IS A SHARED NAMESPACE**: `uniq_transactions_league_action` spans every verb that writes a `transactions` row, so any new writer owes the R732 check in its own direction or it ships a 500. (d) **AN IR SPOT IS NOT A STARTING SLOT**, and the predicate to use is the scoring worker's (`startersOf`/`irKeysOf`, prefix-split on `':'`), not 123's whole-instance-key form, whenever the field exists to predict what the worker will do.
- **D359 — THE TEAM-RENAME VERBS' BUILD MECHANICS: TWO DOORS OVER ONE NAME GATE, AN AUTHORITY GAP SAID OUT LOUD, AND A GUARD DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN (L.E1.7, migration 128 / pgTAP 076).** **(1) NUMBERS.** Migration head measured `127_commish_roster_moves.sql`, pgTAP head `075_commish_roster_moves.sql` (`ls … | tail -1`, D161/D166) ⇒ **128 / 076**, confirmed at write time. No seam needed or taken; **129 / 077** is next free. **(2) 128 REPLACES NOTHING — ZERO D137 HUNKS, and the banner states that rather than leaving it to be inferred.** Six new objects, no `CREATE OR REPLACE` against another migration's file text, so there is no decoy head to get wrong. This is the first M6A schema task with no provenance risk at all, and saying so is cheaper than a reviewer re-deriving it. **(3) TWO DOORS, ONE SHARED NAME GATE.** `team_rename_normalize_internal(name, verb)` is the single place the bound (`z.string().trim().min(1).max(100)`, the league-rename bound) and the EXPLICIT `E' \t\r\n'` trim class live, so the commissioner's verb and the manager's cannot drift on what counts as a name. Plain `btrim` strips SPACES ONLY (R745, fixed twice already at `112:756` / `114:315`) — a naive `NULLIF(btrim(x), '')` ships a franchise called `E'\t'`. **(4) THE COMMISSIONER'S HALF IS 123's TEMPLATE UNCHANGED** (D336's seven parts, mapped line by line in the banner): its own zero-policy `commish_team_actions` ledger with `REVOKE TRUNCATE`; ONE audit row through the shared helper, inside the no-op guard and after the state write, with `IF v_audit_id IS NULL RAISE`; the no-op detected by value over the ONE dimension the verb can change; the in-txn non-disableable chat post; PLAIN internal + DEFINER wrapper; the three-layer reason gate; and a result that names what did and did not follow. **(5) THE MANAGER'S HALF CARRIES NONE OF IT, AND REPORTS EACH ABSENCE AS A FIELD** — `audited: false` + `audited_why`, `system_post: null` + `system_post_why`. No reason (he is not exercising a §10.1 power), no audit row, no chat post (§10.3's post is for OVERRIDE messages; auto-posting an ordinary manager action would be new product), and **no `action_id` and no ledger**, because setting a name to a value is idempotent by construction and the verb has no second effect to dedupe. **A STANDALONE TEAM IS ROUTED, NOT HANDLED TWICE**: `league_id IS NULL` already has a working door (`095:636-639`'s UPDATE policy, proven live by 076 **C3**), so the verb refuses by name and says which one rather than becoming a second writer for a surface that is not broken. **(6) ~~A GUARD DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN, AND THE MECHANISM ASSERTED IN ITS PLACE (§4 rule 14(b) / D267).~~ RETRACTED 2026-09-14 (R1029) — THE GUARD IS WRITTEN, AND THE LESSON IS THE OPPOSITE ONE.** ~~`rename_own_team` has no `retired` refusal: `120:540` is the only writer of `status='retired'` in the whole chain and the same arm re-points the seat's `league_members` row at the SUCCESSOR with `user_id = NULL` (`120:565-570`), so the auth predicate structurally excludes a sealed franchise and a guard placed after it could never execute — nor be proven without a fixture the product cannot produce. 076 B1 asserts the premise and F7 asserts the mechanism, so a future migration that leaves a seated row on a sealed franchise turns that cell red. The general rule: when a guard is unreachable, assert the thing that makes it unreachable — never ship a guard no cell can fire.~~ **THE CORRECTION:** the exclusion was an INVARIANT maintained by three other verbs' guards (`create_league_invite` `062:378`, `claim_league_invite` `062:865`, `assign_manager` `063:688`), not a structure — `seat_league_member_internal`'s fallback at `077:428-437` INSERTs a `league_members` row for whatever team id it is handed, and none of the three guards was pinned by 076. F7's fixture omitted the seated row BY HAND, so it asserted its own premise and could never have noticed drift. The Reviewer produced the state in a rolled-back transaction and renamed a sealed franchise through the manager door (`Unsealed By Manager | retired`). Rule 14(b)/D267 is about a guard an outer condition IN THE SAME FUNCTION has excluded; a guard kept out by remote verbs is a different species and IS provable — so `rename_own_team_internal` step **(3b)** now refuses `retired` by name with the commissioner arm's F354-naming message shape, and 076 **F10/F11/F12** prove it on exactly the Reviewer's fixture (a `retired` team seated by a real user). **The general rule, corrected: "structurally unreachable" means excluded by THIS function's own earlier gate; anything else is an invariant somebody else maintains, and the guard goes in.** Break probe: the guard removed ⇒ F11 *"no exception thrown"*, F12 *"have: Unsealed By Manager"*, 90/92 otherwise green; restored, `diff` empty. **AND THE GUARD READS THE LOCKED ROW (R1036/R1037, the second fix round, 2026-09-15 — by Chris's ruling, see the findings block): the R1029 guard was placed at the old step (3b), evaluated on step (1)'s UNLOCKED select BEFORE the `FOR UPDATE` re-read, so a retire committed while the rename waited on the league lock was invisible to it — the manager door renamed a franchise sealed 4.5 s earlier (`Raced Past The Seal | retired`). The commissioner arm was never exposed (its guard at step 6 already read its locked re-read at step 5). Now the manager arm locks league → team, re-reads, and THEN evaluates auth (step 4) and the retired guard (step 5) against the locked state — the commissioner arm's shape; 076 F13/F14 pin both orders as `prosrc` positions. - **D364 — THE PART-2 ROUTES' BUILD MECHANICS: ONE MODULE PER LEDGER, A VALUE DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT OF ONE GUARD, AND AN OPAQUE COMPOSITE CURSOR (L.E1.11, no migration).** **(1) NUMBERS.** No migration, no pgTAP, no typegen — heads stay 131 / 079; action-id prefix **`b03`** measured free (grep over `src/`, `supabase/tests/`, `e2e/`: af0–aff, b00–b02, b05 taken). **(2) THREE MODULES, NOT ONE — the D362(2) rule applied in the other direction.** D362 made two modules of four verbs because each PAIR shared a replay ledger; 128, 129 and 130 each own their own ledger (`commish_team_actions`, `commish_setting_actions`, `commish_schedule_actions`), so the unit is the verb and there is no cross-door replay class to guard — each guard still compares `verb`, cheaply, so a future sibling door cannot re-open it. **(3) THE SETTING GUARD OMITS THE VALUE, ON PURPOSE AND ON MEASUREMENT.** 129's document echoes `key` and `rescore_requested` as sent but `requested_value` as `v_canon` (`129:1076`): `"72"` for an integer key comes back `72`, R1040's `roster_settings` canonicaliser strips unknown keys, and jsonb re-orders object keys. The source object is ALSO kept verbatim in `raw_stats` (provenance, and the fields the canonical map does not carry — F386); its `pts_*` are the source's preset totals and nothing may read them as a league value. **(3) THE ENDPOINT, MEASURED 2026-09-27 (the fixture `src/lib/sync/fixtures/sleeper-weekly-projections-2026.json`, `_note`).** `GET https://api.sleeper.com/projections/nfl/{season}/{week}?season_type=regular&position[]={POS}` — the season URL plus `/{week}`. Past the last week's `correction_window_ends_at` the plan is EMPTY WITH A NAMED REASON (`seasonComplete`, the one empty plan that is not a failure); an empty calendar, an explicit week the calendar lacks, or an empty `players` table is a FAILURE by name. **(5) THE WRITE (service role).** Upsert in chunks of 500 with `count: 'exact'`, the count asserted equal to the chunk (a short write throws — never "done"); then the week's lines the fresh fetch no longer carries are deleted (a player ruled out drops to filler — a stale line would outrank him), read through `pageAll` with an exact count (the 1000-row cap — the stack cell plants 1,200) and deleted in count-asserted chunks of 200. Unknown source ids are COUNTED and NAMED in a warning (id, name, position, team), never silently dropped; duplicates counted (first kept). `fetched_at` is the TimeProvider instant (the column has NO default by design — 084 A9/B6). What status changes is *stated*, not refused: `reseed_can_overwrite` + `reseed_why` say that in `setup` / `scheduled` a budget change or seat fill re-seeds the seat, and in `drafting` a draft reset does. (2) **Validity binds him** (rule (i)): negative refused by name (22023), 145's CHECK behind it (probe: the gate removed ⇒ 23514). No upper bound but INTEGER (task text: above the budget allowed). (3) **The subject is the seat** (`league_members`, UNIQUE per team): no seat row ⇒ refused by name, nothing minted; a retired franchise ⇒ refused naming its successor (its seat moved there, 120). (4) **The receipt is public** because the balance is (league_members is member-readable; only bids are blind): audit `edit_faab` / `team` / `{faab_balance}` before-after, `acting_as_team_id` NULL (an override, not acting as the manager — the 139 shape); chat post and notification carry the amounts; the actor is never notified of his own act, an open seat notifies nobody. (6) **F412:** `draft_reset` (newest definer 100:2314; 3 hunks) re-seeds every seat whose balance differs from the CURRENT budget when the league returns to `scheduled` and reports `faab_reseeded_seats`; its chat post is byte-identical. A commissioner edit made during `drafting` is therefore undone by a reset — the pre-draft rule, stated in the edit's own result.
