- **D386 — L.D3.2 AS BUILT (migration 148): WHO MOVES A TRADE, WHAT "FITS" MEANS, AND WHAT WAITS FOR L.D3.3.** (1) **Visibility is the spec's:** `trades` / `trade_items` / `trade_drops` are readable by every league member (§12.11's own policies — only waiver bids are blind); no write policy for any role; the ledger `trade_actions` has zero policies. (2) **Whose move:** accept, reject and counter are the RECEIVING team's; cancel is the PROPOSING team's. The other party asking for the wrong move gets a by-name P0001 naming his own move; anyone else a no-leak 42501. A commissioner / co-commissioner may make either side's move (TD5) and writes ONE `commissioner_actions` row (`propose_trade` / `accept_trade` / `reject_trade` / `cancel_trade` / `counter_trade`, target the trade, `acting_as_team_id` = that side) + the §10.3 post + that team's manager's notification; validity (exclusivity, E36, FAAB) binds him. (3) **Only a `proposed` trade can be answered** — a second accept is refused by name, never a silent no-op (its drops would be dropped on the floor); an accepted trade is not cancellable here (review / veto are L.D3.3 / L.D3.5). (4) **Counter** = the offer is rejected with reason "countered by <team>" and a new proposal the other way is created, `countered_from` linking them. (5) **E36 "fits"** = roster count − players out + players in − drops ≤ roster_size (starting slots + bench + IR — 115's formula). The proposer is enforced at proposal; the receiving team's overflow is REPORTED at proposal (`must_drop`) and ENFORCED at acceptance, when it names its drops; a drop must be the team's own, named once, and not already leaving in the trade. Acceptance re-validates everything under the league lock. (6) **FAAB legs** need `allow_faab_in_trades` AND a FAAB league, one amount per giving team, ≤ the giver's current balance — checked, never moved (execution is L.D3.3's). (7) **A one-sided trade** needs `allow_future_considerations` (§7.3.5's "notes-only gentleman's trades" — the consideration lives in the optional note). (8) **E37:** `AFTER DELETE` and `AFTER UPDATE OF team_id` on `league_rosters` mark every in-flight trade (`proposed` / `accepted` / `in_review`) that names that player leaving that team — as a leg OR as one of its drops — `invalid` with a sentence naming the player, the team and how he left, and notify BOTH managers (the actor included). SECURITY DEFINER, `ENABLE ALWAYS` (R616), time = the transaction's `now()` (a trigger has no `p_at`; it is the same instant the verb's door passed). The trade being executed is exempt through `app.executing_trade_id` (F413). (9) **Deliberately NOT here — L.D3.3's (Q75 / Q76 as ruled):** the game-day lock, the deadline, review, execution, E47's rescind. Until it lands a proposal or acceptance naming a kicked-off player, or made after the deadline week, is accepted — nothing moves until execution, which L.D3.3 gates. (10) Broadcast: `trades` INSERT / status change on `league:<id>` (event `trades`), never `action_id`, `*_by` or the note. (11) The commissioner's trade receipts render in League Home activity through the generic line ("accept trade (acting for Bravo)") until L.D3.7 gives them words.
- **D387 — L.D2.12 AS BUILT (no migration): THE WAIVER ROUTES, THE FAAB ROUTE, THE READS.** (1) **Reorder is "move this claim to place N"** — `PATCH …/waivers/[cid]` `{claim_order}`: the service reads the team's pending order under RLS, moves [cid], and hands 145 the WHOLE list, so 145's exact-set check still refuses by name when the set changed; a claim the caller cannot see is 145's no-leak 403; a settled one a 409 by name. The F65(b) guard checks [cid] sits at the asked place in the echo. (2) **The blind read (E13):** `GET …/waivers` defaults to the caller's OWN team (`?team_id=` for the commissioner) and `?status=pending|all`; a member naming ANOTHER team is a 403 by name, never RLS's empty list (break probe: the guard removed ⇒ 200 with an empty list, the stack cell red). (3) **A non-member is the family's 403, not a 404** — the task text says "non-member 404", but tasks-M5 §5 routes these through `inseason-errors.ts` and R807 ruled one posture for the in-season family (`assertLeagueMember`: 403 for a non-member and a nonexistent league alike, 404 only for a member's soft-deleted league). House mechanics, not product — read as a slip in the task text. (4) **R1172:** `balance` and `faab_bid` accept whole numbers 0–2147483647 (Postgres INTEGER); no lower cap, above-budget allowed; one past is a clean 400. (5) **The edit (D383(2))** is three calls — cancel, resubmit, move back — sequenced by `runWaiverClaimEdit` with five ids minted once per gesture; a refused resubmit puts the original back and says so, a refused restore is SAID ("your old claim was cancelled…"), a refused move-back reports the edit made but last. Not one transaction — F417. (6) **Only reorder is optimistic** (tasks-M5 §5; CLAUDE.md list reordering) with snapshot rollback; submit / cancel / edit / FAAB are not; every hook `retry: false`, one `action_id` per gesture. (7) **Reads:** `faab_balance` + `waiver_priority` on each rosters team, each standings row (joined from `league_members` after the RPC gates membership) and each league-detail member — public to members (only bids are blind, D385(4)). (8) **Feed:** a won `waiver_claim` row renders "claimed X off waivers for $N, dropped Y" from 113's `add`/`drop` shape when present, else "a player" — the processor's payload is F416.
- **D388 — L.D2.7 AS BUILT (migration 149): THE WAIVER SCHEDULE, EXACTLY.** (1) **Presets:** the catalog default stays Wednesday 03:00 Eastern (D60's instant); Chris's league 1 = Tue–Sat 09:00 Pacific, free agency from Sunday 06:00 Pacific; league 2 = one run **Wednesday 00:00 Pacific** — "Tuesday at midnight" read as the END of Tuesday, his own idiom ("midnight PST Monday" for the Monday-night release); a preset is editable. (2) **The week's end** for the window = the later of the latest `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at` and the league's draft completing; L.D2.10 adds the Wednesday ceiling (F424). A run AT that end counts (Q78); a weekday opening AT it opens nothing. (3) **A run counts only once settled** when the processor tracks the league (`waiver_next_run_at` set) — no instant add beats the claims a due run is settling (E8); NULL = untracked, the schedule alone decides, so nothing freezes before L.D2.9 (F423). (4) **Pre-season reading:** with no week end yet, a passed weekday opening after the first post-draft run stays open until week 1's last game ends (the ruling's "until the week's last game ends"). (5) **DST:** wall-clock in the league's zone through Postgres `AT TIME ZONE`; the TS twin reproduces its rule (a nonexistent time reads with the pre-jump offset, a repeated one as the later instant), pinned to the same literals in both. (6) **Commissioner:** force add/drop walks past the window and a hold (timing rules, TD5), named `waiver_period:<player>`; a force drop waits for the next run (it would otherwise have read the retired key's 48h default). (7) The settings panel's four retired rows became one preset select + the schedule in words; the full editor is L.D2.13 (F425). **(8) Deploy before push (R1187, fix round).** Merging deploys main to Vercel at once; the hosted database gets 149 only at Chris's `db push`. So the READER tolerates both shapes: `mergeSettings` first runs `waiverScheduleFromLegacy` — the TS twin of 149's `waiver_schedule_from_legacy_internal`, key by key (a new key wins; the old tue/wed/thu day and HH:MM time carry over, read in America/New_York; free agency after the run; else the catalog default; the five retired keys stripped) — so a pre-149 league renders the schedule 149 will write, not a 500; on a post-149 row it is the identity. Pinned as the same stored literals in `split-merge.test.ts` and pgTAP 097 A4a/A4b. Write and validation paths stay strict (a new write naming a retired key is still refused). **The code is backward-compatible with a pre-149 database — Chris should still push 135–149 promptly:** until he does, the pre-149 add path still reads the retired keys (48h hold, no window), and a settings save replaces the whole blob (118's `update_league_settings` writes `settings = p_settings`) with the new keys — the pre-149 SQL then reads the retired keys' defaults (48h, `immediate_after_waivers`, `bench_lock` on), and 149's mapping keeps the saved schedule (a new key wins). **(9) Existing leagues keep their exact day and time, in Eastern (R1191):** a default league lands exactly on the Wednesday 03:00 Eastern preset; a Tuesday or Thursday league (or any non-03:00 time) keeps that day/time and shows as "custom". A deviation from v2.16.58's "migrates to the nearest preset" wording (TD14/D403) — recorded, not ruled; the spec's v2.16.59 row already says "keeping its day and time".
- **D389 — L.D2.8 AS BUILT: THE REFERENCE WAIVER RESOLVER (`src/lib/leagues/waivers/resolve-waiver-run.ts`; pure TS, no migration).** (1) **Contract.** In: settings (waiver type, FAAB tiebreaker, roster size as 115 counts it, caps), teams (roster, balance, acquisitions used, retired), pending claims (bid, `claim_order`), Q72's priority sources (round-1 draft order; standings, null until week 1 is final; stored rolling priority, null until seeded) and the set of players LOCKED at the run instant — locks are inputs the caller computes at its `p_at`, so no clock is read. Out: every claim once, in decision order — `won` / `lost` / `invalid`, reason, FAAB spent, `deadlockBreak`; per team balance before/after, roster after, acquisitions after; priority before/after, its source, whether it rotates. Input array order never matters; ids compare as code-unit strings (SQL: `COLLATE "C"`); `serializeWaiverRunResult` is the byte form L.D2.9's parity test compares. Bad input (a player on two rosters, a priority list that is not exactly the active teams, a FAAB claim with no balance on record, `none_fcfs`) throws by name. (2) **The rules (Q71).** A player goes to the highest bid, then the better priority position — the claim's PRIORITY KEY, (7); a team with two claims on one player wins through its highest-ranked claim that still beats the best other team. Turns run highest bid first across players. A claim is awarded only when it stays valid however its team's higher-ranked pending claims turn out (budget, room, a shared drop, caps — counted as if they all won), so the team's ranking settles its running out, and money is held back for a higher claim only while that claim can still win. (3) **`reverse_standings` does not rotate within a run** — §13.2's "winner drops to the back (rolling) or order resets by reverse standings" (and E7) are ambiguous on whether a team moves after a win inside one run; built reading "the order is the reverse standings for the whole run": the last-place team keeps first priority for the whole run. Rolling (the waiver type, or FAAB with the rolling tiebreaker) moves each winner to the back at once (for its lower-ranked claims — (7)). Open for Chris — F422(a). (4) **The cycle.** When every contested player's top claim waits on its own team's outbid higher-ranked claim (A: #1 X $10, #2 Y $50; B: #1 Y $10, #2 X $50; $50 budgets), the run awards the strongest — both $50 bids win — per Q71's "the highest bid ALWAYS wins him": it takes the strongest top overall and awards that team's HIGHEST-RANKED top claim, not the strongest top itself (R1178's worked example pins the difference). Open for Chris — F422(b). (5) **Reasons** (`waiver_claims.result_reason`): `lost` = `outbid` / `lost_on_priority` (another team's claim won him this run); `invalid` = `team_retired`, `add_rostered`, `add_locked` (Q74), `drop_gone`, `drop_locked` (Q73 — no `bench_lock` input, no off position), `roster_full`, `cap_reached`, `insufficient_faab` (checked in that order — the resolver runs its checks by iterating `FAIL_CHECK_ORDER`, the one list, pinned as a literal; R1177), `own_claim_won`. A claim that does not go through spends nothing; a priority league spends nothing (a stray bid is ignored); `faab_min_bid` is not re-checked at the run (submit's rule, 145). (6) **Proofs:** 27 worked examples as stored literals (the cycle's full byte form pinned) + 11 fast-check properties at 1,000 seeded runs (also clean at 3 × 20,000 on other seeds) + a coverage cell that fails if any rule is never reached; break probes — budget reservation removed, balance check removed, tiebreak reversed — each red, reverted. *Fix round (R1176–R1180):* 32 worked examples + 13 properties + coverage (46 cells), clean at 20,000 runs on seeds 1, 2, 4 and 20260928; five mutation probes red → reverted. (7) **R1176 — RULED on Q71 (orchestrator, 2026-09-28, applying the Q71 text Chris approved: "a team's ranking only settles its own collisions"): a team's lower-ranked win never costs it a higher-ranked claim on the tiebreak.** Built as a per-claim PRIORITY KEY: the team's run-start place, or — in a rotating league — its latest win on a claim it ranked ABOVE this one (a win sends it to the back only for the claims it ranked below the one it won). Reviewer's case (rolling tiebreaker; A priority 1; A #1 P $10 tied with B, #2 Q $30): was `a2 won, b1 won, a1 lost_on_priority`; now `a2 won $30, a1 won $10, b1 lost_on_priority` — Q is still decided first (the bigger bid), P is judged with A still at priority 1. `priority.after` (the next run's order) is unchanged in form — every winner to the back, by last win. Plain rolling-priority leagues and every earlier worked example are unchanged. A first attempt ("a claim waits while a higher-ranked claim of its team is tied") was dropped: its waits can deadlock, and the deadlock break then moved the team anyway — a targeted 1,000,000-run hunt found 253 such losses; the key version: 0 in 2 × 1,000,000.

**2026-09-28 — L.D2.4 (docs only): the M5 breakdown's design decisions TD1–TD16, transcribed as D390–D405** (`tasks-M5-transactions.md` §3, approved by Chris 2026-09-27, PR #323). Short form; the breakdown has the full text. D388 is left to L.D2.7 (building in parallel).
- **D390 — TD1.** Two lanes, ONE schema lane: waivers and trades share `transactions`, the pool, the lineup interplay and the league-row lock; migrations serialize in merge order (TS/UI tasks may run in parallel).
- **D391 — TD2.** FAAB stays on `league_members.faab_balance` (one row per seat, carried with it) with `CHECK (faab_balance IS NULL OR faab_balance >= 0)`; no ledger table — every change writes `faab_before` / `faab_after` on its receipt, and balance at draft start − won bids ± trade legs + commissioner deltas = balance now.
- **D392 — TD3.** Blind means blind after processing too: only a WON claim writes a (member-visible) `transactions` row; lost / invalid / cancelled outcomes live on `waiver_claims` (owner + commissioners) and the owner's notification; no broadcast on `waiver_claims`.
- **D393 — TD4.** `waiver_claims`, `trades`, `trade_items` and votes are written through RPCs only — SELECT policies keyed on membership truth (`league_members.team_id`), no write policy (C73, the F18 precedent).
- **D394 — TD5.** The commissioner can make any manager move for any team (submit / cancel / reorder claims; propose / respond / vote): one `commissioner_actions` row with `acting_as_team_id`, reason optional; validity rules bind him, timing rules do not.
- **D395 — TD6.** The waiver processor is in-database: `waiver_tick(p_now)` on pg_cron every minute claims due leagues (`waiver_next_run_at ≤ p_now`) with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and runs `process_waivers_internal(league, p_at)` per league, league row locked first; a `waivers_paused` `system_flags` kill switch (C78).
- **D396 — TD7.** One reference resolver, two implementations: the pure TS `resolveWaiverRun` (fast-check properties) states the rules once and the SQL processor is proven equal to it on random claim sets (built, D389).
- **D397 — TD8.** Waiver priority lives on the seat (`league_members.waiver_priority`, 1 = first), seeded at the first run from Q72's order; `reverse_standings` reads `league_standings` at run time, so a stat correction (E44) moves the next run's order.
- **D398 — TD9.** A won claim's `transactions` row: `type = 'waiver_claim'`, `status = 'complete'`, `payload.add_player_id` / `drop_player_id` (115's caps count it), `faab_bid`, `faab_before/after`, `claim_id`, `run_at`, `week`. A trade's payload carries NO `add_player_id`, so trades never count against caps.
- **D399 — TD10.** Traded and claimed players land on the bench; dropped / traded-away players leave every `team_lineups.slot_map` from the current week on (115's interplay, copied). No M5 verb calls `lineup_fit_internal`, so F350 stays unowned.
- **D400 — TD11.** Trades obey the add/drop game-day lock (Q34(B)); `trade_lock_behavior = defer` waits until the week's last game ends for ALL players together, `reject` fails by name (Q75, C76).
- **D401 — TD12.** E37 is trigger-driven (an `AFTER DELETE OR UPDATE OF team_id` trigger on `league_rosters` marks a pending trade `invalid` and notifies both managers); `trade_tick` re-validates the rest each minute and execution re-validates once more (built, D386(8); F413).
- **D402 — TD13.** Drops for uneven trades are part of the trade (E36): the proposer names his at proposal, the recipient at acceptance; they execute atomically with the swap and follow the waiver schedule like any drop.
- **D403 — TD14.** The waiver schedule (F229): waiver runs at set local times + free-agency windows of instant pickups, claim-only outside them, drops on waivers until the next run, all in the league's own IANA zone; Chris's two leagues are presets; the old four keys migrate to the nearest preset. RULED as Q70; folded v2.16.58; built by L.D2.7.
- **D404 — TD15.** The Wednesday 00:00 PT week ceiling releases LOCKS only — a sibling read to `release-floor.ts`, never a stamp on `last_game_ends_at` (which still drives week advance and scoring). RULED as Q78; built by L.D2.10.
- **D405 — TD16.** Notifications are in-app `notifications` rows written in the verb's transaction (claim won / lost / failed to the owner; trade proposed / accepted / vetoed / executed / invalid / expired to both managers; commissioner acts to that manager); executed trades and commissioner acts also post the §10.3 `league_chat` line.
- **D406 — L.D2.9 AS BUILT (migration 150): THE WAIVER RUN, EXACTLY.** (1) **F422 in the resolver (re-cut first, its own commit).** A run awards, again and again, the strongest pending claim that can go through — effective bid DESC, the team's place in the CURRENT order, its `claim_order`, claim id — and sends the winner to the back at once (F422(a), every waiver type and the FAAB tie). Under F422(b) that same order ranks a team's own claims (biggest bid first, its order only between equal bids), so a team's claims are never decided out of its ranking and no cycle can form: L.D2.8's readiness check, R1176's per-claim key (D389(7)) and the deadlock break are gone (`deadlockBreak` dropped from the output), and F422(c) is moot (pinned: the bid-size case, A wins exactly one tie). `priority.rotates` → `persists` (only rolling / the FAAB rolling tiebreak store the order); `after` is the rolled order in every type. (2) **The SQL twin** `waiver_resolve_run_internal(jsonb)` is pure (TS-shaped input / output, the TS error text on bad input); the processor gathers its input, calls it, applies its answer and asserts the tables equal it. (3) **F421 as built:** (a) the locked set = claim players whose NFL team `pool_game_lock_any_internal` locks at p_at; (b) every franchise is passed, retired ones flagged (their claims fail `team_retired`); the draft order is `drafts.draft_order` (098's draft_start resolves it for every draft type, the auction included) mapped through `successor_team_id` to the live franchise; standings only for an order that does not persist and only once a week is final (`weeks_final > 0`); the rolling map = the seats' `waiver_priority`, NULL until the first run seeds it; (c) `COLLATE "C"`, FAIL_CHECK_ORDER mirrored; (d) `priority.after` written 1-based when it persists; (e) **DECIDED: claims left pending under `none_fcfs` close `invalid` / `no_waivers`** (nothing spent, owner told, the pending run cleared) — they can never be settled and the player is now an instant pickup; (f) the parity suite maps both answers into one `WaiverRunResult`; (g) a league whose run raises rolls back ALONE in its own subtransaction (claims pending, no FAAB moved, run not advanced), is named in the tick's report and in `waiver_runs` (`refused`, attempts counted, retried each minute); (h) the priority key is the team's place in the rolled order. (4) **When:** the tick runs every minute; a run settles at the tick's instant (locks read then; `waiver_claims.process_at` = the scheduled run it settled); F423 — a NULL league is seeded with the next run after the tick and nothing is decided; a settled league advances to the next run after p_at; `draft_reset` clears it; a second settle of one run is refused by the `waiver_runs` UNIQUE (exactly once). `system_flags.waivers_paused` stops every run and seed and says so. (5) **F407:** submit refuses a kicked-off add with the pickup lock's own words (verb prefix aside); it needs the league calendar, so a league with no `league_weeks` is refused by name like add/drop (093, `waiver-claims-db`, `waivers-api-db` re-cut: calendar pinned / weeks added). (6) **F422(b) and the stored order — both halves, neither alone works:** submit and edit keep a FAAB team's order bid-sorted (stable within a bid) and reorder refuses a smaller bid above a bigger one by name; deriving alone would silently overrule a drag, refusing alone would leave submit appending a $50 claim below a $10 one and L.D2.12's move route building lists the verb refuses (093 D6 / F13 and `waivers-api-db`'s bids re-cut to equal bids). Pending FAAB claims renumbered once. (7) **F417:** `waiver_claim_edit` SETS bid and drop in one transaction (145's template, own verb in the replay namespace); `PATCH …/waivers/[cid]` is a move when the body has `claim_order`, else an edit; `useEditClaim` is one call; the three-call `waiver-claim-edit.ts` is deleted. (8) **F408 / F411:** a retired team's claim reports to its successor's manager; vacate and leave cancel the team's pending claims (`seat_vacated` / `manager_left`) — their results stay 063's seven keys (068 I1/I3 pin them); the record is on the claim rows. (9) **F416:** a won claim's `transactions` row carries 113's `add` / `drop` objects; `faab_before/after` only in FAAB (the feed shows no price for a priority league); the League Home sentence over that exact payload is pinned in `activity-feed-ops.test.ts` and the real rows' names in the parity suite. (10) Measured: 12 teams × 10 claims (40 won / 69 lost / 11 invalid) settle in ≈ 49 ms under the league lock — 0.41 ms per claim against the 50 ms budget. (11) Deploy before push: nothing in the app calls the new RPC until L.D2.13 builds the claims panel, and production lacks the whole waiver chain (145+) until Chris pushes — no live surface can break.
- **D410 — L.D3.3 AS BUILT (migration 151): HOW A TRADE GOES THROUGH.** *(Numbered D410 / F435–F438 / spec v2.16.61 to leave D406–D409, F431–F434 and v2.16.60 to L.D2.9, building in parallel.)* (1) **Review:** `none` ⇒ `accepted` and executed inside the accept's own transaction (a lock wait or a failure is in the accept's answer); `commissioner` / `league_vote` ⇒ `in_review` with `review_deadline` = acceptance + `trade_review_period_hours` (24); the tick auto-approves AT the deadline (inclusive; 0 hours ⇒ the next tick). Approve / veto are L.D3.5's (F436); until L.D3.4 a league-vote trade goes through at its deadline with no veto (F435). (2) **Deadline (Q76, D288):** week N+1's `nfl_weeks.starts_at`; propose / accept / counter refused AT and after it, by name, the instant in the league's zone; reject / cancel stay open; the tick expires every offer still `proposed` (both told); `accepted` / `in_review` finish. No `trade_deadline_week` ⇒ none; N+1 past the calendar's last week ⇒ no instant; a calendar GAP refuses loudly. (3) **Lock (Q75 / E35):** a leg OR a drop inside §13.1's game-day lock locks the whole trade; `defer` parks it `accepted` with `execute_after` = the latest release (`infinity` while a week's end is unrecorded — re-read every minute), both told once; `reject` ⇒ `invalid` naming the players. (4) **The executor** is F413's list: league row first, trade re-read and required in flight, `trade_check_internal` with both teams' drops enforced, retired / out-of-season refused; a business refusal ⇒ `invalid` + reason + both told; a broken invariant raises and rolls back. Swap = `UPDATE league_rosters SET team_id` (the player never leaves the league); drops follow 149's destination (fa_hold / none_fcfs / waivers until the next run); FAAB debit + credit, each one row; `complete` in the same transaction; ONE `transactions` row (`type='trade'`, initiator = the proposing team, no `add_player_id`, `action_id` NULL — the trade is its own record); system post with no author; both managers told. (5) **The week note:** lineups change from the first UNFINISHED week — a trade that waited for Monday night leaves the finished week's starts alone (Q75: "can be started by their current teams"; clearing them would erase those points on the next re-score); 116's carry drops a player no longer rostered, so nothing stale carries. The same defect in add/drop is F437. (6) **E47** = `trg_trade_rescind_on_stint_close` (AFTER UPDATE OF ended_at on `team_managers`, ENABLE ALWAYS): every in-flight trade of that team, either side, ⇒ `invalid` ("called off"), both told — the reading: a trade the departed manager offered or agreed does not bind the next one. (7) **The sweep** (TD12) invalidates a retired party, an unaffordable FAAB leg, a league out of season; roster fit is NOT swept (the manager can still fix it) — execution decides. (8) **F414** option (a): at acceptance the proposer's overflow names the proposer as the one to fix it; at execution the words say the team added players since agreeing. (9) **Re-cuts:** pgTAP 096 (A6's function list; E7a / E8 / F7 / G3 / G8 / G10 / I1 `accepted` → `in_review`) and `trades-db.test.ts` — L.D3.2's interim state under the default commissioner review. 148's `accepted` trades are moved into review by the migration (none exist in production).
- **D411 — L.D2.14 AS BUILT (migration 152): LINEUPS CHANGE FROM THE FIRST UNFINISHED WEEK, EVERYWHERE.** (1) **The rule is 151's, one CASE:** `v_from_week := CASE WHEN v_week_end IS NOT NULL AND v_week_end <= p_at THEN v_current + 1 ELSE v_current END`, `v_week_end` = the current week's `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at`; NULL (not recorded) is "not over" (115's reading — pgTAP 100 F2 pins the arm). All four roster writers now carry it (100 A3 greps it). (2) **Why the current week is not enough:** `lineup_current_week_internal` flips at the next week's `starts_at` (Wednesday), the game-day lock releases at `last_game_ends_at` (Monday night); in between a played starter is droppable and the worker re-scores the finished week from its own `slot_map` (step 5) until its correction window closes. (3) **Adds follow the same rule:** a player gained after the week's end joins his new team from the next week — on its stored row's bench if one exists, else through 116's auto-carry (bench = roster − starters − IR); he is never on two teams' lineups for one week *(except via the commissioner's lineup editor until F441 lands — R1212)* (100 C10 / E9). (4) **The commissioner:** `p_first_week` of 127's sync helper = `v_from_week`, `p_current` stays `v_current` — so a Tuesday move vacates no current-week slot, queues no re-score of the finished week and sets `edited_by_commish` only on the rows it changed (100 C3–C6). A commissioner's move of a played starter in a week STILL IN PROGRESS is unchanged (D346's arm) — F440. (5) **Re-cut:** pgTAP 061 F2 (two cells) had pinned the defect as a Q32 application ("once the week has cleared … his slot is CLEARED in both rows"); Q32's verbatim ruling is about the LOCK and says nothing about a finished week, and the "nothing to keep" premise of that application is false once the week's last game has ended (he played). Re-cut to the week-4-only clear; annotated at Q32. (6) **Not done here:** no backfill (a finished-week slot map the old code emptied is not recoverable from the schema); the worker's step-3 map still cannot reach a correction on a player no league team rosters (F263(a) — reconcile catches it); the transactions `week` / acquisition-cap week stay the current week. Fix: the season command routes every LOCAL request through `scripts/sim-keepalive-fetch.ts` (one `node:http` keep-alive agent; fetch semantics kept — body, headers, HEAD / 204 no body, abort, `TypeError('fetch failed')`); external calls still go through the real fetch and are counted. 11,261 → 974 sockets per 100-league run. Unit pin `sim-keepalive-fetch.test.ts` (a server with `maxRequestsPerSocket = 100`: 1,000 requests ≤ 12 connections; probe keep-alive off ⇒ 1,000, red). The same churn hits every other Node client on the global fetch — **F479**. - **D426 — L.D3.12 AS BUILT (migration 162 / pgTAP 110): THE TRADE SCREEN NEVER LETS A MANAGER BUILD AN OFFER THE LEAGUE WOULD REFUSE (Chris 2026-09-29, in chat: "you can't propose trades past the trade deadline. if you make a trade for 2 players, where you give up one, and your roster is full then you have to select a player to drop in the case that the trade is accepted or if you're accepting you pick the player to drop. as far as i'm concerned there is no such thing as trade that isn't legal so...").** **(1) ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH — no TS twin.** Two member-only SECURITY DEFINER reads over the verbs' own internals: `trade_deadline(league)` (151's `trade_deadline_internal` + `passed` = the verbs' own `deadline_at <= p_at`, judged at the database's now() — the clock `trade_propose` / `trade_respond` refuse by; F452) and `trade_preview(league, trade?, from?, to?, items?, drops?)` (F462): the OFFER arm checks what propose / a counter checks (the offering team's drops enforced, the receiving team's side reported); the ACCEPT arm the stored legs + the proposer's stored drops + the receiving team's drops as given, both enforced. STABLE, write nothing (110 E1 / E2 row counts), one no-leak 42501 for no league / deleted / non-member, REVOKEd from anon. Rejected: a TS roster-size twin with a parity test (two implementations of E36; the deadline instant cannot be computed client-side at all). **(2) THE ONE SUBSTITUTION.** `trade_check_internal` replaced against 151:214-424 (md5 7ba00e04): under the verb `trade_preview` the E36 overflow is REPORTED (`must_drop`, in the facts it already returned) instead of raised, so the preview can give both sides' counts at once; `IS DISTINCT FROM` so a NULL verb never skips it. 110 A3: the body with the substitution taken out is 151's byte for byte; F1–F3: every other verb still raises and only the preview uses the reporting mode. **(3) BOUND TO THE VERBS.** 110 C3 / C4 and D3 / D10: the preview's `must_drop` K is exactly what the verbs demand (K − 1 drops refused by E36, K taken); B2 / B3: `passed` flips at exactly the instant `trade_propose` refuses. **(4) HOW EACH RULE IS PREVENTED.** *Deadline* — once the server says passed there is no Propose (trade center), no Trade on another roster's player row, no Propose trade on a team page, no Counter; an offer still waiting says "The trade deadline passed on <date> — this offer can't be accepted or countered now" (Turn down stays); before it the line names the instant ("Trade deadline: <date>, when Week N+1 begins"); the read re-reads itself 1 s after the deadline from its own `ms_remaining` (a timer, no client clock). *Roster size* — the builder's Send is enabled only on the preview's `ok`; when the offering team would be over, the drop picker opens with "pick N more"; the receiving team's overflow is said ("they'll pick N to drop when they accept"); on a received offer the picker is on the card before anything is pressed and Accept works once the preview says ok; F414 (the proposer added players since) → Accept off with "ask them to call it off and send a new one". *FAAB* — a box above the rosters read's balance is refused on the spot (the preview is not asked); the preview rechecks; FAAB boxes only where the league trades FAAB (unchanged). *Locked players* — Q75 as spec'd (amended by R1283): the lock is judged when the trade GOES THROUGH (151's executor), never at offer time, so a started player is always pickable (legs and drops) and wears 🔒; once picked his row says what will happen (`defer`: the trade waits for the week's last game; `reject`: it can't go through until the week's games are over). The one exact check: under `reject` with review `none` (accepting runs the trade at once) an offer naming a started player can't be accepted until the week's games end (`acceptGate`). The task text said "locked players can't be picked"; that would forbid trades Q75 allows and the server takes, so it is not built — relayed as F490. *A player no longer on the team* — not in the roster list; picks re-filtered. **(5) BACKSTOP.** Every verb refusal still renders through `plainRefusal` (R1244); a deadline refusal still locks the builder. **(6) DEPLOY BEFORE PUSH.** Until 162 is pushed the routes answer a named 503 on PostgREST's PGRST202 anchored on the door's NAME (measured: "Could not find the function public.trade_deadline(p_league_id) in the schema cache") → `unavailable` → D419's behaviour exactly (the week-only line, every door shown, send-and-see, Accept with drops…). Player FK ON DELETE CASCADE, as `player_stats` (the line it annotates — and every fixture that deletes its synthetic players keeps working). SELECT `auth.role() = 'authenticated'` (the `player_stats` shape); no write policy. (2) **The door** — `ingest_write_batch(p_rows, p_now)`: `p_rows` = one element per line of ONE (season, week): `{stat, enqueue, corrections}`, `stat` = `ingestWeek`'s upsert payload minus `updated_at`; every element the same key set, each key a real `player_stats` column (checked against `pg_attribute`, `%I`-quoted — never interpolated raw; pgTAP 115 C34 sends `bogus; drop table players`), `id` / `updated_at` refused; a transaction-scoped advisory lock per (season, week) so two concurrent polls of a week serialize; the events FIRST — OLD read from the stored line (FOR UPDATE), NEW from the line being written, a named key that did not move counted (`events_unchanged`), a repeat at the same instant absorbed by the natural key (`events_replayed`); then the lines — ONE dynamic `INSERT … SELECT FROM jsonb_populate_recordset … ON CONFLICT (player_id, season, week) DO UPDATE SET <exactly the sent columns>`, i.e. PostgREST's own upsert semantics, so the door and the pre-167 path write byte-identical lines; then the enqueue — `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET enqueued_at, deferred_until = NULL` (D321(2), 122; the lease pair untouched, 121). Every count asserted in-body and again in TS. SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path = ''`, a JWT-bearing or anon caller refused in-body (42501), REVOKEd from PUBLIC / anon / authenticated. **No existing body replaced** (D137 not engaged; 115 A8 pins 158's scoring door md5 unchanged — it still refuses a final week). (3) **The classification (TD2 — TS stays the one diff)** — `classifyCorrections(diff, existingStats, existingGames, …)` over inserts + updates: the line's own game (`game_id` on the incoming or stored line) must have been `final` in the `nfl_games` read BEFORE this poll's writes (a game not yet stored was not final); with no game id the WEEK stands in — every in-week game final before this poll (postponed-out games excluded, E43). Then one key per moved registry key under the diff's own equality (absent ≡ 0 except a NULL_IS_PENDING column; an absent advanced key is pending). **Why the stored state:** the poll that first sees a game final carries its last in-game changes, and those are not corrections — the break probe (classify against `merged`) reds exactly those cells (ingest-week.test.ts C2 / W3). The door cannot classify (the poll writes `nfl_games` before it calls the door). **Production consequence (F468(a) — every production line has `game_id` NULL):** detection is at WEEK grain there — a fix to a Sunday line that lands before the week's last game ends is re-scored as today (the week is live) but not recorded as an event → **F507**. (4) **`week_state`** (the door, at `p_now`): `final` iff the NFL week's window has closed AND every game still in the week is final by `finalize_matchups`' own test (`week_games_state_internal(…).all_final`, 116 — a game postponed WITHIN the week holds it open, one postponed past the next week's start has left it; a week with no stored games is open) AND no in-season / playoff league still has the week open; else `open`. `final` ⇒ no league can re-score it — "recorded only" everywhere; `open` ⇒ at least one league still may. Which league a correction actually changed is L.E2.2's per-league record (D438) — the event carries the id it will point at. (5) **Deploy before push (D447)** — PostgREST's answer for the door on a 166 database, MEASURED on the local stack 2026-09-29 before 167 was applied: `PGRST202`, `Could not find the function public.ingest_write_batch(p_now, p_rows) in the schema cache`, `hint: null` (stored literal in ingest-week.test.ts F1). On exactly that answer — D426's `isDoorNotPushed` (a hint offering the door under another signature is drift and THROWS; measured on 167: `…ingest_write_batch(p_rows)…`, hint `Perhaps you meant to call the function public.ingest_write_batch(p_now, p_rows)`) — the poll writes through TODAY's two-call path, unchanged (queue then stats, R706), `report.write.path = 'two_call_fallback'`, a reason line, and the live poll pushes a `problems` line every poll (the route console.warns it) until the push; the detected keys are counted, none recorded. Asked on the FIRST batch only — a later batch meeting "no such function" throws. Any other door error throws. Pre-167, `ingest-week-db.test.ts`'s 14 cells were run against the 166 stack with this code: 11 green, 3 red on exact `reasons` pins (the diff shown: R707's list meeting the added fallback line; on 167 all 14 are green). The stack cells for the fallback ask the door under a name no database defines (`IngestIo.door`, a test seam; production passes nothing) and get PostgREST's real PGRST202 (stat-corrections-db SC7, the R706 cell). (6) **TD5** — `FINAL_WEEK_REPOLL_DAYS = 7`, `FINAL_WEEK_REPOLL_UTC_HOUR = 11` (07:00 ET, before the 11:15Z reconcile): at that hour's sweep the plan adds `finalWeeksForRepoll` — weeks before the current one whose `correction_window_ends_at` is ≤ now and > now − 7 days — i.e. now < window end + 7 days (inclusive at the lock, exclusive at day 8; D146 pairs pinned), after the current week and F270's open-window weeks, never doubling one. **2026-09-29 — L.E1.28 (docs only): the M6 breakdown's design decisions TD1–TD16, transcribed as D433–D448** (`tasks-M6-commissioner-console.md` §3, approved by Chris 2026-09-29, PR #360). Short form; the breakdown has the full text. **Where Chris's rulings changed a TD, the ruled form is what is transcribed** (marked). D432 is left to L.E2.1 (building in parallel — the D388 precedent).
- **D433 — TD1.** Two lanes, ONE schema lane: L.E2 (ingestion, scoring records) and L.E1 (receipts) both write migrations and serialize in merge order; TS/UI tasks fan out in separate worktrees; one local database — `db reset` / `test:db` one at a time.
- **D434 — TD2.** A correction is a change to a **scoring** stat of a line for a game already `final` at the previous write, or a first line for such a game (a late-filled gap — F269(a)). A `metaOnly` rewrite is never one (F268). One event per (season, week, player, stat key) change with old / new value and the week's state at detection (`open` / `final`). Events are NFL data: SELECT `authenticated`, no write policy.
- **D435 — TD3.** Events land in the same transaction as the stat line (F267): a service-role `ingest_write_batch(p_rows, p_now)` door (DEFINER, `search_path = ''`, in-body role check, REVOKEd) writes stat rows + events + the `score_fanout` enqueue; `ingestWeek` computes the diff and calls it. Until the door is pushed (PGRST202) `ingestWeek` keeps today's two-call path and says so — the production poll never stops scoring.
- **D436 — TD4.** Finality governs, not the clock (**Q82 / Q47 — ruled**): an open week (live, in its window, or held past it by an unplayed game) re-scores through the ordinary worker; a `final` week is never re-scored — the event is recorded, `player_stats` moves, 158's lock holds.
- **D437 — TD5.** Re-poll reach: open weeks unchanged (F270); each **final** week is re-polled once a day for 7 days after it locks (a named constant) so a late correction is recorded and research stays right. Nothing it finds changes a score.
- **D438 — TD6 (as ruled by Q81).** `league_stat_corrections` — one row per (league, week, team, player, event batch): player points and team score before → after, result before → after — written by the door **in the same transaction as the re-score** of an open week, only for teams that **started** the player, and none for a correction that moves no points. **Q81 struck the rest:** no "would-be" numbers are computed for a final week and nothing a member can see lists a post-lock correction — so the breakdown's `week_final` rows (which carried only those numbers) and `stat_correction_record_final_week` are not built. For a final week the stat event itself (and `player_stats`) is the whole record; if a later task needs anything more recorded for a final week, that is a new question for Chris (F510 lists the breakdown sentences this touches). SELECT league members; no write policy.
- **D439 — TD7.** Announce once per league per re-score: one league-chat system post naming each correction and each changed team score; an in-app notification only to a manager whose matchup **result** changed (§16.4). A score-only change is in the post and the view. A post-lock correction posts nothing (nothing changed — Q81).
- **D440 — TD8.** F245's apply half is the door's: an in-window re-score writes `result` with the score in one statement (no `result_drift`); a post-lock change goes only through `commish_edit_score` (126). F476: a re-score of the last regular-season week or a playoff round runs the bracket sync at once.
- **D441 — TD9.** Every commissioner write gets a receipt: the tasks-M6 §2.3 functions gain D336's receipt on their commissioner arm — one row per change, none per no-op, none for a mock; a receipt never carries an invite token, an invitee's email, a blind bid or a queue (the log is member-readable).
- **D442 — TD10.** The backstop is proven three ways: (i) a pgTAP catalog census over `pg_proc` (every commissioner-gated league writer reaches the helper or sits on a named allowlist with its reason); (ii) a behavioural matrix (change ⇒ one row, no-op ⇒ none); (iii) the D343-shape `ENABLE ALWAYS` guards on every `*_action_id` column, each column's writers measured first. **Q83:** the matrix has no report / resolve verbs to include.
- **D443 — TD11 (Q87 — a design choice).** The console is a launchpad, not a second copy of the tools: every control stays where M6A / M5 put it; the console shows what needs the commissioner now, one door per tool group (landing with override mode on), and recent actions. No new shared component.
- **D444 — TD12.** One activity renderer, no code words: League Home, the Activity page and the console's recent list render through `activity-feed-ops.ts`; a census test fails if any §12.12 `action_type` or setting key has no plain-words copy — the `replace(/_/g, ' ')` fallback retires. Trade lines per **Q84**.
- **D445 — TD13 — VOID (Q83 dropped the illegal-lineup flow).** Its content survives only as the fact the spec now states (§10.2): the remedies are the existing verbs — `commish_edit_lineup`, `commish_edit_score`, `commish_set_result` — each with its own receipt, the score / result ones bound by Q61 / Q67. No report state, no `resolve_lineup_report`.
- **D446 — TD14.** Prevent, don't refuse (Chris 2026-09-29): no console, correction or log control is offered that the server would refuse; when an action isn't possible yet, the reason is shown in words. Server checks stay as the backstop.
- **D447 — TD15.** Deploy before push: merged code reaches fieldscout.gg at once, the database only at Chris's push; every M6 read and write degrades on a database without its migration (GET, never HEAD — R1257; PGRST202 / PGRST205 / 42P01 named) and each PR says how.
- **D448 — TD16.** Act-as-Manager is already delivered by override mode (standing rule (h)) plus the commissioner arm on every manager verb (M5 TD5); M6 proves it (L.E1.31's manager-verb census) rather than building a second mechanism; the log renders `acting_as_team_id` as "for <team>".
- **D449 — L.E1.29 AS BUILT (migration 168 / pgTAP 116): THE DRAFT-ROOM CONTROLS WRITE THEIR RECEIPTS — no product rule changed; the build mechanics of D441 (TD9) for F40's draft half and F45.** (1) **One seam, not sixteen copies.** `draft_commish_receipt_internal(league, is_mock, verb, action_type, target_type, target_id, reason, before, after, metadata, acting_as)` — PLAIN, `search_path = ''`, REVOKEd from PUBLIC / anon / authenticated (123:417's posture): a mock or a league-less (standalone) draft ⇒ NULL, `before IS NOT DISTINCT FROM after` ⇒ NULL (D336 part 3 — the no-op DETECTED by value, the verbs pass every dimension they change), else exactly one `log_commissioner_action_internal` row with `metadata.verb` + `bypassed: []` + the verb's keys and `IF v_id IS NULL THEN RAISE` (D336 part 2). (2) **Sixteen bodies, receipt hunks only (D137).** Newest definers measured by grep + md5 over 001–167, file text = live prosrc on the 167 chain: `draft_pause` / `draft_resume` 095; `draft_set_clock` 101; `draft_undo`, `draft_reassign_pick`, `draft_move_player`, `draft_force_pick`, `draft_set_order`, `draft_reverse_won_bid`, `draft_adjust_budget`, `draft_cancel_nomination`, `draft_end` 100; `draft_reset` 150; `draft_start_internal` 110 (its `CREATE FUNCTION` header becomes `CREATE OR REPLACE` — same signature); `draft_create_internal` 066; `set_team_autodraft` 072. Hunks 1–4 each, all additive except `draft_pause`'s `RETURN draft_pause_internal(…)` → `v_result := …; <receipt>; RETURN v_result`. Derived by script (every substitution asserted once, the reversal asserted byte-identical); pgTAP 116 A3 / A4 pin both md5 sets through `pg_temp.un168`. No older suite pins these bodies by md5 (grep), so no older cell was re-pinned; the prosrc containment pins (036:416, 049:44, 058:163) hold. `draft_pause_internal` (the tick's outage pause too) is untouched. (3) **Whose call is a commissioner call.** `draft_start_internal` / `draft_create_internal` receipt only when `p_require_commish` (the tick and draft_start's create-if-absent pass FALSE — a system act has no actor, §10.3 / D338; a commissioner start writes ONE row); `set_team_autodraft` only on the commissioner path (`NOT v_is_self` — his own seat is not an override). `acting_as_team_id` = the team acted for: `draft_force_pick` (both arms — the team on the clock, §8.7 "on behalf of") and `set_team_autodraft` (the toggled team); NULL on the other fourteen, which act on the draft (the team also rides in `metadata`: `for_team_id`, `affected_team_ids`). It is an FK with no ON DELETE on an immutable log, so a suite that tears such a league down takes the F406 order (detach teams → delete league → delete teams) — five stack suites now do (R1320). (4) **What each receipt carries** — the pick {pick_number, team, player, price}; the clocks {the four timers}; the order {draft_order, nomination_order, on_clock}; the budget {budget_adjustment} (remaining / open / max in metadata); undo {last_live_pick, on_clock, picks[]}; status for pause / resume / end / reset / start; start's `after.placeholder_team_ids` = non-retired teams with no `league_members` row carrying a user (D339 — a placeholder row AND a seat with no row; F45). Nothing blind or private: every value is already in the room's chat post (D441). Vocabulary: 13 new action types + target `draft` (spec §12.12, v2.16.79). (5) **Receipts change no behaviour.** Results, refusals, messages and chat posts byte-identical (a same-value clock still posts, and writes no receipt — pgTAP 116 D17); the reason is normalised (blank ⇒ NULL, Q66); a reason over 500 characters is the ONE new refusal — 22023 by name with 131's sentence, raised in the seam after the write so it rolls the change back (R1321; only a direct RPC caller can meet it — the routes bound the reason at 500). No signature changes: `draft_start` / `draft_create` take no reason and store NULL. (6) **Proof.** pgTAP 116 `plan(121)`: per verb change ⇒ one row with its before / after as stored literals, no-op ⇒ none (early returns, replays, and the by-value cases: same clock, same order, a no-change pick edit, same auction clock, same nomination order), mock ⇒ none (a league mock the commissioner launched: pause / clock / order / resume + a still-shut refusal; a standalone pause), manager ⇒ 42501 on all sixteen doors with nothing written, the tick's create / start ⇒ none, members read the rows, the owner cannot edit one; held lock (min of three, on the fresh 001–168 chain) force pick 0.61 ms / undo 0.52 ms (< 50 ms, §8.3). Every pgTAP suite is green UNMODIFIED (none pinned "no audit row"). Stack suites touched, each NAMED: `auction-commish-api-db.test.ts`'s F40 cell pinned "`draft_adjust_budget` writes nothing to the audit table" and said so ("the day that verb starts logging, this cell reds") — inverted to exactly ONE receipt with the reason and before / after, the replay / unstamped / refused calls none; `members-api-db.test.ts`, `draft-queue-api-db.test.ts`, `draft-commish-db.test.ts`, `draft-commish-api-db.test.ts` and `auction-commish-api-db.test.ts` teardowns take the F406 order (detach the teams → delete the league → delete the teams), because the autodraft and force-pick receipts reference a team. `npm run test` run TWICE on one database, both 306 / 5,345, proving the teardowns leave nothing behind. Beside it, `…<snapshot>.lines.json` (`correction-line-meta.ts`): each recorded line's player name, position, the team he played for that week, opponent, game date and Sleeper's `last_modified`, read from the SAME public endpoint the adapter polls — because the §23.1 line carries no team or game (F468(a)), a canonical recording alone cannot name a changed line's game. No stat value is read from the sidecar; the fixture's lines come only through the provider (D24). Public NFL data only. (2) **The diff** — `correction-snapshot-diff.ts` (pure) + `npm run diff:fixtures -- --season <y> --week <n> [--write]`: every change to a line whose game was final at snapshot 1, under **the ingest's own equality** (`toStatRow` + `movedStatKeys` imported from `ingest-week.ts` — absent ≡ 0 except a NULL_IS_PENDING column; registry keys only; never a second definition), each named — player, key + label, scorable / context, old → new, game (the line's id → the player's team in the week's schedule → else the whole week, D432(3)'s rule), updated vs a line first seen late. Listed APART, never merged: changes on a game not final at snapshot 1 (in-game), lines the provider dropped (the ingest keeps a stored line), and production events no change accounts for. THROWS (never an empty diff): a snapshot without a successful week-stats read, a pair of different weeks / providers, a snapshot 2 not later, a player with two lines. A week with none prints *"FINAL-GAME CHANGES: none … Nothing to capture this week (never fabricated)"*. (3) **F528's measurement** — per change, the minutes from the game's first observation as final to the change, as honest BOUNDS: the change happened after snapshot 1 read the old value and no later than snapshot 2 (or Sleeper's stamp of the line, when that falls between the two); the first-seen-final instant is production's `nfl_games.updated_at` (the settle grace's own clock, D453(6)) from the export file, else only the recorder's own bound (a lower bound on the minutes, the upper unknown). Verdict against `SETTLE_GRACE_MS`: inside / outside / undetermined. Plus a per-snapshot **settle profile** (each line's Sleeper stamp − its game's first-seen-final, bucketed; `--profile-only` prints it for the "final" snapshot before its pair exists — week 3's: 385 lines, 30 last stamped at most 6 h after their game's first-seen-final, 355 later — the hourly restamps). **Measured limit of the stamp:** Sleeper restamps lines hourly (at :08) for non-stat fields — 53 of week 3's rows were restamped after production's last write while NO canonical value moved (below) — so a stamp only bounds a line's last stat change from above; the profile is weak evidence and the pair's diff is the measurement. (4) **The production route** — `correction-events-export.ts` + `npm run export:correction-events -- --season <y> --week <n> --confirm-target <host> [--write [--overwrite]]`: `--confirm-target` is required even to READ (the house `confirmTarget`); the export reaches the database only through `readOnly(db)` = `from(table).select` and nothing else (no insert / update / upsert / delete / rpc reachable — frozen objects; a test proves the surface, a full run's call log, and a source pin over both files). It reads the week's events (+ the season count, so zero is an answer with its reason), games, bounds, stored lines and the event players' names; names each event with its minutes after first-seen-final (the game's instant, else the week's latest — `finalObservedAt`'s arms) and the grace verdict; a pre-167 database (PGRST205 on the table) is named, any other error throws. `--write` writes `production-events.json` beside the snapshots — public facts only (no event id, no host, no key). Not built: a fixture PAIR derived from production events (→ F541). (5) **Measured 2026-09-30 13:37–13:44Z (production, read only):** `stat_correction_events` holds **0 rows for the 2026 season**. Week 3: 16 / 16 games final, the last first seen final **2026-09-29 03:18:00Z**; all 390 stored lines last written at that instant, **0 after** (34 h); and Sleeper's current 385 week-3 lines are **identical** to production's stored lines under the ingest's equality (385 / 385; 5 stored lines are absent from Sleeper's current set — the ingest never deletes) — so the week-3 "final" snapshot taken **13:40:10Z** holds exactly the week's lines at its last final game: measured, not assumed. They were not recordable (pre-167; `player_stats` keeps only the last write — no old values), so they are evidence of timing, not a capture. - **D471 — F558 / F559: THE M5 TRANSACTING STAGE'S FLAKES WERE ONE HARNESS RACE (PR #387, 2026-10-02).** Both failure modes are the same mechanism: every league job (`lineup_lock_tick`, `league_week_advance`, `finalize_matchups`, `waiver_tick`, `trade_tick`) selects its leagues `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, and the local stack's pg_cron runs `lineup_lock_tick()` / `league_week_advance()` unscoped every minute at wall time — for a 2099 league it finds nothing due but still locks every in-season league row while it looks. The sim's scoped call at a virtual instant then visits 0 leagues and returns a well-formed empty report, which the harness read as "ran, nothing to do" (the season-runner banner called the cron "inert" — inert, but not invisible). (A) F558: the orphan week's arm-(c) pass skipped ⇒ no `autopiloted[]` entry ⇒ `ghost-takeover`. (B) F559: the run-instant `waiver_tick` had no retry ⇒ `no_league_due`. **Classification (i)** — the expectation is already Q63's (the sim switches autopilot ON as the commissioner; nothing auto-enables it; no product code changed); in production the next minute's cron catches up, which is what SKIP LOCKED is for. **Fix:** `runScopedJob` (`src/lib/leagues/sim/scoped-job.ts` + `scoped-job.test.ts`, 5 cases) re-runs the same call at the same instant until the job's own `leagues` count says it visited the league, asks the job's selection (read back) only when it did not, and fails loud after 60 × 250 ms; all five scoped jobs use it; `jobs.skippedOnLock` is printed on the JOBS line. **Evidence:** natural run a4 logged 4 × `lineup_lock_tick@2099-09-22T07:01Z leagues=0` (stayed green — a non-critical instant); a lock-holder (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on every in-season league, 1.5 s per 2.5 s) on the old harness: RED, 41 failures = 9 × `ghost-takeover` (F558's text) + 32 × `unmanaged-seat-autopilot`; harder lock (4 s per 4.2 s) on the old transact code: 5 × `TRANSACT ABORTED — waiver_tick … never tracked the league` (B's seed-tick sibling). Fixed harness under the 1.5 s lock: GREEN, 97 calls re-run. **Probe:** the retry disabled under the same lock ⇒ RED (17 × `scores_written` — skipped advances), restored. **10 × `sim season --leagues 24 --weeks 2 --seed 42 --transact`, unstressed: 10 / 10 GREEN, 0 invariant failures each; lock skips caught and re-run: 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0.**
- **D472 — F560: THE `auction-storm.spec.ts:399` RED WAS A PRODUCT DEFECT IN THE DRAFT ROOM, NOT A HARNESS FLAKE (PR #387, 2026-10-02).** **Evidence (the gate's own trace + the stack, read before the sweep):** `realtime.messages` shows the award's `drafts` broadcast (manager on the clock, `updated_at …19.982053`) and its `draft_picks` INSERT committed at 18:23:19.982 — the award HAPPENED and WAS broadcast; realtime logged no `too_many_requests` in the window (so not F311), and the pg_cron jobs ran 3–18 ms each (so not D471's lock contention — `draft_tick` returned and awarded). The manager's trace: its refused mid-storm bid (400 at 64553) settled ⇒ `useAuctionMutation.onSettled` invalidated the room query ⇒ the refetch's SELECT read the HELD lot (stored response: `updated_at …19.871235`, deadline 18:25:19.91, high bid $25) **7 ms before the award committed**; the award broadcast was patched onto the cache; the refetch then RESOLVED and React Query REPLACED the cache with the pre-award snapshot. The snapshots show it: the clock read 0:00 at the award and **1:58 two seconds later — the hold's deadline, back**. Only the next 5 s heartbeat's deadline-gap check could heal it; the spec waits 2 s. `ECONNRESET` was the dev server logging aborted requests at context close — unrelated. **Classification (ii), product:** the room-state query (`draftKeys.detail`) was the one cache on the `draft:<id>` channel still written straight through `setQueryData` — the exact fetch window R401 closed for the bid feed and F75 for chat. In production it is reachable whenever a manager's bid (or any room action) settles within ~a round trip of an award: the room un-renders the sale for up to one heartbeat. No product call needed — §9.3 already requires broadcasts as monotonic hints over fetched state. **Fix:** `createStateSink` (the R401 sink, generalised over the cached value; `createFeedSink` is now that with rows) + `createRoomStateSink` / `applyRoomBroadcast` in `src/hooks/use-draft-feed-sink.ts`; `use-draft.ts` routes `drafts` / `draft_picks` through it (held while the room fetch is in flight, replayed onto the result; the reducer's `incoming < known` rule makes a replay the snapshot holds a no-op), disposed with the channel. No migration, no server change. Tests: `src/hooks/use-draft-room-sink.test.ts` (9 — mechanism control, the gate's instants as stored literals, version rule, the no-cache paths, wiring pins). **Reproduced by construction** (browser route holding the manager's `drafts` GET response 800 ms across the award, a bid click as the natural trigger): on the pre-fix tree the manager's room was NOT on the clock 300 ms after the stale response (assertion RED); with the fix, on the clock. **Probe (§4.3):** `applyRoomBroadcast` reverted to the pre-fix straight-onto-cache shape ⇒ 3 of 9 RED (the window pin, the first-fetch pin, the common-path pin); restored ⇒ 9/9. **The 2 s window stays** — it is exit criterion 3's < 2 s convergence and is now met with margin. **Counts:** `auction-storm.spec.ts --repeat-each 25`: 25/25 (22–42 ms); full `npm run test:e2e` × 3: 23/23 each (19 / 29 / 36 ms); unfixed tree isolated × 25 before the fix: 25/25 (the race needs a refetch in flight at the award — load-dependent, seen 1 in ~4 gate browser runs). **(2) Review R1452 [SHOULD-FIX] / R1453 [NIT] (2026-10-02).** R1452: replaying a held `draft_picks` event onto the fetched snapshot could add a ghost — INSERT(#5 P live) then UPDATE(#5 P undone) held, snapshot already `#5 P undone` ⇒ the INSERT appended a live row (undone-ness differs) and the UPDATE matched two rows. Pick events carry no version and no id (D109(2)), so the sink cannot know if the snapshot post-dates them. **Fix:** `createStateSink` takes `replayable`; the room sink replays ONLY `drafts` events (versioned, `incoming < known`). A pick event arriving while the room fetch is in flight is dropped and the room refetched ONCE after that fetch settles (none if nothing was dropped; none extra if the drained `drafts` replay's own gap refetch already started — that fetch post-dates the drop). Outside a fetch, picks apply at once as before. Not taken: "same (pick_number, player_id) already present ⇒ applied" in `reducePickInsert` — it drops a genuine re-pick of P at #5 after its undo. Cells: 9 → 13 (the reviewer's probe; no-refetch-loop; re-pick after undo; undo just after the resolve); the F560 window cell now asserts the pick is NOT replayed and one refetch is asked for. **Probe:** `replayable: () => true` ⇒ 2 of 13 RED (the probe cell, the window cell); restored ⇒ 13/13. R1453: the stale L.E1.37 "GATE RE-RUN PENDING" clause in §2 struck as superseded. **Counts:** `vitest src/hooks src/components/draft` 1160/1160; `test:unit` 5146/5146 (257 files); type-check clean; lint clean; `auction-storm --repeat-each 10` 12/12 (10 + 2 setup); full `test:e2e` 23/23. M6 gate not re-run (client cache path only; the browser specs exercise it).
